News.title: Supermarket handbags are urgently recalled in UK over ‘serious chemical risk’ that can ‘damage reproductive systems’
News.content:
A MAJOR supermarket has pulled three of its handbags after they were found to pose a serious chemical risk.

Shoppers have been urged to return the bags to their nearest store to receive a full refund.

Three ladies handbags sold in Asda have been pulled from shop shelves after they were found to contain excessive concentrations of chemicals.



The Front Pocket XBody Bag, the Opp Tote Bag, and the Black Nylon Phone Bag all contain unsafe levels of Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP).



Phthalates, commonly used to make plastics softer and more flexible, can pose a health risk to children.

The chemical can also cause possible damage to the reproductive system if it is found in excess quantities.

Asda has therefore issued an urgent recall as the bags do not reach the safety requirements of REACH Regulations 2008.

Sold as part of the supermarket’s fashion range, the black bags retailed between £8 and £16 – with the Phone Bag at £8, the XBody Bag at £10, and the Tote Bag at £16.

The Office for Product Safety and Standards has recommended that consumers stop using the product immediately.

Shoppers who have bought the affected bags have been urged to bring them back to the nearest store where they will receive a full refund.

Full list of Asda Ladies Handbags that have been recalled Front Pocket XBody Bag (Product Code: 1199257937001, Price: £10, Barcode: 5059206286959)

Opp Tote Bag (Product Code: 1100260834001, Price: £16, Barcode: 5059206491797)

Black Nylon Phone Bag (Product Code: 1100258939001, Price: £8, Barcode: 505920628577)

The supermarket has further confirmed that no receipt is required to get any money back, and to contact customer relations for further information.



A spokesperson for Asda said on the product recall: “We are very sorry for any inconvenience caused.”

News.title: Westwood Elementary School on lockdown & building evacuated over ‘emergency’ after shooting reports
News.content:
AN emergency situation has been unfolding at an elementary school in Waynesboro, Virginia.

The children at the Westwood Elementary School were confirmed to be safe on Wednesday morning after a massive police response was seen at the school.



There was a report of an active shooting at the school, but no further details were available, WTVR reported.

The Waynesboro Police Department said it was “managing an emergency” at the school, added a reunification center would be set up at the nearby Westminister Pressbyterian Church.



“The children are safe and are being evacuated from the School. Please wait for notification and instruction from Waynesboro Public Schools,” The Augusta County Sheriff’s Office said, according to WHSV.

“Please DO NOT respond to the school we need access for the buses and emergency vehicles.”

The sheriff’s office said at 10:23am that the incident was “contained and secured.”

Teachers and staff have also been evacuated.

Other schools in the area, including Stuarts Draft and the Wilson Complex, were placed under lockdown as a precaution.

Ambulances and dozens of cop cars could be seen at the scene.



The FBI also arrived on scene and officers could be seen putting on vests and armed with rifles, according WHSV.

The emergency situation happened just weeks after students returned for a new school year on August 12.

News.title: Age of the dinosaurs tops children’s ultimate time-travel wish list, research reveals
News.content:
THE age of the dinosaurs tops kids’ ultimate time-travel wish list, with the long-extinct creatures still ruling their imaginations, research has revealed.

A poll of 1,000 parents with children aged three to 12 found 34 per cent would choose to go back to the prehistoric age, with the biggest appeal being the chance to come face-to-face with a real dinosaur (43 per cent).



The next desired time-travel destination was the future world (20 per cent), while seven per cent wanted to go to ancient Egypt and scout out the pyramids.

It emerged 78 per cent of kids are interested in dinosaurs, which last roamed Earth millions of years ago, with 20 per cent of mums and dads also naming them as their child’s number one fascination in general.



Gaming came second (18 per cent), followed by superheroes (14 per cent), and arts and crafts (14 per cent).

The research was commissioned by Park Plaza London Riverbank [https://www.parkplazariverbank.com/dino], which is searching for the UK’s biggest “T-Rexpert” for a chance to win a family stay in its new Natural History Museum Dinosaur Suite, which opened for booking on September 1st.



Maxine Lister, head of licensing at the Natural History Museum, said: “We are delighted to see dinosaurs continue to captivate children and spark their curiosity in the natural world.

“Together with Park Plaza London Riverbank, we have created a new way for families to immerse themselves in a wonderful prehistoric adventure together, from the comfort of their own hotel room.”



There were no surprises as the Tyrannosaurus rex was voted the dinosaur children would most like to see in real life (42 per cent), followed by Triceratops (11 per cent) and Velociraptor (nine per cent).

The biggest fascinations about them include their size (50 per cent), their appearance (46 per cent) and the fact they lived so long ago (41 per cent).

Interestingly, just 22 per cent of parents think they know more about dinosaurs than their little ones, with half of children (50 per cent) having corrected them at one point on a fact about them.

But mums and dads are seemingly delighted with their passions – as 81 per cent agreed learning about the prehistoric animals has sparked their kids’ interest in science and history, according to OnePoll figures.

Overall, 84 per cent believe it’s important for family days or holidays to have an educational element attached to them, and 79 per cent believe their child would be excited about the potential of staying in a dinosaur-themed hotel suite.



Families can win a stay in the suite, which includes a hidden bookcase opening into a world inspired by dinos, featuring many goodies and experiences, by submitting a short video to @ParkPlaza on Instagram showing why their child is the ultimate dinosaur fan by September 21st.

Suat Binkaya, senior general manager at the hotel, added: “Collaborating with the Museum means we have built real storytelling and discovery into the experience that every family will have.

“From a dinosaur-inspired bunk bed and prehistoric murals to interactive games, discovery activities and hidden specimens waiting to be uncovered, every corner of the suite has been built to spark curiosity and bring the ancient world to life.

“Every part has been meticulously designed to be immersive, educational and highly memorable, while still delivering on the comfort and quality guests expect.”

News.title: Sick parents ‘kept four children locked up in “rolling dungeon” for six years where they were sexually abused & starved’
News.content:
'ABUSE' HELL Sick parents ‘kept four children locked up in “rolling dungeon” for six years where they were sexually abused & starved’

A DEPRAVED couple allegedly sexually abused their four children in a “rolling dungeon” for six years.

Tamra Marshon Stewart, 37, and Keysha Monique Epps, 51, are accused of confining two girls and two boys in their semi-truck.



The alleged abuse – that continued over six years – was laid bare during a press conference held by Attorney General James Uthmeier.

He said: “These children were trapped in a rolling prison and abused by the adults who were supposed to protect them.”



“The evidence makes clear, the girls were sexually abused by Stewart,” Uthmeier added.

“The boys watched it, when they would confront Stewart or report it to Epps, they would be physically abused themselves and injured.



“They were malnourished, they were not frequently fed, they were not cleaned, they were not given showers.”

According to the investigation, the crimes took place from January 2020 through April 2026.

The sickos were the primary caregivers of the four children who lived with them in the sleeper cab of Epps’ truck as she ran routes from Atlanta to Miami.

The youngsters were required to share a bunk, were denied food, hygiene, schooling, and medical care.



At times, when the truck would pass by a station, Stewart and Epps would use the restroom and take a shower, but the children would be left under a lock inside, Uthmeier explained.

Two suffered untreated burns that left significant scarring. One child was also diagnosed with a sexually transmitted infection.

It is alleged that Epps knew of the abuse, failed to stop it and report it.

Meanwhile, Stewart admitted to three sexual batteries against one of the girls.

Asked how the kids are doing since Stewart and Epps’ arrests, Uthmeier said: “They are safe, I think they’ve got a long road to recovery.



“They are going to need a lot of help, a lot of therapy, lot of prayer.”

He explained that investigators had received a tip which had led them to make “observations” and intervene to get the victims to safety.

Stewart is charged with two counts of sexual battery by a person in familial or custodial authority, two counts of lewd or lascivious molestation of a child under 12, two counts of battery of a child by expelling certain fluids or materials, two counts of child neglect without great bodily harm, and two counts of child neglect causing permanent disfigurement.

Epps is charged with two counts of sexual battery by a person in familial or custodial authority, two counts of lewd or lascivious molestation of a child under 12, two counts of child neglect without great bodily harm, two counts of child neglect causing permanent disfigurement, and four counts of failure to report child abuse.
