Texas Sen. Ted Cruz actually praised President Donald Trump for calling him“Lyin’ Ted” and slapping him with other derogatory nicknames during the 2016 presidential campaign, saying it was “political genius.”

Cruz, one of the many Republican candidates who lost to Trump in 2016, admitted to Fox News host Sean Hannity that the nickname was “brilliant” because it turned people against him.

“My biggest strength was people trusting me,” Cruz said Monday on the podcast “Hang Out with Hannity.” “People trusted that I believed what I said, that when I said I would do something, I would do it.”

“It was actually, it was political genius,” Cruz told Hannity.

Though Cruz and Trump get along now, during the 2016 primary, Trump hurled insults at the Texas senator, calling him “Lyin’ Ted,” tying Cruz’s father to the assassination of former president John F. Kennedy and insulting Cruz’s wife, Heidi, for her appearance.

open image in gallery Texas Senator Ted Cruz said that President Trump's 'Lyin' Ted' nickname was 'genius' and 'effective' ( Hang Out with Sean Hannity/Fox News )

At one point during the Trump–Cruz 2016 feud, the president tweeted an unflattering photo of Heidi Cruz and threatened to “spill the beans” about her.

Cruz responded by condemning Trump, saying “real men don’t attack women.” Trump later admitted tweeting the photo of Heidi Cruz was a “mistake.”

On Monday’s podcast, Hannity revealed to Cruz that he had a private conversation with Trump, seemingly referring to the president’s rude remarks about Heidi Cruz.

“I yelled at him, let’s say using very New York-style language,” Hannity told Cruz. “I’m like, ‘Will you stop attacking people’s families?’ It went harder than that, but that’s all I said.”

Mediaite was the first to report on Cruz and Hannity’s comments.

While “Lyin Ted” helped Trump defeat Cruz in the 2016 Republican primaries, Trump eventually publicly retired the nickname in 2018, telling reporters: “He’s not ‘Lyin’ Ted’ anymore. He’s ‘Beautiful Ted.’ I call him ‘Texas Ted.’”

open image in gallery Though they were once political foes during the 2016 Republican primaries, Ted Cruz (pictured left) is now one of Donald Trump’s strongest allies in the Senate ( AFP/Getty )

Since then, Cruz has been one of Trump’s strongest allies in the Senate and continues to support most of the president’s actions, voting with Republicans, on average, 86 percent of the time.

Trump is well-known to give his opponents nicknames – though they don’t always last.

Like his nickname for Cruz, Trump had also once insulted his now-Secretary of State Marco Rubio during the 2016 Republican primaries, calling him “Little Marco.”

Cruz also told Hannity he believed Trump’s nickname for Marco was “devastating.”

American Airlines is adding more premium seats to its Boeing 777-300ER long-haul fleet, reflecting a broader effort by U.S. carriers to attract higher-spending travelers.

The carrier is also eliminating its first-class cabin while expanding its business-class seating.

Seeking to boost profitability with expanded premium offerings, American said its first retrofitted aircraft will enter commercial service Wednesday from New York to Buenos Aires. Upgrades across all 20 of its 777-300ERs are slated for completion in 2027.

The redesigned layout will feature 144 premium seats—up from 116 currently—increasing the overall proportion to about 44% from 38%. The configuration includes 70 Flagship Suite business-class seats with privacy doors, 44 Premium Economy seats, and 30 Main Cabin Extra seats offering extra legroom.

open image in gallery The revamped aircraft will feature 144 premium seats, up from 116 under the current layout, including 70 Flagship Suite business-class seats with privacy doors (pictured) ( American Airlines )

The current 777-300ER layout contains 52 business-class seats and eight Flagship First seats, its top international offering. American is eliminating Flagship First during the retrofit, ending sales for travel beginning November 19.

American was the last of the big three U.S. network carriers offering a separate international first-class cabin.

Delta Air Lines combined its international first and business cabins in late 1998, while United Airlines stopped selling international first class in 2018 as it transitioned long-haul planes to Polaris business class.

open image in gallery The jets will offer 44 Premium Economy seats, redesigned with sculpted headrests, adjustable calf and foot rests and enhanced storage ( American Airlines )

American announced in 2022 that it would drop international first class because passengers were not purchasing the product, allowing space for business-class seats that passengers are willing to pay for.

The retrofits extend American's emphasis on premium travel as it attempts to narrow a profit gap with Delta and United.

Premium passengers generated nearly half of American's ticket revenue in the second quarter despite filling about 30% of seats. American revealed last month that premium seating on narrowbody flights will expand to roughly 40% in coming years from around 25% now.

open image in gallery Customers traveling in Main Cabin can access hundreds of entertainment titles with the latest inflight entertainment technology ( American Airlines )

The shift reflects a broader trend across U.S. airlines. Revenue from premium offerings is outpacing cheaper options as higher-income consumers continue spending while price-sensitive travelers cut back on travel expenditures.

Lower-fare carriers are also adapting. Southwest Airlines is evaluating features historically tied to network airlines, including airport lounges, transoceanic flights, and premium seating. Frontier is introducing first-class-style seats, and JetBlue is expanding its premium product with lounges.

American flies its 777-300ERs on key long-haul routes including London, Tokyo, Sao Paulo, Buenos Aires, and Sydney. Updated planes will offer enhanced inflight entertainment, while members of American's AAdvantage loyalty program will receive free high-speed Wi-Fi access.

Volodymyr Zelensky has issued a stark threat to airlines and businesses using Russian airspace, saying it will be “effectively closing” as Ukraine escalates its drone campaign.

"We want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, everyone who still uses key Russian airports: the Russian sky is becoming completely dangerous," the Ukrainian president said in an address late on Tuesday.

“Drone-infested skies are no place for civilian aviation ... the safe days in Russia’s skies are over,” he added.

President Vladimir Putin has responded, saying that his comments were tantamount to a "declaration of state terrorism”.

Experts say that te

open image in gallery The Ukrainian president has declared Russian airspace "effectively closed" as the country steps up its drone strikes ( AFP/Getty )

Who still uses Russian airspace?

Many international airlines continuing to operate flights to Russian airports, especially in major cities like St Petersburg and Moscow.

Kyiv has emphasised that civilian aircraft will not be targeted, but his comments may spark alarm among commercial airlines that continue to operate in the region.

Airlines including Emirates, Air China, Turkish Airlines, Flydubai, Qatar and Etihad Airways are among those that have maintained lucrative routes connecting Russia to Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America over the course of the conflict.

open image in gallery A number of airlines have continued to use routes that go through Russian airspace ( Getty/iStock )

The war has already proved dangerous for civilian aircraft. In 2024, Putin admitted that Russian forces had shot down an Azerbaijan Airlines plane that crashed in Kazakhstan, killing 38 people. He blamed the incident on Russian defence systems attempting to intercept a Ukrainian drone.

Ukraine has closed its airspace to civilian aircraft since the beginning of the war.

Why is Zelensky making the threat?

Katia Glod, the deputy head of foreign policy at the New Eurasia Strategies Centre (NEST), says there are two main reasons why Zelensky is making the threat.

“Of course, Zelensky is partially exaggerating — this closure is not in any way similar to the way Ukraine’s airspace has been closed,” she says.

open image in gallery The aftermath of a Russian strike on Kyiv this week ( AP )

“As Ukraine’s drone strikes are escalating, Zelensky probably felt it was a good ‘PR moment’ — a signal to tell everyone making use of Russian airspace that they are going to lose if they continue to do so.”

But she adds that there is also a more strategic element behind the Ukrainian leader’s logic: “It’s part of a wider aim to target the Russian economy, and hit the war machine.”

If Moscow becomes difficult to reach for aircraft, there will be “significant” financial consequences, she says.

How could the threat influence the future of the war?

Analysts say Ukraine’s drone campaign is already having a significant impact on the course of the conflict.

“It is altering the cost-benefit of continuing the war,” Ms Glod explains. “So far, Putin has been able to shield Russians from the impact — but over the past months, Ukraine’s strikes are really bringing the war home.”

open image in gallery Ukraine’s latest move may encourage Putin toward ending the war, say foreign policy experts ( AFP/Getty )

Because of this, Zelensky’s threat will influence Putin’s thinking, Ms Glod says.

“While he is stubborn, and doesn’t really take advice from the government, he is quite conscious of the people around him. And if this harms their interests, the oligarchs that surround Putin may eventually influence him to begin negotiating an end to the war.”

How would the closure of Russian airspace affect Europe?

Zelensky’s threat also holds consequences for broader Europe.

Together, Nato member states have provided Ukraine with an estimated $120 billion to $130 billion in assistance since 2022.

Over the summer, Ukraine has dramatically increased its domestic defence capacity, striking deeper into Russian territory in hopes of bringing an end to the war.

But while Kyiv’s threat is hoped to force Putin into negotiations, Ms Glod says a move to target airspace could cause anxiety across the region as Russia ramps up threats against Europe.

“While Nato really welcomes Zelensky’s ability to impose costs on Russia, these costs are also a source of worry.”

US president Donald Trump has insisted he “couldn’t care less” if Iran signs a “worthless” deal to end the war, as both sides launched fresh strikes in the spiralling conflict.

The war saw a dramatic re-escalation as Washington and Tehran traded attacks in the biggest exchange of fire in weeks on Tuesday, with US forces attacking Iran’s southern coast and Iran attacking American bases across the region.

Tehran accused Washington of hitting a wedding in Sirik, killing four people and wounding dozens, before vowing to drive the US from its military installations in the Middle East. The exchange pushed oil up to $97 per barrel - its highest rate since July.

“I’m not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table,” Trump wrote on Truth Social overnight, responding to speculation around his motives after the US resumed attacks this week. “I couldn’t care less if they sign a worthless, to them, agreement.”

“I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing,” the president added. “They are just playing out the inevitable.”

open image in gallery An F/A-18 Super Hornet prepares for takeoff on 29 August ( US Navy )

Trump called for the Iranian people to “rise up and fight” as Iran and its Arab neighbours were plunged back into war with another barrage of airstrikes on Tuesday.

The US military claimed strikes along Iran’s southern coast while Iran took aim at American bases in Jordan, Bahrain and Iraq after threatening more devastating attacks.

“Last night was like the end of the world,” Mahmoud, 38, a municipal worker in Sirik County along the strait, told Reuters on Wednesday, describing attacks on the area where Iran said US forces had struck a wedding party.

Iranian media said that as many as 68 people were wounded at the wedding event and released images of children injured in a hospital. The Independent was unable to verify the incident.

open image in gallery Iran accused Washington of striking a wedding party, killing five people and wounding dozens ( Iranian Red Crescent Society )

Iran responded by striking what it said were American assets in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Iraq, and said its objective was now to oust US forces from its vast array of bases occupied across the region for decades.

“American evil in the region will be met with heavier, more widespread, and devastating responses, and any country that cooperates with the aggressive American army must accept its dangerous consequences,” Iran's military command said.

US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for Central Command, said they were aware of reports of an attack on a wedding, noting that they originated from Iranian state media.

“The US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” he said, referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he did not care about Iran coming to the table to negotiate peace as Iran vowed to oust the US from its bases in the Middle East ( AP )

Central Command also confirmed that American forces had successfully completed a wave of strikes against Iranian military targets on Tuesday.

“U.S. forces struck Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites,” a statement read, adding that they followed IRGC attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members.

Tuesday’s wave of strikes followed an American attack on Iran’s Larak Island overnight into Monday.

Washington said it had struck Iranian launchers firing mines into the Strait of Hormuz in the first exchange of direct attacks in a month, before Iran claimed strikes on two US air bases in Jordan.

open image in gallery An injured victim lies in a hospital bed following an attack at a wedding near Sirik ( Reuters )

The dramatic re-escalation of the conflict, now in its seventh month, pushed oil prices back up to levels unseen since July as hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict faded.

Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian insisted that the Islamic Republic was ready to sit down for serious talks aimed at ending the war, though the regime is determined to emerge from the conflict stronger with new control over the Strait of Hormuz, billions in blocked funds released and sanctions lifted.

Trump agreed to many of Tehran’s demands in a June deal, but the ceasefire agreement collapsed within weeks over control of the Strait, and no public talks have been held since.

Frank Warren says that Anthony Joshua is yet to sign the contract for an all-British blockbuster fight with Tyson Fury as the wait goes on for an official announcement.

Fury suggested on Tuesday that confirmation of the hotly-anticipated showdown was close, posting a mocked-up image of himself facing off with Joshua above the words “New York City” on Instagram.

The expectation is that the bout will be hosted at the world-famous Madison Square Garden, as is the desire of Turki Alalshikh and Saudi state-owned promotional company Sela, though Joshua’s camp prefer Wembley Stadium as the venue, which would allow for the element of a home crowd.

Warren, however, says that location is no longer a factor for Fury who has penned a contract that does not hinge on where the fight takes place, with the Queensberry chief insisting that “The Gypsy King” is now just waiting on Joshua’s signature.

Anthony Joshua has not yet signed the contract to fight Tyson Fury ( PA Wire )

“The latest is Joshua's not signed yet,” Warren said.

“It's not for me to give him [a deadline], it's the people who are paying the money. It's all this stuff, as I said from the beginning, it's about contracts. I know what the contracts say. The contracts have all got to be amended.

“Tyson's signed. Tyson's done. He don't care when the fight takes place. [If] they want it in New York, they want it in Barbados, they want it on the Isle of Wight, he's signed. He's done.”

Warren also added that Fury signed up for the “AJ” fight as early as the beginning of this year, with plans originally being for the pair to fight in this month.

However, Joshua’s involvement in car crash that took the lives of two of his close friends last December forced the date of fight night to be rearranged.

“He signed for the fight in January,” Warren continued. “The fight was supposed to take place in September, but what happened with AJ and his accident, that all got pushed back.

“Where we got to with it was obviously AJ had his fight back and we'd already had that one in December with Jake Paul.

News.title: We installed a heat pump – here’s what I learned
News.content:
Swapping a gas boiler for a heat pump can feel like a big leap. Will the house stay warm in winter? Will there be enough hot water for a busy family? And will running the system actually cost less?

Those were some of the questions facing Paul and his family when they replaced the gas boiler in their four-bedroom Liverpool home with an Octopus Cosy 9 heat pump. Since making the switch, they’ve experienced everything from the installation itself to living with steadier heating, managing hot water and making use of cheaper electricity at different times of day.

So, what is it really like to live with a heat pump? Here’s what they learned after making the move away from gas.

When ambition meets reality

For many homeowners like Paul, the upfront cost is perceived as a barrier. But extensive Government support and grants is making that decision far easier ( Octopus Energy )

Before making the switch, Paul did his homework. He had no doubts about the system’s ability to heat their home, seeing the fears often voiced about heat pumps as similar to “range anxiety” with electric vehicles – something he had experience with and had long learned was largely unfounded. “I had zero anxiety at all about whether or not we’d be able to warm our house effectively. I guess that’s the heating equivalent of ‘range anxiety’. But both my wife and I have driven EVs for years, so we know that fears about them are a myth. I knew concerns about heat pumps not working in winter or in older houses are a myth too.”

Don’t listen to the naysayers or the people who have zero actual experience of heat pumps when they trot out the tired old disproved myths

The biggest barrier for many homeowners, including Paul, is the upfront cost. Government support, however, made the decision far easier. “I knew getting a heat pump would unlock far cheaper energy bills going forward, so it was worth doing everything I could to get one. Obviously, the £7,500 government grant was invaluable, and getting it was easy. Octopus did all that for me on my behalf.

Four days, minimal disruption and a warmer home

Paul considered a Daikin system but ultimately chose Octopus’ own Cosy 9 heat pump. The decision was guided by integration and future-proofing: the Cosy’s controls sit within the same app as their electricity account, aligning perfectly with other smart systems in the home, such as EV charging and solar battery storage. “I feel that is where the future innovation and clever automations are more likely to be – in the same way that Octopus can intelligently charge my car when energy is cheapest and greenest, I’m hoping that will become an option one day,” Paul explains.

Installation took just four days and caused minimal disruption. The results have exceeded expectations. “Our house has been lovely and warm all the time,” Paul says. “Don’t get me wrong, our previous gas boiler was capable of heating the house, but reservations about carbon emissions and the extremely high cost of gas central heating in recent years put us off having it on much in previous years.”

Heating your house using cheap off-peak electricity is a huge benefit which just doesn’t exist with gas

Noise has not been an issue. “99 per cent of the time you’re completely unaware of any noise. The heat pump’s gentle whirring happens outside, and when it’s cold, you’re generally inside. During the warm summer months when you’re outside your house in the garden, it’s generally off apart from when it’s doing the hot water cycle – even then, you have to go and stand right next to it if you want to hear it. It’s so quiet.”

See if an Octopus heat pump could save you money. GO TO WEBSITE 

See if an Octopus heat pump could save you money. GO TO WEBSITE 

Comfort is now a priority rather than a compromise. There’s plenty of hot water for morning showers and the kids’ baths at night, and the family keeps the thermostat at 23–24C, a significant step up from last year’s 17C. “This year is the first time since the energy crisis that we’ve been toasty and warm inside, without having to worry about huge bills. Heating your house using cheap off-peak electricity is a huge benefit which just doesn’t exist with gas,” Paul says.

Sign up to our Independent Home newsletter: your one-stop shop for home improvement inspiration, expert tips and exclusive offers.

Why we wouldn’t go back

With no gas standing charge, no risk of carbon monoxide or anxiety over fluctuating gas prices, Paul’s confident he made the right move ( Ryan Jenkinson for Octopus Energy )

Ten months on, Paul says there are many things he no longer misses: the gas standing charge, the risk of carbon monoxide, and the anxiety over fluctuating gas prices. He has become a passionate advocate for heat pumps, stressing that the technology works effectively even in homes that are far from “perfect” in terms of insulation or installation conditions.



“Just like with electric cars, don’t listen to the naysayers and the people who have zero actual experience of heat pumps when they trot out the tired old disproved myths about them being too noisy, not working, or costing a fortune. Take it from someone who has one and lives in a house with far from ideal and perfect installation conditions – they work brilliantly.”

For the family, the switch has not only brought tangible financial and environmental benefits but also a sense of reassurance and control over their home energy use. It’s a glimpse into what a greener, smarter and more cost-effective future for home heating could look like.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

Sports.title: Joey Barton could face six more months in jail as trial for ‘beating man at golf club’ is delayed until next year
Sports.content:
CLUB 'ATTACK' Joey Barton could face six more months in jail as trial for ‘beating man at golf club’ is delayed until next year

JOEY Barton could face six more months in jail after his trial for allegedly attacking a man at a golf club was delayed.

The ex-footballer was charged following the alleged attack close to the Huyton and Prescot Golf Club, Merseyside, on March 8.



He was due to face trial this week at Liverpool Crown Court but Judge David Potter adjourned the case to March 8, 2027.

Barton has been remanded into custody – meaning he faces a six month wait in prison until the trial if he is not granted bail before then.



The former City star appeared in court today for the hearing, on his 44th birthday, wearing a navy blue suit and tie with a blue shirt.

He made a thumbs up gesture to a man in the public gallery as he left the dock.



Barton has pleaded not guilty to assault occasioning grievous bodily harm.

The court previously heard Kevin Lynch, 51, had been drinking with Barton at the £1,440-a-year golf club on March 8 before the horror.

Kevin – a former non-league football manager – was rushed to hospital with injuries to his face and ribs.

He was left in a serious but stable condition but there is a possibility he may lose sight in one eye.



Barton started his football career with Manchester City in 2002 after going through their youth system and went on to make 150 appearances for the club.

He then moved to Newcastle United in a £5.8million transfer in July 2007 before leaving for Queens Park Rangers in August 2011.

The midfielder was then put on loan to French side Marseille during the 2012-13 season before making his way to Burnley for one season – helping promote them to the Premier League.



He moved to Rangers on a two-year deal but that was ripped up after just eight games following bust-ups with team-mate Andy Halliday and manager Mark Warburton.

He was also investigated by the Scottish FA for breaching gambling rules.

Barton made one appearance for England in 2007 – despite criticising some of his fellow players.

The footballer later attempted a management career with stints at Fleetwood Town and Bristol Rovers.

Sports.title: ‘Next Kvaratskhelia’ spotted at airport as he travels for Arsenal medical after Gunners beat Liverpool to transfer
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are set to win the race for Georgian wonderkid Andria Bartishvili.

The winger, 17, was photographed on Wednesday morning at an airport in Georgia as he prepared to travel for a medical in London.

Bartishvili is currently on loan at Iberia 1999 from fellow Georgian side Kolkheti 1913 and cannot move to the Gunners until he turns 18 next March.



The teenager has been tipped for the top and was scouted by several top clubs this year, including Juventus and Liverpool.



He has been compared to Paris Saint-Germain forward Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and signing him is viewed as a coup for Arsenal.

The Premier League champions’ pursuit of Bartishvili is thought to have been driven by Maurizio Micheli, the assistant to sporting director Andrea Berta.

Micheli is regarded as one of the game’s top scouts and is credited with being the man that spotted Kvaratskhelia.



Bartishvili hinted over the weekend that he was joining Arsenal via his social media account.

The Gunners have made a point of signing young talent over the past 18 months as part of an academy recruitment drive.

The club has targeted young British players this summer – such as Welsh midfielder Axel Donczew and striker Igor Tyjon.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But they have not been afraid to look overseas, too, for players with great potential.



Ecuadorian twins Edwin and Holger Quintero are a prime example of that and will be joining next year when they turn 18.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Sabah tickets: Where can I buy them and how much do they cost for huge Champions League clash
Sports.content:
CHAMPIONS LEAGUE football returns to Old Trafford next week as Manchester United take on Sabah.

The Red Devils have not been in Europe’s elite competition since the 2023/24 season, when they were knocked out in the group stage.



Michael Carrick was the man who guided the club back to the Champions League after he led a stunning resurgence following Ruben Amorim‘s departure.

United face tricky tests against European giants Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Roma during the league phase, but they have a favourable opener on their return.



Carrick’s side face little-known Azerbaijan champions Sabah, who were founded under a decade ago.

Tickets are still available for the highly-anticipated Champions League fixture at Old Trafford.



Where can I buy Man Utd vs Sabah tickets and how much do they cost?

Man Utd vs Sabah is scheduled to take place on Thursday, September 10, with kick-off set for 8pm BST.

Tickets for the match are still available to buy on secondary ticket site Ticombo.

At the time of writing, seats in the upper tier start at £86, while tickets in the lower tier are for sale from £120.

Prices will likely increase as kick-off nears.



How to watch Man Utd vs Sabah

If you can’t make it to Manchester, fans in the UK can watch the match live on TNT Sports.

The broadcaster holds the rights to the majority of Champions League fixtures for the 2026/27 season.

For those looking to stream the action, the match will be available to watch via the HBO Max app/website.

Alternatively, SunSport’s live blog will bring you minute-by-minute coverage of the Champions League tie.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer asks ‘what fool said that?’ as Premier League prediction comes back to bite him
Sports.content:
ALAN SHEARER has been left red-faced after his bold prediction about Sunderland came back to bite him.

The Newcastle legend previously claimed he wanted the Black Cats to be promoted in 2024-25 because it would mean his beloved Magpies get “six points guaranteed”.



But Regis Le Bris’ side famously did the double over Newcastle the following season and then finished above them in the Prem.

Sunderland came seventh and qualified for the the Europa League for the first time, while Newcastle came a disappointing 12th.



Shearer was reminded of his prediction after Betfair unveiled their ‘Wall of Shame’ on Wembley Way.

The installation saw some of the worst takes in football immortalised on the famous road leading up to Wembley Stadium.

Shearer responded: “What fool said that? Let’s hope I was just 12 months early in my prediction.

“It will be a more challenging season for Sunderland this year than it was last year.

“I do think it will be tougher times for Newcastle as well and we’ll have to be patient. So, let’s wait and see.

“We all think we know what’s going to happen. But even the best of us can completely miss the mark.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Betfair’s Sam Rosbottom added: “Football is a game of opinions, some sensible and accurate, some spectacularly, unforgivably wrong.

“Fans, pundits, managers, players… we all have our say. Most of our views on the beautiful game don’t turn out to be quite accurate.

“We’ve only had one round of the new Premier League season, but already we’ve seen fans’ hope, dreams and aspirations for their teams shattered in 90 minutes.

“Man United are back… only to lose against newly promoted Hull City, Spurs are going for it this season… only to be humbled 3-0 by London rivals Brentford. Life comes at you fast in football.”

Newcastle have a new look team this season after losing manager Eddie Howe, plus top stars like Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes.



But the Magpies have had a good start under new boss Matthias Jaissle after drawing with Liverpool 2-2 and beating Tottenham 2-0.

Sunderland, meanwhile, were beaten 2-1 by newly-promoted Ipswich and then won 1-0 against Fulham.

Sports.title: Non-league footballer rushed to hospital with heart condition as his club release health update after fan concern
Sports.content:
FOOTY WORRY Non-league footballer rushed to hospital with heart condition as his club release health update after fan concern

A N0N-LEAGUE star has been forced onto the sidelines after suffering from a heart condition.

Darlington defender Scott Barrow was substituted during a 4-2 defeat to Harborough Town last month.



And the former Swansea City youngster, 37, was rushed to hospital to undergo checks.

National League North side Darlington have now released an update on Barrow’s health after fans pleaded for positive news.



The Quakers have revealed the left-back’s condition is set to be reviewed by a cardiologist.

A club statement read: “The club realises that there has been some concern about the condition of defender Scott Barrow, who left the field near the end of the away game at Harborough on August 22.

“We can inform everybody, with Scott’s permission, that he is suffering from a heart condition which needs further analysis from a cardiologist in the coming weeks.

“He spent several days in hospital following an ECG after the Harborough away game, and is now resting at home.

“Everyone at the club would like to wish Scott a speedy recovery and that he is in our thoughts.”

Barrow came through the ranks at boyhood club Swansea before being released without making a first-team appearance.



The Welshman has gone on to feature for the likes of Tamworth, Macclesfield, Newport County, Gateshead and York City.

Barrow then played a key role in Darlington staving off relegation from the National League North when he joined on loan in 2024.

And the move became permanent after his contract with York expired at the end of the season.

But, in a huge blow for Darlington, Barrow is set for a spell out of action as he continues his recovery.



The Quakers are preparing to face King’s Lynn Town in a National League North clash on Saturday.

Darlington are only one point clear of the drop zone after winning two of their six clashes so far this term.

Sports.title: Former England star Conor Coady coaching at old club days after Wrexham contract ripped up
Sports.content:
CONOR COADY is coaching with Liverpool’s Under-21 side after leaving Wrexham.

The defender, 33, agreed to rip up his contract with the Championship club on Monday despite having a year left on it.



Coady is a product of Liverpool’s academy and has returned to help out with the coaching there as he assess his options.

He told the BBC: “I’m trying to keep myself busy. I’m lucky enough to get the opportunity to go into Liverpool’s U21s.



“I came through there. I’m doing a little bit of coaching with the boys, which has been brilliant.

“If they need numbers, I’ll jump in and keep myself fit as well.



“That’s what it’s looking like at the minute. I’m obviously speaking to my agent about different bits that are going on.

“I’m not massively in a rush because I want to make sure it’s right.”

Coady made two first team appearances after coming through Liverpool’s academy.

He went on to play for Huddersfield, Wolves, Leicester and the Reds’ big rivals Everton.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The centre-back also earned 10 England caps between 2020 and 2022, earning a spot in Gareth Southgate‘s Euro 2020 squad.

Last summer he joined Wrexham in a deal thought to be worth around £2million.

Coady started their first five matches of last season but then failed to make a single further appearance.

He was subsequently loaned to Charlton in January, playing 12 times for the Addicks.

Sports.title: Mo Salah’s Trabzonspor make shock U-turn and ACCEPT manager’s resignation less than a week after blocking it
Sports.content:
MOHAMED SALAH’s new club Trabzonspor have accepted the “emotional” resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after the Turkish side initially rejected his request to step down.

It was only at the beginning of August that Salah made the move to Turkey.



But already they have been knocked down to the Europa Conference League for the new season after a 5-0 Europa League play‑off round aggregate drubbing by Hungarian club Ferencvaros.

Tekke, who led Trabzonspor to a third‑place finish in the Super Lig last season, tendered his resignation after the loss.



However, the club initially rejected it, believing he made the decision under the “intense emotional impact” of the Europa League exit.

However, 48 hours on, the Turkish giants have now agreed to part ways with their head coach.

In a statement released on Wednesday, Trabzonspor said it reached a “mutual understanding” with Tekke and decided to part ways “in line with Trabzonspor’s interests and long‑term objectives”.

The club, which is based in the north-east of Turkey in Trabzon, has put together a real mismatch of stars ahead of the new season, undoubtedly led by Liverpool legend Salah.

Another ex-Red, Fabinho, is in the midfield while Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana remains on-loan in goal.

The club captain is former Manchester City centre-back Stefan Savic and they also signed World Cup fairytale man Sidny Lopes Cabral, whose wondergoal against Argentina took the eventual finalist to extra-time with Cape Verde this summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It hasn’t been a great start for the club in the league this term with one win, one draw and one loss from their opening encounters.

However, Salah is holding up his end of the bargain with three goals in as many games.

Despite the rocky past couple of months, Trabzonspor paid tribute to their outgoing manager in a statement.

It read: “Over his approximately 18‑month tenure, Fatih Tekke brought significant value to Trabzonspor.



“Beyond contributing to the development of the players added to our squad during this period, he delivered important sporting and financial gains for our club.

“By bringing the Turkish Cup back to our museum, he once again wrote his name into Trabzonspor’s history.

“At this point, we reached a mutual understanding with our coach – who stated he would never allow his presence to harm Trabzonspor in any way – that drawing a new roadmap, prioritising the club’s interests above all else, had become unavoidable.

“We thank our coach for his efforts, his dedicated work, the successes he delivered, and the value he added to Trabzonspor.”

After a deadline day full of drama, the summer transfer window has finally slammed shut. Premier League clubs have concluded their incoming business and will hope they've done enough for the new football season.

‌



A whopping combined £3.4bn was spent by Premier League clubs this summer in a new record total outlay. And while some leagues outside England remain open for business, the majority of European sides are done making deals until January.

‌



There could still be some outgoings to places like Saudi Arabia or the Eredivisie in the Netherlands, but one thing's for certain. Premier League clubs won't be improving their squad until after Christmas.

‌

As a result, the squad make-up on EA Sports FC 27 has shifted slightly. After revealing the ratings of every player in the game last month, we now know that some of those stars have moved to other clubs.

The leading example of this is Liverpool's staggering £123m signing, Bradley Barcola. The French forward earned an overall rating of 85 and joins Ryan Gravenberch and Hugo Ekitike as Anfield's men on that figure.

Another high-rated player who's changed clubs is Enzo Fernandez, who was also the summer's most expensive transfer. His £125m move to Man City means the Blues have two 86-rated players in him and Rayan Cherki, while Chelsea have only one with Moises Caicedo remaining.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez completed his move to Manchester City at long last on deadline day (Image: Manchester City FC)

City have also however lost their second-best rated player in Rodri, who moved to Barcelona. While the Premier League's top-rated star, Erling Haaland (91 overall), remains at the Etihad, the league's only 90-rated player is no longer plying his trade in England.

There are some significant drops in ratings for some clubs who sold a number of their best-rated players, unfortunately. Aston Villa are arguably the biggest casualties of a summer spending spree in the Premier League.

‌



Villa lost three of their highest-rated players this summer. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez (85 rated, to Chelsea), Ezri Konsa (84 rated, to Arsenal) and Morgan Rogers (84 rated, to Chelsea) have all moved on.

Some moves earlier in the summer guaranteed a new top star for plenty of other Premier League clubs. Sandro Tonali's £100m transfer from Newcastle to Spurs is the biggest of these, as the Italian midfielder is Tottenham's top-rated man at 85 overall.

Another example of a club that improved upon their best rated player is Brighton, who signed Luka Vuskovic and is their joint-top best player in the game alongside Kaoru Mitoma and Bart Verbruggen (all 81 overall). Harry Wilson (81 OVR) is the highest rated Leeds United player after his move from Fulham.

Unsurprisingly, two of the newly-promoted sides have all improved upon their previously highest-rated stars. Hull and Ipswich have both brought in a whole new top three, with Konstantino Tzolakis (79 OVR) and Exequiel Palacios (83 OVR) spearheading those sides respectively.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso and Lamine Camara phone call as Monaco chief risks Chelsea wrath with statement
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso and Lamine Camara phone call as Monaco chief risks Chelsea wrath with statement

Chelsea missed out on AS Monaco's Lamine Camara late on deadline day and now face fierce competition for his signature next year.

View Image Lamine Camara saw a move to Chelsea collapse

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso spoke directly to Lamine Camara after the transfer collapsed on deadline day, while Monaco's sporting director has since told the midfielder he will have 'even better options soon.' The Blues found themselves seeking for a new midfielder once it became clear that Enzo Fernandez was heading to Manchester City.

‌



After seeing two bids rejected by Monaco, Chelsea finally made a breakthrough and were closing in on a £47.1million deal for Camara - before the plug was pulled at the eleventh hour. Camara was in the middle of his medical at a private clinic when he was abruptly told the move had been scrapped, after Folarin Balogun's transfer to Everton collapsed for a second time.

‌



Problems were first raised during the striker's medical, prompting talks to be paused before later being revived. But in the end, Balogun decided against joining Everton, leaving Monaco's plans in tatters.

‌



Chelsea were left furious by the collapse, with Alonso now short in midfield, even if Fernandez had been sidelined for much of the early season amid uncertainty over his future.

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro admitted Camara had asked to leave, but said he has since spoken to the midfielder and reassured him that a major move will come 'very soon' - adding that he could have 'even better options than he did yesterday,' a pointed remark towards Chelsea.

Liverpool also made contact with the Ligue 1 side and may be tempted to sign him in the future, potentially next summer. Roma midfielder Manu Kone was another target high on Chelsea's wishlist, but the Blues failed to land the Frenchman, who impressed at the World Cup.

‌



Chelsea were close to an agreement for Kone, yet Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini was determined to keep hold of him, according to Sky in Italy.

Camara has now rejoined Monaco training and is back working alongside his team‑mates. Reports in France say he looked fully focused in training and even received a 'warm embrace' from his team‑mates during the warm‑up, as Monaco stepped up preparations for their clash with Paris Saint‑Germain.

The Monaco chief also outlined how both deals collapsed, setting out the extraordinary chain of events in detail. "At this moment at 4pm, Balo was in Liverpool making his medicals. Everything was going pretty well. At around 7pm we were contacted by Everton raising questions on the medicals of Balo, which for our medical staff, which for the personal medical staff of the player, there was totally no sense.

‌



"The explanations were not enough to justify or to bring concerns of the future of the player. This discussion started between medical departments from here and there. It took forever, about two to three hours, to go deep on the assessment check with other doctors. This is a normal situation when the doctor of the club raises concerns. It's quite normal that clubs will look for other specialists sharing the images and discuss the case.

"Meanwhile, as everything on the last day, this was in the press quite quickly. I would say around half an hour after we were contacted, it was already in the media that Balo is failing on the medical. Then Chelsea saw the opportunity. Okay, Monaco needs money. Balo is struggling there. Let's go. Let's try. And this is the game. It's fair to play this game. There is no problem. Chelsea came and said 'here, I can be here for the solution'. And on this moment, we had to open the door for the discussion.

"We started to open negotiations with Chelsea for Lamine. I informed the player directly myself. I called him. I informed his agent as we always do. Very open. We had discussions between the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balo. And what happened was that around 10pm in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that okay, there's no problem. We are ready to do let's sign the contract.

‌



Scuro continued: "Chelsea was always testing and trying. 'What about Lamine? What about Lamine?' I've been talking to them from the last 10 days. As soon as we got the information, yes, we did came back to Chelsea and told 'okay, we have our deal there'. There is no deal on Lamine because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game.

"There's no reason that this kind of discussions or dynamic on the last day of the transfer window which all of us decided to be on the last day trying to find solutions with the clock ticking in our neck that now this kind of interaction becomes the bad guys in the room that Monaco is not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in football industry just Monaco is not too much. So this is the storytelling."

‌



‌

Sports.title: Three Man Utd transfers can still happen as fresh interest appears from abroad
Sports.content:
Three Man Utd transfers can still happen as fresh interest appears from abroad

Although deadline day has passed in England, Manchester United could still do some shrewd business in the transfer market

View 4 Images Michael Carrick could consider selling three more Manchester United players (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee, Manuel Ugarte and Harry Amass could still depart Manchester United this month - despite the transfer window slamming shut in the UK.

‌



United didn't make any moves on deadline day, doing their business at the start of the summer. Andrey Santos arrived first for £48million, before Youri Tielemans followed for a £35m fee.

‌



Karl Darlow then joined on a free transfer before Brighton finally sold Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. Michael Carrick also shrank the squad size by allowing some fringe players to depart Old Trafford.

‌



Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek both left for the Championship, joining West Brom and Middlesbrough, respectively. Rasmus Hojlund made his loan move to Napoli permanent after the Serie A side qualified for the Champions League, triggering the buy option.

Full list of Man Utd ins and outs as 7 join and 24 leave after deadline day READ MORE :

How Man Utd managed to end up without a new left-back despite late call to rivals READ MORE :

This season's loanees include Jacob Devaney, Ethan Wheatley, Elyh Harrison, Solomon Honor, Andre Onana, Jayce Fitzgerald, Dan Gore and Andre Onana. Carrick also released six players: Casemiro, Jadon Sancho, James Bailey, Sonny Aljofree, Tyrell Malacia and Malachi Sharpe.

And despite the UK transfer window closing, several leagues' deadline days are still to come. Qatar, Scotland, Austria, Belgium and Hungary have until Thursday, September 3, to make transfers.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Meanwhile, Turkey's window shuts on Friday, September 4, with Portugal and Saudi Arabia following suit on Saturday and Sunday. Other leagues still planning deals include: Croatia (September 7), Poland (September 9), Brazil (September 11), Greece (September 15), Serbia (September 18) and UAE (September 28).

Here, Mirror Football has examined three players who could still depart Old Trafford this month.

‌



Joshua Zirkzee

View 4 Images Joshua Zirkzee has been subject of plenty transfer speculation (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee joined United in 2024 for £36m but has struggled to make any meaningful impression. Across 75 appearances, the Dutch forward has found the net just nine times and could still leave this summer.

Zirkzee attracted interest from Everton and was reportedly keen on a switch to Merseyside. However, The Athletic reports that United turned down the approach, keeping the striker at Old Trafford beyond the deadline.

‌



Compare the cheapest flights to Champions League games This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more Various prices Skyscanner See the deals here Product Description Skyscanner helps football fans compare the cheapest flights across Europe so they can follow their team's Champions League campaign, while Booking.com offers deals on flights, accomodation and car rentals.

Despite this, Zirkzee's future remains uncertain, with Sporting CP in Portugal and Turkey's Fenerbahce both touted as potential destinations. Napoli and Juventus had also been linked, though the Serie A transfer window has since shut.

Zirkzee could yet link up with former United striker Romelu Lukaku in Turkey, where he leads the attack at Fenerbahce alongside 32-year-old Vedat Muriqi. Sporting are considerably well-stocked in attack, with Fotis Ioannidis, Luis Suarez and Rafael Nel all competing for places in Portugal.

‌



Harry Amass

View 4 Images Harry Amass may plan to head further north (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Harry Amass appeared destined to depart United this summer after being placed on the transfer list. The Mail reports that the defender was valued at approximately £6m, though any move was hinged on the club bringing in another left-back.

United may yet move the academy graduate on, with one Scottish club eager to address their own left-back concerns. Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney acknowledged that the club have "key positions that we still need a bit of work on," highlighting the full-back area as a priority.

‌



Maloney is keen for Celtic to recruit a left-back to push Scotland international Kieran Tierney for his place, and Amass could fit the bill perfectly. Tierney clocked up 53 appearances last season following his return to his boyhood club, but cover for the position will almost certainly be required.

Manuel Ugarte

View 4 Images Manuel Ugarte's exit looked like a certainty (Image: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

Manuel Ugarte also appeared to be another departure before a knee injury threw his exit into doubt. Having sustained ligament damage while on duty for Uruguay at the World Cup, Ugarte returned to United to begin his recovery.

Article continues below

Club officials were seeking around £30m for the midfielder, with AC Milan keen on reuniting him with former manager Ruben Amorim. Juventus were also said to be interested, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport, though that enthusiasm cooled following Ugarte's injury setback.

United could still send the 25-year-old to Galatasaray, with the Turkish club's transfer window remaining open until September 4. The I Paper reported that the Super Lig side were amongst the frontrunners for his signature, and could plan to nurse him back to fitness before integrating him into their squad.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun 'cancelled Everton transfer' as Monaco chief reveals extraordinary accusation
Sports.content:
Folarin Balogun 'cancelled Everton transfer' as Monaco chief reveals extraordinary accusation

Folarin Balogun's proposed move to Everton fell through at the 11th hour on deadline day after he turned down the chance to join David Moyes' side

View 3 Images Folarin Balogun's proposed move to Everton collapsed on deadline day (Image: Getty Images)

AS Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro has claimed that Folarin Balogun walked away from a move to Everton after he felt 'mistreated' during his medical.

‌



Balogun, 25, was set to join David Moyes' side on a long-term contract after a £40million deadline day deal was agreed. However, after issues were raised in his medical, Balogun rejected the chance to join Everton and left the club's Finch Farm training ground without signing.

‌



Now, less than 24 hours on from Balogun's decision, Monaco chief Scuro has opened up on the situation and alleged that the United States international was "not comfortable" about joining Everton.

‌



In a press conference on Wednesday morning, Ligue 1 chief Scuro said: "The allegation of Balogun is that, 'I'm not feeling well by the way the club treated me, the way the medical team brought doubts about my future or my health. I'm not comfortable to sign a long contract here'. That the way we finished the transfer window here."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

After an issue was flagged during the medical, Everton restructured the deal with Monaco to a much lower fee than the one that had been agreed, with the new terms including an appearance-related trigger for additional payments, according to the Liverpool Echo.

‌



Monaco agreed to those changes to the structure of the transfer, and all parties were happy to sign the deal sheet just before 11pm. However, an hour later, Balogun made it clear he wanted to return to his current club.

Balogun's decision has left Everton with one senior striker following the end of the summer transfer window after they allowed Beto to sign for Fiorentina on a permanent deal. Thierno Barry has started the season with four goals in three matches and, unless the Toffees sign a free agent centre forward, the 23-year-old Frenchman is the club's only No.9 up until January at least.

Everton and Chelsea found themselves in a transfer tug-of-war with Monaco throughout deadline day, with the Toffees wanting Balogun and the west Londoners eyeing up a move for midfielder Lamine Camara. The Ligue 1 side went into deadline day open to selling Balogun, but against sanctioning a deal for Camara.

‌



But Monaco were forced to open the door to a sale for Camara when concerns around Balogun were raised. Scuro argued that Everton's concerns regarding his medical made no sense but were not unique in the moment.

View 3 Images Folarin Balogun pulled out of his move to Everton (Image: John Nacion/Getty Images for Fanatics)

Scuro said: "During the day (transfer deadline day), we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton, Balogun flew to Everton to undergo a medical.

‌



"Our plan worked very well in this moment in terms of generation of revenue, players transfer. Balo going, besides the salary, an important income to help balance the season and Lamine staying.

"What happened in the afternoon, Chelsea was always testing and trying for Lamine, I was in contact for the last 10 days. Around 4pm, we got a call from Chelsea, 'Okay, we sold a player in this position, is there any possibility that Monaco would sell Lamine (Camara)'. The answer was the same. No.

"Balo was in Liverpool going through his medical, around 7pm, we had a call from Everton raising questions on the medicals of Balo, which for our medical staff, the personnel staff of the player, made totally no sense.

‌



"The explanations were not enough to justify or bring concerns for the future of the player, this discussion started for medical departments, it took Everton two to three hours to check through the assessment, this is a normal situation.

View 3 Images Chelsea wanted to sign Lamine Camara (Image: Getty Images)

"This was ongoing, meanwhile this was in the press quite quickly, it was already in the media that Balogun is failing the medical and of course, Chelsea saw the opportunity, 'Monaco needs money, Balo is strugglng there, let's go, let's try'. This is the game.

‌



"On this moment, we had to open the door for the discussion, we started conversations for Lamine, I informed the player directly, I informed his agent, we had discussions for the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. Meanwhile, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balo.

"Around 10pm, Everton realised there is no problem. As soon as we got the information, we came back to Chelsea that we have our deal there and there's no deal for Lamine. It's fair to do this, it's part of the game.

"Premier League has a mechanism where you have one extra hour to finish the paperwork, this was done five minutes before the close of the transfer window for us to finish paperwork between Balogun and Everton. I signed the contract, Everton signed the contract, at the last moment the player decided not to sign.

‌



"Now, we are still waiting for Balo to come back and to sit and discuss and to realise between us what is next. We still have other markets open, which we are having discussions in different players including Balo, let's see what can still happen until Thursday, because we still have markets that have the financial capacity to do something and this is what happened and this is where we are today. Whatever was not clear, I am open to answer."

Balogun and Camara are now expected to remain at Monaco until at least January. The duo could be both in Filipe Luis' squad for their trip to Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr's agent slams failed Liverpool transfer in furious statement
Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr's agent slams failed Liverpool transfer in furious statement

Liverpool failed in their pursuit of Ismaila Sarr and the Crystal Palace star's agent has taken aim at the reasons for the transfer not materialising

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr remains a Crystal Palace player despite Liverpool's interest

Ismaila Sarr's agent, Diomansy Kamara, has made his frustrations public after his move to Liverpool failed to materialise, claiming: "African players deserve respect."

The Crystal Palace star, who was the top scorer for the Eagles last term, was heavily linked with a move to Anfield as Andoni Iraola sought more firepower. In recent years the south Londoners have seen a host of their leading lights leave Selhurst Park.

This summer Maxence Lacroix headed to Chelsea and 12 months ago they saw Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke depart for top Premier League sides. Palace were keen to avoid another high profile exit and weren't prepared to sanction Sarr's exit, despite Liverpool's interest. The Reds had been keen on Brighton's Yankuba Minteh before their bids were rejected.

On deadline day, Chelsea also saw their hopes of signing Lamine Camara from Monaco curtailed at the eleventh hour - and Kamara has lamented those failings.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He issued an angry statement which read: "The cases of Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara must all interrogate us. We have to get out of this logic where the African player can sometimes give the feeling that he is just a commodity: you buy it, you set its price, you negotiate its future and, too often, your will seems to go to the background.

"Our African players deserve respect. The respect of their work. The respect of their career. Respecting their ambitions. The respect of their voices. A transfer shouldn't just be a matter of two clubs and numbers. Behind every contract, there's a man, a career, dreams and life choices. The fact that clubs can sometimes have the final word is a reality of professional football.

"But one question remains: what about the career and the will of the player? The player must be able to be heard and respected in the decisions that determine his future. Let's never forget what's important: behind every success, it's the players who write history first."

View 2 Images Lamine Camara is another player whose deadline day move fell through (Image: Getty Images)

Sarr hasn't played in either of Palace's games this season, both of which they have lost. His absence from their opening day defeat at Everton came despite Pierre Sage insisting the Eagles would keep their player, who had been nursing an injury issue.

During the summer transfer window Liverpool did spend £123m to secure Bradley Barcola from PSG and had been keen to add another winger, but ultimately failed to do so.

Elsewhere in the Premier League Manchester City spent £85.6m to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. That move came after he excelled with African nation Morocco at the World Cup - prompting those at the Etihad to make him the most expensive teenager in English top flight history.

Sports.title: Everton's amateurish transfer window was a SHAMBLES - it's no wonder Balogun did a runner
Sports.content:
Everton's amateurish transfer window was a SHAMBLES - it's no wonder Balogun did a runner

A late deal for Monaco forward Folarin Balogun collapsed and has left the Everton manager with only one recognised central striker in a squad that is now without Iliman Ndiaye

View 4 Images David Moyes has been left with one hand tied behind his back (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Grealish never removed Everton from one of his social media profiles, even though he had gone back to Manchester City. Grealish could not stop talking about how much he loved life at Everton.

‌



He had not featured in Manchester City’s squad for their win at Crystal Palace on Friday, August 28. No clubs were interested in making Grealish, whose Etihad contract expires at the end of this season, a permanent transfer.

‌



The return of the 30-year-old midfielder to Hill Dickinson Stadium was a formality. Yet it was a formality that did not happen until an hour or so ahead of the transfer window closing.

‌



Every deadline day deal as Premier League clubs rushed to complete last-minute transfers READ MORE :

In the grand scheme of Everton's awful window, it is only a minor point, but a significant one. Grealish should have been done and dusted long before the deadline, allowing Everton executives to completely focus on sorting out the mess that their pursuit of a striker had become.

No wonder Folarin Balogun decided to walk away from the shambles and go back to playing in front of one man and his Ferrari in Monaco. It was amateur hour.

How else can you describe a transfer window that has left David Moyes with a squad smaller than he had when it started? How else can you describe a transfer window that has left Moyes with one striker?

‌



And that striker is Thierno Barry. Don’t forget, only five clubs scored fewer than Everton’s 47 Premier League goals last season.

View 4 Images Thierno Barry has been left as Everton's only senior centre-forward (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Barry scored a bagful against Preston reserves the other night but in 41 appearances last season, he scored eight goals. And a couple of them went in off his backside. Lovely lad, great attitude, but not a bona fide Premier League line-leader.

‌



He was not even top of Everton’s Premier League scoring list last season. That honour - with the grand total of nine - went to Beto, who was then sold to Fiorentina.

He was no Harry Kane, Beto, and he was in the last year of his contract, but he was better than having no alternative to Barry. Instead, he was sold before another striker’s services were secured. Amateur hour.

Just for good measure, of course, Everton then sold their best player, Iliman Ndiaye, for £65million, to Manchester City. It is a good, lucrative move for Ndiaye but he had three years left on his Everton contract.

‌



View 4 Images Everton have sold Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City for £65million (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

The club could have said no, just as Liverpool did when City asked for Cody Gakpo. Instead, Ndiaye went with the club’s best wishes.

This is also the club that was about to make a quick buck by selling a 19-year-old local lad who had come through the academy to Nottingham Forest. They called off Harrison Armstrong’s £35million move to the City Ground after supporters threatened mutiny.

‌



Well, it will certainly be mutinous if Manchester United arrive and take advantage of Moyes’ limited options at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday. But in a distinctly unwelcome way for the manager, it has probably strengthened his own position.

After a reasonably encouraging start to the Premier League season - a home win over Crystal Palace and a draw at Bournemouth - any downturn will now be put firmly at the door of owners The Friedkin Group, chief executive Angus Kinnear and the recruitment department. And rightly so.

View 4 Images Jack Grealish will be back in an Everton shirt this season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The news that Everton were scrabbling around for striking alternatives late on deadline evening - asking Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham - was simply embarrassing. But at least they got a player who would have walked from Manchester to Merseyside to sort the loan deal out himself.

Grealish might do great things for Everton but he is no miracle worker. And neither is Moyes. Ahead of this season, Kinnear said: “Everybody is thinking about how we mount a challenge for Europe and don’t fade in the last critical matches.” Everybody, it seems, but himself and the owners.

Sports.title: Amazon's Champions League fixtures confirmed as League Phase kicks off next week
Sports.content:
Amazon's Champions League fixtures confirmed as League Phase kicks off next week

The UEFA Champions League gets underway on September 8 and Amazon has revealed which games will be streaming live on Prime Video

View 2 Images Amazon will broadcast one Champions League game per gameweek.

Amazon has confirmed its UEFA Champions League coverage schedule ahead of the first round of fixtures. The competition’s League Phase kicks off on September 8, and as usual, one match will be broadcast exclusively on Amazon’s Prime Video on the Tuesday of each gameweek.

This starts with Porto vs Man City on September 8, which will see Enzo Maresca make his European debut as Blues boss. Then after the first international break of the season, Man United will head to the Spanish capital to face Atlético Madrid on October 13.

On October 20, Liverpool will host Villarreal in Andoni Iraola’s Champions League debut, before Man United welcome Roma to Old Trafford on November 3. Finally, Arsenal will face Borussia Dortmund at home on November 24, when the Gunners begin their charge to go one step further after suffering defeat in last season’s final.



Prime Video will also broadcast one exclusive fixture on December 8, to be announced at a later date. Football fans can watch these games at no extra cost with a Prime Video subscription or 30-day free trial.

A caveat is that the free trial will automatically renew at the usual £8.99 unless cancelled, so customers should cancel before 30 days if they want to avoid paying. Alternatively, Amazon Prime’s £95 annual subscription offers a £12.88 saving compared to paying monthly and includes Prime’s entire 26/27 Champions League coverage.
