Sports.title: New Champions League kit rule could create money-spinning chance for football fans
Sports.content:
Debutants in the Champions League will wear a patch on their shirts as part of a new deal with UEFA.

Fanatics and European football's governing body have agreed to the additional kit requirement as part of a six-year extension to their current trading card partnership.

1 The new debut patch will appear on shirts for the next six years after the new deal was announced Credit: Claudio Lavenia – UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images

The 'debut' logo is to be set into the Champions League's 'starball' logo before the match.

Afterwards, the patch will then be given to Topps - Fanatics' trading card brand - who will authenticate it and place them into a one-of-a-kind collectible.

This card will also be autographed before being placed into packs for collectors to purchase.

Only players who start games and enter the fray as substitutes are eligible.

Those named but unused from the bench will not earn a debut patch and must wait until they make an appearance for the honour.

The historic move comes on the back of similar patches being rolled out in the World Cup.

It's been a Major League Baseball regular for many years with the highest public sale for a debut patch card coming in 2025.

Dick's Sporting Goods paid $1.1million for Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes' card. However, this record could soon be beaten.

NBA rookies Cooper Flagg, Dylan Harper, and Kon Knueppel will see their cards go up for sale on Fanatics Collect.

Their auctions will run from September 10 to September 24 and expected to go for huge sums.

Flagg's card has already had multi-million cash offers rejected and a $5m bid is believed to be within the realms of possibility.

The patch scheme is also run by Topps in the NFL, Bundesliga, Formula 1, MLS, UFC, and WWE.

It's also expected to be rolled out in the Women's Champions League in the future.

Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA President and Chair of the UC3 Board said: “Renewing our partnership with Fanatics for UEFA club competitions reflects the strength of our collaboration and our shared commitment to delivering best-in-class products for fans and collectors globally. Fanatics know how to make big moments feel special. We are excited for what’s next.”

Michael Rubin, Founder and CEO of Fanatics, added: “The timing of this announcement – on the eve of the Champions League season – is incredibly meaningful for us, especially as Fanatics Collectibles continues to meaningfully expand its footprint across Europe.

“Together UEFA, European Football Clubs and Fanatics will continue to bring innovative products to fans and collectors for years to come – and through new introductions like the Debut Patch, bring them even closer to the players and clubs they love and support.”

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes to make decision on Argentina future after World Cup shame and Lionel Messi retirement
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes to make decision on Argentina future after World Cup shame and Lionel Messi retirement

Leandro Paredes has admitted it will be 'difficult' for him to continue playing for Argentina following his 10-match international ban.

The 32-year-old was handed the lengthy suspension by FIFA for his role in the ugly brawl at full-time after Argentina's World Cup final defeat, which saw him throw punches and attack Spain players.



4 Leandro Paredes was one of the villains of Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain Credit: Getty

Paredes grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground, before appearing to throw a punch in wild scenes.

In August, he was found guilty of three counts of 'assault', which saw him receive a 10-match ban as well as a $90,000 fine.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also handed respective bans and fined for their part in the post-World Cup final chaos, as well as coach Roberto Ayala.



Paredes reveals Argentina uncertainty

With Paredes staring at a lengthy spell away from international football in the wake of his ban, he has now admitted he is currently weighing up his Argentina future.

His hint comes just days after footballing great Lionel Messi called time on his legendary Argentina career.



Citing his 10-match ban, Paredes then revealed Messi's retirement was another reason why he is considering whether to continue with the national team.

The ex-PSG star told Argentine media on Tuesday: "It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team.



"Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision ... It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make."

4 Leandro Paredes pushed Spain's Gavi and Eric Garcia and appeared to throw a punch in wild scenes following the World Cup final Credit: Getty

4 Lionel Messi has retired from international football, after scoring eight goals at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty



While Paredes' suspension means he is facing a long spell away from international football, his absence might not be as long as first feared if he chooses to continue.

Having been set for over a year out of action, FIFA recently approved the Argentine FA’s request to allow their bans to be served in Class A friendlies – as well as official games.

This means Argentina's players can serve their suspensions in far less time - especially Paredes, who could potentially complete the majority of his ten-game ban before the end of 2026.

Messi decision to have knock-on effect

While Paredes considers international future, he admitted Messi's absence from the national team going forward will be keenly felt.



He went on: "Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled.

"We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us."

Messi recently announced his retirement from international football, saying he had "nothing left to give', having "given it my all".

4 Messi and Paredes tasted World Cup glory together in 2022 Credit: Getty



He captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, but fell agonisingly short of a second triumph against Spain in his final game for his country.

Messi scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina to become his country's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

He also inspired his national team to Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024, and won an Olympic gold medal with his nation in 2008.

With Messi announcing the end of his 21-year international career on social media, Paredes paid tribute to him in a touching comment.



Responding to Messi's post on Monday, Paredes called the former Barcelona icon 'the greatest of all' in his tribute.

He wrote: "Thank you for absolutely everything. You are and always will be the greatest of all. We love you, captain.'

Sports.title: Tottenham star warned about Roberto De Zerbi after transfer mistake
Sports.content:
Richarlison has been told he may have been naive with his conduct as he remains at Tottenham after the transfer window shut.

The Brazilian has been linked with leaving Spurs on numerous occasions since a £60million move from Everton in 2022.



3 Richarlison started the 3-0 loss to Brentford and hasn't been used since this season Credit: Getty

Beset by injury issues at various points, he has been unable to show his best form across four seasons.

He did, however, provide 11 important Premier League goals last term with Tottenham only just surviving the threat of relegation on the final day.

Richarlison also played a vital role in their Europa League triumph over Manchester United in 2025.



This summer he finally looked set to return to Goodison Park in a deal which could have seen Iliman Ndiaye join Tottenham.

This, though, fell through with the player releasing a strong statement on social media having seen Roberto De Zerbi talk about his future after Spurs' loss to Newcastle.



He wrote: "After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me.

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.



"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!

"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.

3 Richarlison played the majority of pre-season but now finds himself out in the cold Credit: Getty



"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.

"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."



Former Tottenham defender Sebastien Bassong, though, believes Richarlison may now have made a rod for his own back with his comments.

He told the Sports Breakfast: "Roberto De Zerbi is someone that's kind of vulnerable. He talks a lot. What you see is what you get. So when he's with you, he's with you. When you come out and you say you want to leave, you better leave. So he wants committed players.

3

"I think Richarlison's been a little bit… He's been inexperienced the way he came out, because I don't think he was sure that he was going to be able to leave.



"Look at that now. I think he's going to be really far down the pecking order.

"But then, once again, that gives him a challenge to prove people wrong and to come back.

"Maybe that's what he needed. But at the moment, I don't see him being so performing. And it's not going to happen anytime soon."

Richarlison, who now has new signing Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke ahead of him in the pecking order, could still leave Tottenham.



Clubs from Turkey, Netherlands, Portugal, and Saudi Arabia all have extra time to get transfers done and potentially land players like the Brazilian forward.

Sports.title: ‘Nothing personal’ – Conor Coady explains sudden Wrexham exit after contract ripped up
Sports.content:
Conor Coady insists his Wrexham exit was amicable despite wishing he got more opportunities to prove himself at the club.

The former England international joined the Red Dragons from Leicester City last summer in a £2million deal on a two-year contract.



3 Coady's two-year contract at Wrexham included the option of a further year, which now won't be activated Credit: Getty

Coady started Wrexham's opening five games of the 2025-26 campaign but swiftly fell down the pecking order in north Wales.

The 33-year-old has struggled for game time since then, making just six appearances in all competitions for the Welsh outfit.

He spent the second half of the season on loan at Charlton and featured 12 times for the Addicks.



Despite returning to the club, the defender did not feature for Wrexham in the early stages of the current campaign.

It led to Wrexham mutually agreeing to rip up his contract earlier this week, allowing him to leave as a free agent.



Coady exclusively told talkSPORT his reasons for the departure. He said: "You say it's a bad ending and it always is when you come to these kinds of scenarios, where you've got to leave a football club for certain reasons.

"One thing I will say is the club was brilliant, Wrexham were fantastic. The owners, I'm sure everybody knows, are fantastic.



"My time there has been tough, for one reason or another, I didn't feel I got the opportunity to make a difference, if we want to put it that way.

"For one reason or another, it just didn't work and I found myself at Charlton at the back end of last season, which I loved, by the way. It was fantastic, a wonderful football club, and a wonderful manager.

"So, I knew this was coming. I wanted to fight for my place a little bit in pre-season, but when you get to the end of the transfer window and you know things aren't going to materialise the way you want...

3 Coady carries a lot of top-flight experience for any club who is targeting promotion Credit: Getty



"I just want to play, I want to be involved, I want to be a big driving force behind whatever club I'm at. I never got the opportunity to do it at Wrexham. Listen, they were great, I had a conversation with them over the weekend.

"They knew I didn't want to just sit there and do nothing, and they didn't want me sitting there doing nothing, so it was amicable, everything was fine. Like I said, I didn't really feel I got that opportunity but, come the end of it, they were brilliant with me."

The next chapter

The ex-Everton defender is now working with Liverpool's Under-21s following his departure from the Championship club, yet confirmed he is still searching for his next club.

He has 128 top-flight appearances, most famously captaining Wolves in the Premier League.



It did not work out at Wrexham - but Coady insisted that was not down to a rift with manager Phil Parkinson.

He added: "When I went there last summer, it was something I really wanted to be a part of and sometimes I think people look at footballers and think something's happened.

3 Coady's most successful spell of his career came at Wolves Credit: AFP

"Nothing's ever personal in football. Sometimes a manager just doesn't take to you and I think that was what it was.



"[But] I've got a really good relationship with Phil Parkinson - nothing's ever happened between us.

"I had a great relationship when I was there and they were brilliant with me in January when it came to maybe wanting to leave if there was an opportunity.

"Wrexham is a brilliant, brilliant club so I can't sit here now and rule anything out because I don't know what's going to happen."

Sports.title: ‘So light’ – Chelsea had 9/10 window before getting rolled over at the last minute
Sports.content:
‘So light’ – Chelsea had 9/10 window before getting rolled over at the last minute

Jason Cundy was delighted with Chelsea's summer transfer window right up until the final hours of Deadline Day.

The Blues spent nearly £350million on new players - but Cundy has been left furious by their last-minute drama.



4 Cundy isn't happy with how the final day of the transfer window went for Chelsea Credit: Getty

Enzo Fernandez departed to join Manchester City in a record-equalling £125m deal following a long transfer saga.

Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara was then soon identified as a replacement, with a deal agreed to sign him.

But things came crumbling down after the deadline passed, with the Ligue 1 side pulling out of the deal in a decision that left Chelsea accusing them of acting 'in a deeply unprofessional way'.



The U-turn meant that the Blues were unable to sign a replacement for Fernandez after his departure, despite a late enquiry for Everton's James Garner, who they were willing to pay up to £65m for.

And that's something that has really impacted the success of the window for Cundy, who thinks his beloved former club could find themselves in trouble in midfield this season...



Chelsea's transfer window 'plummeted'

Reacting to the collapsed Camara transfer, Cundy said on The Sports Bar: "Monaco have absolutely rolled us over...

"I'm not going to France on holiday ever again, they've absolutely rolled us over."



He added: "From Chelsea's transfer business, I'd have probably given us an 8.5 or 9/10.

"But that has plummeted now, we are so light in the middle of the park, we're so light.

"Two injuries in there and we are [in trouble]."

4 Camara was set to join Chelsea when Monaco pulled the plug on the deal Credit: Getty

4 And it meant that the Blues were unable to replace Fernandez, who joined Man City Credit: Getty



Chelsea sold Fernandez after already letting Andrey Santos and Dario Essugo leave the club too in the summer window.

It leaves the Blues with Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson as natural midfielders in the squad.

And that's something that Jamie O'Hara has been left bemused by, as he questioned why they have strengthened a rival whilst making their own situation worse on Deadline Day.

O'Hara said: "I cannot believe that Chelsea have weakened the squad with Enzo Fernandez and gave him to a direct rival in Man City, which makes them way better in midfield."



"That's not the problem, the problem is we haven't replaced him...selling Enzo wasn't the issue," Cundy replied.

"It's £125m, the issue isn't selling Enzo. The problem is we haven't replaced him."

4 Cundy wanted to rate Chelsea's window highly after some impressive deals Credit: Getty

Who did Chelsea sign and sell this summer?

If Fernandez had been replaced, then Cundy would have stuck with his impressive 9/10 rating for Chelsea's business.



And that rating was so high following the £117m arrival of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, who has already scored and assisted for the club in two Premier League games.

Maxence Lacroix, Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria also joined to strengthen the defence, while Henderson and Danny Welbeck were signed to add some more experience to a very young squad.

And the Blues acted quickly to replace Robert Sanchez in goal after an opening-weekend howler, bringing in Emi Martinez.

Meanwhile, when it comes to sales, Chelsea were also very active, letting Sanchez go on loan, alongside Alejandro Garnacho, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Filip Jorgensen and Mykhailo Mudryk.



Tosin Adarabioyo and Trevoh Chalobah left permanently, with Liam Delap also leaving for a huge fee of £50m.

Chelsea's key summer ins and outs In Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa) - £117m

Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace) - £52m

Marco Palestra (Atalanta) - £43m

Geovany Quenda (Sporting) - £40m

Honest Ahanor (Atalanta) - £40m

Emanuel Emegha (Strasbourg) - £22m

Pep Chavarria (Rayo Vallecano) - £18m

Denner (Corinthians) - £8.7m

Emi Martinez (Aston Villa) - £7.5m

Dastan Satpaev (Kairat Almaty) £2.1m

Jordan Henderson - Free

Valentin Barco (Strasbourg) - Undisclosed

Danny Welbeck (Brighton) - Undisclosed Out Enzo Fernandez (Manchester City) - £125m

Nicolas Jackson (Aston Villa) - £65m

Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid) - £52m

Andrey Santos (Manchester United) - £50m

Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest) - £50m

Trevoh Chalobah (Como) - £25m

They also brought in over £120m from the sales of Marc Cucurella, Nicolas Jackson and Tyrique George.

Before, of course, they sold Fernandez to Man City for £125m, but failed to replace him on Deadline Day in the end.

And due to the big money brought in, Chelsea actually ended up making a profit in the summer window.



The Blues spent £349m but sold £382m worth of players, so made a profit of £33m altogether.

However, Cundy struggled to celebrate that, as they now continue the season with limited options in midfield.

Sports.title: Transfer notebook: Chelsea’s ‘mystery’ deadline day target revealed after last-minute £65million attempt
Sports.content:
Everton rejected an 11th-hour attempt by Chelsea to prise James Garner away from Merseyside.

Chelsea identified a list of deadline day midfield targets as they looked to replace Enzo Fernandez - including what was being described as a 'mystery' Premier League player.



3 Chelsea were snubbed by Everton after a desperate Deadline Day attempt to sign Toffees star Garner Credit: Getty

That player was Everton ace Garner, with Xabi Alonso attracted to the former Manchester United youngster as he can also provide cover at right-back.

Sources at talkSPORT say the Blues were willing to pay £65m for the 25-year-old, having held out for their full record-equaling £125m Fernandez valuation from Manchester City.

However, Everton were unwilling to entertain any offers so late in the window.



England international Garner is settled at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Liverpool could hijack Chelsea target

Chelsea face competition from Liverpool if they want to revive their ill-fated move for Lamine Camara.

Camara was set to complete a £47m deadline day move from Monaco to Stamford Bridge.



The west Londoners were left fuming when Monaco reneged on the deal despite the two clubs having a written agreement in place.

talkSPORT can exclusively reveal Liverpool contacted Camara's advisers to express an interest in signing him next summer.



The 22-year-old Senegalese is being eyed as a replacement for Alexis Mac Allister, who could leave Anfield at the end of the season.

The Argentine's father recently came out to quash wild rumours of a possible late summer move to Man City, insisting his son sees his immediate future at Anfield, with his contract running until the summer of 2028.

3 Camara angered Chelsea by going back on an agreement to join them... and he could anger them further by joining Liverpool instead Credit: Getty

New signings bad news for PL promotion hero

Premier League new-boys Hull were one of the most active clubs in the transfer window.



The Tigers signed no fewer than 18 new faces, including SIX on deadline day, taking their spending to more than £150m.

The raft of new arrivals means manager Sergej Jakirovic has too many players for his 25-man Premier League squad

talkSPORT understands Jakirovic will be forced to leave out former Rangers midfielder and promotion hero Kieran Dowell.

Doswell played 13 Championship games, scoring one goal, after moving to the MKM in January from the Scottish Premiership giants.



He even scored in Hull's EFL Cup second round win over Stoke last month, but now faces being axed from the squad.

3 Dowell played a role in Hull's top flight promotion but could now be ditched from the squad less than a year after joining from Rangers Credit: Getty

Blackburn eye move for free agent star

Blackburn are among a number of Championship clubs showing interest in Republic of Ireland midfielder Will Smallbone.

Smallbone is available as a free agent after leaving Southampton at the end of last season.



Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray is keen to bring the 22-year-old ex-Premier League star to Ewood Park.

Sports.title: Footballer, 20, breaks down in floods of tears alongside his mum after being forced out of his boyhood club due to strict financial rules
Sports.content:
LaLiga star Pablo Garcia was left in tears after being forced to leave boyhood club Real Betis on deadline day. Twenty-year-old Garcia has been a regular for Betis, playing in all three league games so far this season, but has now put pen to paper on a deal to join Racing Santander. He joined Betis aged six, and worked his way through the academy ranks to become a first team regular. He played 33 times for the club in total, scoring six goals – including a late winner against Valencia last week. But, with the club keen to re-sign former Arsenal and Real Madrid man, they needed to make quick money, and decided to let Garcia go. He was seen in floods of tears as he left Betis' stadium on Tuesday evening, waving to fans as he wiped his eyes. Ceballos, 30, was contracted to Madrid for nine years in total, with two of those spent on loan at Arsenal. He had joined Betis as a teenager, playing for them until 2017, when he moved to Madrid. 🟢❗️ Así se ha marchado Pablo García del #RealBetis. ↪️El canterano, a lágrimas con su madre. @manu_colchon pic.twitter.com/NXZsUxTmHJ — Deportes Sevilla (@deportesDDS) September 1, 2026 A teary Pablo Garcia waved goodbye to Real Betis fans on Tuesday as he was sold for financial reasons Garcia joined Betis at the age of six, but has now left the club for Racing Santander Betis, therefore, were essentially forced to pick between the two players, and chose Ceballos, who signed a three-year deal. Football fans, though, were left stunned by the decision. 'Shameless!' one fan wrote on X. 'You don't do this to family!' Another posted: 'Aren't you ashamed?' A third shared: 'This really is sad. We have to blame (Javier) Tebas (LaLiga president).' Garcia told Spanish media: 'It is a very difficult time for everyone, but we have to keep our heads up and look forward. I hope to return, that is what we all want.' 'There were many things I could not influence. I wish everything had gone as we had all hoped. Thank you very much from the bottom of my heart to all Betis fans.' His father added on RadioCOPE: 'This is really hard for us. If that is how Betis fans feel, imagine how we must feel. It was 15 years, a whole eternity.' While Ceballos could be in line to make his second debut against former side Madrid this weekend, Betis will take on Rayo Vallecano on Saturday. The two teams will face off next in December.

Sports.title: Tennis bad boy tries to quit US Open match in remarkable moment after smashing racket in furious outburst... but umpire tells him he can't
Sports.content:
Tennis bad boy tries to quit US Open match in remarkable moment after smashing racket in furious outburst... but umpire tells him he can't

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tennis bad boy Corentin Moutet was initially told he could not retire when he tried to quit his US Open match in a bizarre ending to his first-round match.

Moutet had a tough time against Australian Dane Sweeny and put an end to his struggles by retiring through injury while two sets down and 3-0 down in the third set.

The previous set, he had demolished his racket in a furious outburst, earning a racket abuse penalty, and eventually decided enough was enough as he cited an injury as his reason to end the match.

But in a bizarre finish, the umpire initially told him he was not able to retire as he had not yet been seen by a physio.

Moutet caused confusion when he approached Sweeny to shake his hand, then shook the umpire's hand.

The umpire appeared confused and called a physio to examine the Frenchman, who then insisted he didn't need a trainer and wanted to end the match.

Corentin Moutet's US Open game to a bizarre ending when he retired from his match

Moutet was told he had to see a physio as a supervisor was called to the court

Moutet had smashed his racket in a trademark outburst earlier in the match

After a supervisor arrived on the court and suggested an assessment would be needed to officially declare the match over, Moutet's retirement was eventually accepted.

Moutet later explained: 'It's my wrist, it's been bothering me, it just won't go away despite all the effort I've put in. I don't really know what to say about it, it's been hurting for a long time. Since Vienna last year.

'The problem is that I tried to play, to push it every time. And that triggered pain elsewhere. In Cincinnati, I decided to take a break to try and put the racket down and prepare for here.

'I worked very hard physically, without playing tennis. It was long, it was hard, and it's frustrating not to be ready to play the last Grand Slam of the year.'

Moutet has built up a bad-boy reputation after a number of emotional on-court outbursts and an expletive BBC interview that saw him fined around $40,000 before Wimbledon.

'I never understood why you become the bad guy if you're mad when you lose. For me, the strange guys are the ones smiling after they lose,' he recently said on The Tennis Insider Club.

'From the age of seven until I was about 16, I barely lost a match—maybe 10 a year at most. So I never learned how to lose. For a long time, that was very hard for me, because when things started going badly, I didn't know what was happening.

'The reality is that, at some point, you're going to lose. Then you're going to lose again, and again, and again. Nobody ever told me that.'

Moutet later discussed the injury that caused him to retire from the match while two sets down

Australian wildcard Dane Sweeny has progressed after the match against the fiery Frenchman

Wildcard Sweeny has joined qualifier and childhood friend Tristan Schoolkate in the second round.

'Yeah, it's really nice,' Sweeny told AAP. 'I'm always rooting for the Aussie boys and it's nice to see a couple get over the line, especially Tristan. We've known each other for so long.'

He left the match against Moutet with battle scars of his own, icing a lump on his elbow after the match.

'The lump's usually standard, but I haven't been icing it,' he said. 'When I dive, I land on the same spot every time, so it just keeps popping up,' Sweeny said.

'I've got like permanent fluid build-up there. Sometimes I can't help it - I'm in the air before I even know it.'

Sports.title: Time is running out for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: AJ is still yet to sign Battle of Britain deal, reveals Frank Warren
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has still not signed the contract, so the Battle of Britain against Tyson Fury remains in jeopardy.

Time is running out.

Promoter Frank Warren, who suggested that in reality boxing's longest hatching deal had to be finalised by this weekend, says: 'AJ hasn't signed yet.

'Tyson signed in January. He's training in Miami for the fight in early November and doesn't care where it takes place. '

The original agreement stipulated England, putting Wembley Stadium on alert.

But Netflix, the mega-paymasters for the broadcast, have joined their Saudi partners in insisting on New York's fabled Madison Square Garden so as to maximise US revenue.

Anthony Joshua (pictured) is still yet to sign the deal to fight Anthony Joshua, Frank Warren has revealed

Warren (right) said Tyson Fury (left) has signed and is already in training for a potential bout

Joshua will need at least a two-month training camp for a fight of this magnitude and ideally nine to ten weeks.

It comes after Joshua was given 10 days to agree a deal on August 26 - seven days ago - with Warren previously warning: 'Unless AJ commits by the end of next week I'm afraid this will slip away like so many of those great fights which never happened.'

He added: 'At some point everyone has to say the most important thing is that it happens. Not this bulls*** about money.

'That everyone wants the fight. Does AJ really want it? I don't know. He's been through that tragedy of the car crash which killed two of his closest friends. Only he knows what he wants.'

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's 'missed opportunity' transfer window: How Gunners lost out on Morgan Rogers, Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Junior, late move for blockbuster target revealed - and the market wins that soften the blow
Sports.content:
Inside Arsenal's 'missed opportunity' transfer window: How Gunners lost out on Morgan Rogers, Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Junior, late move for blockbuster target revealed - and the market wins that soften the blow

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Arsenal end the summer transfer window with three fewer attackers than they started it with. That is certainly not a state of affairs many would have predicted, particularly as they are reigning Premier League champions, yet here we are.

The need to evolve in the face of their Big Six rivals strengthening was an area co-chair Josh Kroenke had claimed was a key target. After sealing the title in May, he said: ‘Right now there are other teams that are already trying to strengthen to come at us for next season. So we need to be aware of that.

‘We’ve already had a few conversations about different areas that we think we can improve – both on and off the pitch. We are looking forward to getting that going this summer.’

A decent-ish window with solid additions has followed, you could argue, but far from a dominant one. A squad sturdy enough to retain the title, yes, but a chance to create an impregnable line-up capable of leaving their rivals in the dust was squandered.

It was almost a throwback summer for a club which seems to have an allergic reaction to strikers.

Last year, the signing of Viktor Gyokeres had quelled the years-long cries from supporters to invest in a top-quality centre forward. This summer, however, was a return to the days of 2023 and 2024, where the club’s inability to land a striker (Kai Havertz was signed initially as a midfielder) caused bewilderment and frustration in equal measure.

Arsenal may have missed out on several of their top targets this summer - but the addition of Bruno Guimaraes was one of the most impressive deals any club made in the window

New winger Christos Tzolis was signed to be one for the future, but has made an impressive start to life in north London

The hierarchy’s overall plans this time were executed with mixed results, some areas nailed impressively. The £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes looks like a bargain, in comparison to the prices of other midfielders across the league – such as Enzo Fernandez (£125m), Elliot Anderson (£116m) and Sandro Tonali (£100m). Guimaraes is arguably a better player than Tonali, but was signed for £25m less. So that was a real win. It’s in the forward line where the issues arise.

Arsenal wanted Morgan Rogers, but he went to Chelsea. Vinicius Junior was the prize the Gunners wanted most, but he chose to stay at Real Madrid, some cynics arguing he used the interest to get himself a better contract.

Julian Alvarez was a more long-term target, an ultimately unrealistic one in that he had his heart set on Barcelona. It is understood Arsenal knew the chase was up last weekend.

Yet, the pursuit of a striker went beyond this. Daily Mail Sport understands assistant manager Gabriel Heinze reached out to Inter Milan’s Lautaro Martinez – a fellow Argentine – early last week over a potential move.

In response Inter refused to entertain any kind of deal, the attacker still having three years left on his contract. So, Arsenal were actively trying to bring a striker into the club, aware of the need for one to supplement Havertz and Gyokeres with Gabriel Jesus out the door to Barca.

In fact, Gyokeres hasn’t played a single minute in either of Arsenal’s two league matches thus far. Was that a sign from Arteta to the board? Maybe.

Arsenal were interested in Rogers, but only for a fee of around £80million. Once that had been exceeded by Chelsea, they walked away from the table. Sources claim Rogers was keen on a move and that his camp urged Arsenal to match Chelsea’s bid as the player wanted a move to the Gunners.

Arsenal also had a look at Bradley Barcola, the Paris Saint-Germain winger eventually sold to Liverpool for £123m. The Gunners weren’t convinced he was worth the money so didn’t put a bid in.

Arsenal missed out on England star Morgan Rogers after Chelsea far exceeded their vaulation of the player

Gunners assistant manager Gabriel Heinze reached out to Inter Milan’s Lautaro Martinez (pictured) – a fellow Argentine – early last week over a potential move

Away from Rogers and Barcola, the Arsenal frontline is more bare than before. The club have lost three forward players in Leandro Trossard, Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli (Martinelli’s move to Al-Hilal is still to be finalised, the Saudi window closing on September 6) and added one, in Christos Tzolis. Attacking midfielder Ethan Nwaneri also headed out, on loan to Borussia Dortmund.

It’s the left-wing area where the lack of options is particularly stark, Tzolis and Eberechi Eze the only two obvious candidates.

Greek winger Tzolis was earmarked as a player with a high-ceiling who would fight for a starting place, but more one for the future than right now. Eze, meanwhile, spent most of last season as an attacking midfielder. Bring the possibility of injuries into the mix, which hurt Arsenal last season, and the options thin out.

With no Martinelli, Noni Madueke is now expected to play on either wing more than last season.

Arsenal’s inability to bring in an attacker aside from Tzolis is a tough pill to swallow for a fanbase believing they would land a marquee signing in the form of either Vinicius or Alvarez. Madueke potentially filling in on the left is some fall in expectation.

It must be said, the market in which Arsenal are hunting for a forward is a highly exclusive one with very few options – and sky-high prices. That is not easy to navigate, even though sporting director Andrea Berta will now face scrutiny for his inability to land such a signing.

The biggest purchase of deadline day for Kroenke Sports and Entertainment (KSE) wasn’t a pricey forward, but the £2.9billion acquisition of baseball franchise Los Angeles Angels. How Arsenal fans would have wished for that level of ambition to be directed towards the Emirates instead.

There are positives, though, in what is still a good window for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa was a smart addition. He bolsters an already formidable backline, cementing the Gunners’ squad as the league’s best defensive unit.

The imminent departure of Gabriel Martinelli (right) means Noni Madueke is likely to have to fill in on the left wing at points this season

The signing of Ezri Konsa was a double win: Arsenal got a good player to bolster their backline, and denied several of their biggest rivals the chance to sign him

But the England man also performs another function: depriving the other Big Six clubs of signing a proven centre back. All of Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea were in much more need of Konsa than Arsenal. Preventing them getting him is a boost.

Tzolis showed promising signs in the Community Shield victory over Manchester City and his man-of-the-match display against Coventry. He struggled against Villa on Monday, but that is to be expected for a player acclimatising to such a tough league.

A further victory from the window for Arsenal is their sales. For years, they have attracted attention for being poor at securing major outgoings.

The terminated contracts of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Mesut Ozil, Nicolas Pepe and Sead Kolasinac in previous years did little to quell narratives that the Gunners are worse at selling than their rivals.

A record sale of £35m for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool back in 2017 didn’t help, either. This summer, that record is set to be broken once Martinelli’s £55m move to Al-Hilal goes through.

Overall, more than £100m has been raised through selling Jesus to Barcelona (£9m), Trossard to Besiktas (£15m), Jakub Kiwior to Porto (£15m), Fabio Vieira to Hamburg (£9m) and Christian Norgaard to Everton (£7m).

The departures of Martinelli, Jesus and Vieira, for example, take around £500k off the wage bill; that has an impact.

Arsenal have had a decent window - though ultimately missed out on the blockbuster forward addition that would have made Mikel Arteta's men overwhelming favourites for the title

Ultimately, Arsenal have had a decent window, strengthening a solid backline and adding depth in midfield. Though the failure to add another forward to the squad feels like a missed opportunity.

This was the summer when Arsenal had the chance to go from defending champions to overwhelming favourites after finally ending a 22-year wait for the title. Instead, they have arguably finished the window with less attacking depth than previously.

Arsenal remain one of the best teams in Europe and are clear favourites to retain the title.

With Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea and others all looking to close the gap, though, the margin for error will be smaller than it needed to be.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods strikes deal and pleads guilty to reckless driving... after arriving at court with doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has pleaded guilty to reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after striking a deal with prosecutors in the wake of his DUI arrest.

The golf legend was suited-and-booted as he arrived at court with girlfriend Vanessa Trump on his arm, looking stoic while wading through photographers outside the Martin County Court shortly after 8am on Wednesday.

Woods was pictured in the courtroom moments later, where he stood in front of a judge and changed his plea. He was originally charged with driving under the influence but has now pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

Tiger Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving at a hearing in Florida on Wednesday morning

Woods appeared puffy-eyed as he left the court alongside doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump

Vanessa led him back to their car after he had pleaded guilty and had his license suspended

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

He was able to crawl out of the car without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’s system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by the Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

A previous hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods's attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods appeared puffy-faced as he arrived for his change-of-plea hearing in Florida

Vanessa was front and center inside the court as Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods in the back of a police cruiser after being arrested on suspicion of DUI in March

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

Woods' legal problems have since been put into perspective by Vanessa's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

The March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods's adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

Witnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) in Jupiter, Florida, on May 29, 2017. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods changed his original not guilty plea in the wake of his DUI arrest back in March

Vanessa with him and her 19-year-old daughter Kai back in March

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was found by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers - Vicodin and Dilaudid - the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

He later claimed he had been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia. Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service. He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

In July 2017, Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on painkillers.

Woods stands alongside his lawyer to face County Judge Darren Steele on Wednesday

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story. After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of the November 27, 2009 crash were ultimately included in the best-selling biography by Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: How Chelsea won the transfer window: Why Blues insiders think Enzo Fernandez deal is a win, the stars they kept despite circling vultures, how the five big-wigs split the work... and the one major regret
Sports.content:
How Chelsea won the transfer window: Why Blues insiders think Enzo Fernandez deal is a win, the stars they kept despite circling vultures, how the five big-wigs split the work... and the one major regret

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Some supporters whose focus is fixed on English football might not have heard of Lamine Camara before Chelsea agreed to sign him for £47million on deadline day. He’s 22 years old, an international for Senegal and a tenacious midfielder for Monaco.

They have heard of him now, a few fans even suggesting what happened with the promising Camara on Tuesday evening spoiled an otherwise successful summer. We will get to why that is something of an overreaction in a moment, but first, there is no question it made for a messy end to the window.

Camara had completed medical tests in Monaco overseen by Chelsea staff on standby. He had spoken with Xabi Alonso to understand his plans for him. He had agreed a six-year contract with the option of an additional 12 months. A private plane had been arranged to fly him to London on Wednesday morning to begin a new chapter in his career because a full, written, club-to-club agreement was in place.

Then it collapsed, with Monaco informing Chelsea in writing that they were cancelling the transfer, minutes before the 11pm deadline and with the French side declining to sign a deal sheet which would have given everyone an extra two hours to resurrect it.

That would have been helpful when Monaco's Folarin Balogun then decided at 12am that he did not fancy being transferred to Everton. Monaco needed the money and got none.

Chelsea are angry at Monaco. Some of that anger might also be aimed at themselves for leaving it so late to sign a replacement for Enzo Fernandez and running such a risk. It felt an inevitability that Fernandez would leave this summer. There was too much smoke. In the end, he was sold and not replaced.

Enzo Fernandez was no stranger to a yellow card during his time at Chelsea, who are pleased with the fee they got from Manchester City for him

Morgan Rogers (right) is already linking brilliantly with his mate Cole Palmer and looks like a great signing despite the hefty fee

However, this singular failing should not cloud what was overall a corrective window for Chelsea after a campaign in which they finished 10th in the Premier League.

Of the 20-man squad that Chelsea took to Sunderland on the final day of last season, 10 were sold or loaned, Fernandez included. A cultural reset was required. There were still some Enzo Maresca soldiers in the ranks. Liam Rosenior never stood a chance as his successor. Alonso only wanted to keep those totally committed to the cause.

Since BlueCo acquired Chelsea in 2022, nobody had been booked more for dissent than Fernandez, cautioned 12 times for bad behaviour. He was one of those who added to the narrative that this team was too ill-disciplined to succeed. Maresca clearly liked that competitive edge he carried as his vice-captain.

So Chelsea sold Fernandez to City for a big bag of cash – as big as any ever secured in English football, tied with that which Newcastle nabbed from Liverpool for Alexander Isak. Fernandez is a fine footballer, but it is hard to think this 25-year-old Argentinian is worth a fixed fee of £125m even in this silliest of summers.

Chelsea got themselves a good deal from that perspective, particularly after City opened negotiations by proposing a payment of £104m plus add-ons. While Chelsea wanted closer to £135m, they ended up making a profit on a player they signed for £106.8m from Benfica in 2023 and who never truly lived up to that price tag’s hype.

The hair in the soup is that they did not then replace Fernandez. They tried over the summer. They bid £64m for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott in July. They held talks for Roma’s Manu Kone. They chased Camara. Signing nobody for the midfield was a disappointment, and that view will be shared internally at Chelsea after how deadline day unfolded.

It was the only area within the team that they did not strengthen. City did not play along with the deadline they set for offers on Fernandez earlier in August, and by the time they agreed to sanction his sale, they were somewhat snookered and against the clock.

Chelsea managed to keep hold of Joao Pedro despite the advances of Barcelona

But they missed out on Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara (left) after a deadline-day farrago

While Chelsea can be pleased with their big bag of cash, it will not help them on the pitch, starting this Sunday at the home of the Premier League champions, Arsenal.

They will now be relying on Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson as senior midfield options. Malo Gusto can also be used centrally if required. Reggie Watson, their academy prospect aged 16, impressed in pre-season under Alonso along with Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, also 16.

What will help Chelsea, though, are the others they brought in. While they tried and failed to sign Camara after Monaco’s U-turn, this was still the summer in which Chelsea got serious.

They tried being Todd Boehly’s plaything. They built the Premier League’s youngest-ever side under Behdad Eghbali. In this window, they signed Emiliano Martinez to solve the goalkeeper problem, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Marco Palestra, Pep Chavarria, Danny Welbeck and Henderson.

They kept hold of Joao Pedro, who was wanted by Barcelona, and Cole Palmer, who spent the last season hearing how Manchester United were ready to recruit him. All in all, it was not bad business considering Chelsea entered into this summer amid the usual forecasts of financial Armageddon.

At the same time, Chelsea cleared house, selling or loaning Robert Sanchez, Tosin Adarabioyo, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Alejandro Garnacho, Mykhailo Mudryk, Marc Guiu, Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, among others.

They insisted they would only sell Pedro Neto for close to £100m and Gusto for £75m, with Liverpool making a play for the latter on deadline day to no avail.

After some of their more out-there experiments in recent years, this was the summer Chelsea got serious - as additions like Emiliano Martinez proved

Chelsea’s approach was described as a collaboration, each of their five sporting directors concentrating on their own areas and Eghbali more invested than most co-owners would be.

For example, a great deal of Paul Winstanley’s work focuses on negotiating with clubs and agents and arranging contracts, such as that signed by Joao Pedro this summer.

When working on signings, Laurence Stewart might deal with the data team, or Joe Shields with the scouting department. Sam Jewell’s remit extends to Strasbourg as well as Chelsea, and then there is Dave Fallows, their newest sporting director who is still building his internal portfolio with background checks on prospective purchases among his responsibilities.

Nobody does everything. Chelsea decided some time ago to narrow their directors’ focuses so that they can go deeper into each area, while Alonso has been allowed his own voice with every signing greenlighted by him as manager.

While it ended in anger over the collapse of Camara, the bigger picture shows this club coming out of this summer better than they went into it.

Sports.title: Controversial Real Madrid star Raul Asencio is slapped with eight-month driving ban for driving nearly four times over the legal limit - ahead of trial for allegedly sharing explicit video involving a minor
Sports.content:
Real Madrid player Raul Asencio has been banned from the roads for eight months after being convicted of drink-driving ahead of his sex tape sharing trial. The 23-year-old defender has also been fined £12,350. Details of the conviction emerged on Wednesday and were confirmed by court sources in Gran Canaria, where the footballer hails from. He was stopped at a police checkpoint while driving a Porsche Macan GTS in San Bartolome de Tirajana in the south of the holiday island around 6.30am on August 16. He pleaded guilty to drink-driving at court three days later in a speedy trial. The Los Blancos star, who is currently out injured, is understood to have been nearly four-times over the drink-drive limit in Spain, which stands at 0.25 milligrams of alcohol per litre in exhaled breath. Raul Asencio (right), pictured with influencer Selenia Suarez, has been charged with drink driving Asencio’s reading was 0.90 milligrams per litre. The conviction is the latest setback for the footballer who is due to go on trial on Thursday over the alleged sharing of a sex tape involving a minor. He is accused of sharing the tape as well as distributing the intimate footage without consent. Both alleged victims have withdrawn their complaints against the footballer, paving the way for a probable acquittal. Public prosecutors continue to demand a prison sentence of two-and-a-half years on conviction but have said they will withdraw the charges against Asencio if the alleged victims ratify in court the apologies they say he offered them during the court investigation. Asencio’s former team-mates Ferran Ruiz, Juan Rodriguez and Andres Garcia are also set to stand trial. Ruiz, Rodriguez and Garcia are accused of recording and distributing sexual videos involving a minor and another woman. Asencio is not accused of being involved in the alleged incident. The Real Madrid defender, 23, is awaiting trial over the alleged sharing of a sex tape involving a minor Ruiz, Rodriguez and Garcia were arrested in September 2023 over the June 15 2023 incident at a beach club in Gran Canaria during which the three then-Real Madrid academy players had consensual sexual relations with the two females but allegedly filmed them without their consent. Asencio was initially interviewed by police in connection with the case before becoming part of the investigation itself. In May 2025, the Real Madrid defender released a statement fiercely denying allegations made against him.

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara's furious agent accuses clubs of failing to 'respect African players' in astonishing attack after both stars fail to secure deadline day moves
Sports.content:
The agent of Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and Monaco's Lamine Camara has astonishingly accused football clubs of failing to respect African players after his two clients missed out on deadline day transfers.

Diomansy Kamara, who previously played for Portsmouth, West Bromwich Albion and Fulham during his career, told clubs to stop treating African footballers as 'just a commodity' in a scathing attack on Instagram, hours after the window slammed shut.

Senegal international Sarr had hoped to secure a move away from Crystal Palace amid links to Liverpool and Galatasaray but ultimately finished the window at Selhurst Park, while Camara's £47million transfer to Chelsea collapsed at the 11th hour after Monaco pulled out of the deal.

Furiously speaking out on the failed transfers on Wednesday morning, Kamara posted on his Instagram story: 'The cases of Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara must all interrogate us.

'We have to get out of this logic where the African player can sometimes give the feeling that he is just a commodity: you buy it, you set its price, you negotiate its future and, too often, your will seems to go to the background.

'Our African players deserve respect. The respect of their work. The respect of their career. Respecting their ambitions. The respect of their voices.

The agent of Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr (left) and Monaco's Lamine Camara (right) has launched a scathing attack on clubs after his players failed to secure a move on deadline day

Agent Diomansy Kamara has accused clubs of treating African players as 'just a commodity'

'A transfer shouldn't just be a matter of two clubs and numbers. Behind every contract, there's a man, a career, dreams and life choices.

'The fact that clubs can sometimes have the final word is a reality of professional football. But one question remains: what about the career and the will of the player?

'The player must be able to be heard and respected in the decisions that determine his future.

'Let's never forget what's important: behind every success, it's the players who write history first.'

Camara's failed move to Chelsea became one of the main stories of deadline day as it left Xabi Alonso's side short in midfield following the British record departure of Enzo Fernandez for £125m to Manchester City.

Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal.

Yet, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached.

Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn.

Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Monaco's sporting director Thiago Scuro described the club's decision to pull out of the transfer as 'part of the game' in Wednesday's press conference.

Scuro revealed that Alonso had spoken to Camara, who had told Monaco he wanted to leave, but explained they pulled the plug after Balogun's move to Everton fell through.

According to the sporting director, wantaway Camara was told that Monaco would secure a major transfer for him 'very soon' and could present him with 'ever better options' than those that surfaced on deadline day.

He urged that Camara remains fully committed and professional with regards to his role at Monaco, despite feeling disappointed.

Sports.title: 5 Liverpool transfers can still happen this month as Euros winner linked with move
Sports.content:
5 Liverpool transfers can still happen this month as Euros winner linked with move

The Premier League deadline may have passed, but Liverpool could still complete five transfers before their summer business concludes

View 2 Images Lewis Koumas looks set to stay at Anfield but could still leave to gain experience elsewhere (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

The Premier League transfer window is shut, but Liverpool's summer activity isn't necessarily complete. A late surge of deals at Anfield saw Bradley Barcola arrive for £123million, while Lucca Brughmans completed a £30m deadline day switch, though he'll remain at Genk for the remainder of this campaign.

‌



All told, Liverpool recorded the highest net expenditure of any side in England's top tier this summer. The Reds finished £219m in deficit, more than any other Premier League club, after splashing out heavily while generating minimal income through departures.

‌



There may be an opportunity to further balance the books, however, given that various leagues across the globe remain open for transfers. Mirror Football has outlined a selection of players who could still depart Liverpool in the coming days and weeks.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Lewis Koumas

Lewis Koumas sits near the top of Liverpool's current crop of emerging talent and caught the eye during an encouraging pre-season spell. All signs suggest he's done enough to earn a spot in the first-team squad this term but a loan away could still work out best for all parties in the long term.

Liverpool made Monaco call to make plan clear as Chelsea's Lamine Camara transfer collapsed READ MORE :

Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool facing new deadline after late summer transfers completed READ MORE :

Koumas, 20, came off the bench for a 12-minute cameo in the draw against Newcastle before he was an unused substitute against Nottingham Forest. Barcola's arrival only serves to further restrict opportunities for those on the fringes of the left wing.

‌



A Championship loan could have been the perfect solution for the 12-cap Wales international, while the Scottish Premiership and Belgium's Pro League shut up shop tomorrow (Sept. 3). The Eredivisie transfer window closes at midnight tonight, while the windows in Turkey (Friday) and Portugal (Sept. 15) offer more time.

Harvey Davies

With Alisson and Giorgi Mamardashvili both remaining at Anfield this summer, the pathway to the No. 1 shirt appears congested for Harvey Davies. Freddie Woodman also penned a fresh contract this summer, while Vitezslav Jaros' presence probably means four goalkeepers sit above Davies in the hierarchy.

Reports earlier this summer suggested there are intentions to extend Davies' own deal, which is set to run out next summer. Those same reports indicated the 22-year-old, who has been at the club since 2011, would be retained as cover until January before another assessment is made regarding his future.

‌



Those arrangements could yet be brought forward, however, in order to afford the youngster a much-needed opportunity at senior football. His possibilities are wide open, with transfer windows in Belgium, Austria, Hungary and Scotland shutting tomorrow, while those in nations like Croatia (Sept. 7) and Greece (Sept. 15) have additional time remaining.

Federico Chiesa

View 2 Images Federico Chiesa could still leave Liverpool this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Despite appearing one of the most probable exits at the beginning of the summer, Federico Chiesa remains a Liverpool player. The Euro 2020 champion has been persistently linked with a return to Serie A for months now, but wishes to compete for his position under Andoni Iraola.

‌



Chiesa's adaptability across the forward line does provide value, with the player delivering some decisive moments in red. However, the acquisition of Barcola only makes it even less likely for him to anticipate significant game time.

"Federico is not thinking about leaving Liverpool," Chiesa's father, Enrico, told 365Scores. "Chiesa is very happy at Anfield and feels extremely good within the club. As for renewing the contract, his first desire is to continue and stay with Liverpool."

The Serie A transfer deadline has now passed, ruling out any return to Italy for the former Juventus star. That said, Turkey's Super Lig remains active until Friday evening, while one of Portugal's heavyweights could still make a move right up until the evening of September 15.

‌

Jayden Danns

Jayden Danns' injury setbacks over the past year or so have limited his opportunities for any senior involvement at Liverpool. The striker is on the road to recovery again, but is close to full fitness after missing the pre-season preparations.

The case can certainly be made that Danns requires a loan spell away from Anfield as urgently as any other academy prospect. His injury problems threaten to halt his development if he isn't afforded the opportunity to compete at the appropriate standard, and a fresh environment could provide precisely the impetus he needs.

‌



Clubs in any of the previously mentioned second-tier European leagues would welcome an imposing, physical force in attack. And Danns, who appears too talented for under-21 football, could make his way back to Merseyside at some stage in 2027 looking considerably more prepared to establish himself at Anfield.

Sports.title: Famous jumps track closed due to £1.3m debts to reopen for racing in October 2027
Sports.content:
Famous jumps track closed due to £1.3m debts to reopen for racing in October 2027

Towcester racecourse has agreed to host six fixtures in the 2027-28 fixture list, having not staged horse racing since May 2018 when the track went into administration

View 2 Images The track where Sir AP McCoy (centre) rode his 4,000th winner will reopen in October 2027 (Image: Getty Images)

The track where Sir AP McCoy rode his 4,000th winner has announced the date when it will reopen for racing.

‌



Racing was first staged at Towcester racecourse in Northants in 1876 but it was forced to close eight years ago after the track went into administration with debts of more than £1.3 million and its remaining fixtures sold. Lately it has operated as a greyhound racing venue which has staged various editions of the Greyhound Derby.

‌



But it is poised to resume jumps racing during the 2027-28 season following the announcement of a landmark partnership between racecourse owners Orchestrate and online bookmaking brand Betway.

‌



World’s richest racehorse Romantic Warrior retired with immediate effect due to leg injury READ MORE :

Galopin Des Champs tragedy as dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero dies five days after retirement READ MORE :

As a result the track will officially be renamed Betway Towcester Racecourse with the bookmaker becoming the exclusive betting partner across all fixtures.

Now Towcester has agreed a programme of fixtures with the BHA which have been leased for the 2027-28 campaign

The agreed dates are October 20, November 30, December 16, January 16, February 4 and February 15. The racecourse is in the process of applying for a licence.

‌



Richard Thomas, chief executive of Orchestrate, said: “Seeing dates in the diary for the first time in nearly a decade is a genuinely exciting moment for everyone here.

“We said in July that we wanted to bring horse racing back to Towcester for the local community and for the sport, and we now have a clear programme to work towards. “There is plenty to do between now and October 2027, but work on the track is already well underway and we can't wait to welcome horses back.”

View 2 Images Towcester racecourse has not staged horse racing since 2018 (Image: PA)

‌



Orchestrate and Betway are investing more than £2 million in the venue. This will be used to fund a comprehensive overhaul of the racing surface, alongside significant improvements and modernisation of the spectator facilities.

The 20-time champion McCoy rode his historic 4,000th winner at the track in 2013.

He said: "Towcester is a track that means a great deal to me. I rode my 4,000th winner there, which was one of my most memorable milestones, so I have a strong personal connection with this racecourse.

Article continues below

"It’s fantastic to see National Hunt racing returning to the racecourse after such a long absence. It’s a proper Jumps track and with the investment being made and the plans for its future, I’m sure it can re-establish itself as a valuable course for National Hunt racing.”

Towcester is aiming to host Point-to-Point fixtures in spring 2027 ahead of the resumption of Rules racing later in the year.

Sports.title: Liverpool made Monaco call to make plan clear as Chelsea's Lamine Camara transfer collapsed
Sports.content:
Liverpool made Monaco call to make plan clear as Chelsea's Lamine Camara transfer collapsed

Chelsea missed out on landing Monaco's Lamine Camara late on deadline day - but Liverpool have told the French side they're keen on landing the midfielder next summer

View 2 Images Lamine Camara was close to a move to Chelsea (Image: Jan Kruger, Getty Images)

Chelsea's move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara failed to materialise late in the day - with Liverpool putting a call into the French side to express their interest in a future transfer.

‌



The Blues found themselves seeking a new midfielder on deadline day after it became apparent that Enzo Fernandez was bound for Manchester City. After having two bids turned down by the French outfit, Chelsea eventually secured a breakthrough and were closing in on the £47.1million signing of Camara, before the plug was pulled at the eleventh hour.

‌



TalkSport reports that Monaco still believe they can demand top dollar for their midfielder and Liverpool made contact to let the Ligue 1 club know that they would be keen to sign him in the future, potentially next summer. Liverpool's call had no bearing on Chelsea's move not coming to fruition.

‌



Monaco are ready to hold out for £60m and the Reds' midfield is an area that could be exposed this season, which would prompt action in the transfer market.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea were left fuming by the collapse of the deal with Xabi Alonso now lacking a body in midfield, even if Fernandez had largely been shunned to begin the season, owing to the noise that was surrounding his future.

‌



Roma's Manu Kone was another midfielder high on Chelsea's wishlist but they failed to land the Frenchman, who impressed at the World Cup. They were close to an agreement to sign Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini was determined to keep hold of the player, according to Sky in Italy.

So far this season Romeo Lavia, who has been plagued by injury issues, has started both Premier League games for Chelsea in midfield and been paired with Reece James and Cole Palmer as the Blues adapt to the new system employed by Alonso.

View 2 Images Liverpool have informed Monaco of their future interest in their midfielder (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



Another of Monaco's potential outings also fell through when Folarin Balogun, who was close to joining Everton, opted against the move. After initial concerns were raised during Balogun’s medical the player himself decided not to go ahead with the move to Merseyside.

Monaco have ultimately shown themselves willing to cash in on their top assets if the price is right. Kylian Mbappe remains the biggest departure of the last decade but since him the likes of Aurelien Tchouameni head to Real Madrid whilst this summer Maghnes Akliouche headed to PSG.

Sports.title: How Man Utd managed to end up without a new left-back despite late call to rivals
Sports.content:
How Man Utd managed to end up without a new left-back despite late call to rivals

Manchester United were able to secure several midfield signings over the summer but missed out on adding a left-back despite identifying several targets and making a late call to their rivals

View 2 Images Luke Shaw remains Man Utd's left-back after the club failed to get any signings through the door

Manchester United were able to address their immediate priority this summer, which was bolstering their midfield, but ultimately missed out on adding a left-back, which was also on their agenda.

‌



The Red Devils ploughed more than £150million into their midfield with Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba all moving to Old Trafford.

‌



But despite being linked with a host of names in recent months Michael Carrick was unable to improve his backline. Seeking more cover at left-back was on their radar this summer with the reliance on Luke Shaw becoming a concern.

‌



The Englishman showed himself to be more durable last season, playing in every game, but in the years before that the former Southampton man has spent long periods out injured. He's also now into his 30s and was exposed for Ipswich's opening goal on Sunday - owning the mistake himself post-match.

United's backline hasn't had a notable signing in two years. It is seen as the next area the club will strengthen, but that will likely have to wait until next summer. Until then Carrick could come to bemoan the failure to add more quality - not that United can be accused of failing to identify potential targets.

‌



Four players missed

Lewis Hall was the most high profile left-back that the Manchester outfit were linked with. He's just enjoyed the best year of his career to date with Newcastle, but after the Magpies cashed in on a host of their leading lights, they were determined not to sell another of their top performers. Even if Newcastle had been prepared to sell, the likelihood is that United would've lacked the finances to pursue the deal.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde is someone who was on the market. A loan deal could've been pursued and, despite a deadline day check in on the player, United opted against trying to land the Spaniard.

View 2 Images Rayan Ait-Nouri emerged as a late target for Man Utd (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Jorge Sanilas at Racing Santander is highly-rated in La Liga and was reported to have a relatively modest release clause. Atletico Madrid were heavily linked with him, as were Barcelona, and ultimately United never backed up their interest with a bid.

It meant Carrick's options beyond Shaw, who will need to prove he can rediscover his top form, are teenager Harry Amass. The 19-year-old was tipped for a loan move to the Championship, but ultimately remained at the Championship. Diogo Dalot is among those who could swap from the right to the left if needed.

As United desperately sought solutions they put in a late call to Manchester City. Deals between the two have been few and far between but that didn't stop them making a shock approach for Rayan Ait-Nouri.

‌



The Manchester Evening News have confirmed that they approached to see whether Ait-Nouri would be available. But City were only prepared consider a loan with an obligation to make the move permanent - the Red Devils didn't want to commit to signing Ait-Nouri permanently, and thus a deal for the Algeria international failed to materialise.

All of which has left United right where they started.

Sports.title: World’s richest racehorse Romantic Warrior retired with immediate effect due to leg injury
Sports.content:
World’s richest racehorse Romantic Warrior retired with immediate effect due to leg injury

The eight-year-old, whose regular rider was James McDonald, earned more than £27 million in prize-money and was twice named Hong Kong horse of the year

View 3 Images Romantic Warrior: retired with immediate effect (Image: Getty Images)

The world’s richest racehorse Romantic Warrior has been retired with immediate effect.

‌



Romantic Warrior earned more than £27 million in prize-money and was twice named Hong Kong horse of the year. Trained by Danny Shum, he won 24 races, 15 at Group 1 level, including four in a row in the Hong Kong Cup under regular jockey James McDonald.

‌



On the international stage he won the Cox Plate in Australia, the Yasuda Kinen in Japan and fought a famous duel with Japanese dirt champion Forever Young in the 2025 Saudi Cup, in which he was ultimately beaten by a neck.

‌
