'But we don't know who we have today in regards to Tyson Fury and where he's really at, and we don't know which AJ we have, especially after his last fight and everything he's been through.

'Look, it's going to be a big fight. Is it around about three, four, maybe five years too late. But regardless, I think the British public still want to see it.'

And that, ultimately, is why Hamed's excitement about Itauma feels so significant. He remembers what it was like when British boxing had fighters who could command the attention of an entire country. He believes Itauma could be the next one.

There is only one thing left for Itauma to do: prove him right.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic weigh-in descends into chaos as British star PUSHES rival off stage - before being SLAPPED
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic had to be pulled apart by security after their heavyweight weigh-in descended into chaos when Hrgovic was pushed off the stage before slapping his British rival.

The two heavyweights exchanged heated words during their face-off before lining up for one final set of photographs.

But when Hrgovic stepped in front of Itauma, the Brit shoved him forward, sending his opponent tumbling off the stage.

A furious Hrgovic immediately climbed back up and slapped Itauma, who then went berserk as both men attempted to fight before security rushed in to drag them apart.

The extraordinary scenes came just 24 hours before Itauma's first shot at becoming heavyweight world champion.

It was a notable change from the 21-year-old, who has remained largely calm throughout the build-up despite Hrgovic's repeated attempts to get under his skin.

Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic had to be pulled apart by security after their heavyweight weigh-in descended into chaos

Itauma started the chaos when he pushed Hrgovic off stage before his rival slapped him

Itauma had previously dismissed his rival's insults as 'schoolground banter', while Hrgovic has tried to provoke him at almost every opportunity during fight week.

The British heavyweight had even told his manager not to nibble at Hrgovic during Thursday's press conference, seemingly determined not to be drawn into any of the mind games.

But after keeping his composure throughout the week, it was Itauma himself who finally snapped at the weigh-in.

And while it offered a side to the unbeaten heavyweight that few have seen before, those watching appeared to love it.

Hrgovic was still furious when he spoke after the confrontation and vowed to 'smash' Itauma when the pair meet in the ring tomorrow night.

Itauma, meanwhile, admitted that he had been unable to resist the temptation to react.

'I had a scratch to itch and I had to do that today,' he said.

Sports.title: Red Bull to keep Dutch GP driver line-up for Monza with Hadjar still injured
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar will sit out this weekend's Italian Grand Prix at Monza as he recovers from a wrist injury he sustained during Formula 1's summer break. As a result, Liam Lawson will once again replace him at Red Bull and Yuki Tsunoda slots back into the Racing Bulls car.

Hadjar sustained a wrist fracturing during a boxing session during the summer break, forcing him to watch the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort from the sidelines on 21-23 August. Racing Bulls regular Lawson deputised for the Frenchman in the Red Bull RB22, with reserve driver Tsunoda being recalled to run Lawson's vacant VCARB 03 alongside rookie Arvid Lindblad.

Red Bull had been hopeful Hadjar would be ready for a return to competition at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, but also didn't want the 22-year-old to take any undue risk as he recovers from his injury.

Yuki Tsunoda, Racing Bulls Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

Both Red Bull-owned teams have now confirmed they will field unchanged driver line-ups in Monza.

"Liam will drive alongside Max at the Italian GP in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress," a Red Bull statement read. "The team is closely monitoring his rehabilitation and will take no unnecessary risks with his return to competition and wishes him a speedy recovery."

Both Lawson and Tsunoda impressed on their stand-in roles in the Netherlands, with Lawson guiding his Red Bull to seventh from eighth on the grid. Tsunoda just missed out on points in 11th, with both drivers sticking close to their respective team-mates on one-lap pace.

Meanwhile, the team's other reserve driver Ayumu Iwasa will replace Verstappen for opening practice, fulfilling one of the team's four mandated rookie sessions this season.

Sports.title: Ferrari to bring upgraded engine to Italian GP under ADUO
Sports.content:
Ferrari will introduce an upgrade to its Formula 1 power unit at this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix with it permitted under the Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities system.

This year, F1 introduced the ADUO system, which grants manufacturers extra opportunities to improve their engines should they be lagging behind on performance, with results taken every quarter of a season.

Red Bull was contentiously named as F1’s benchmark and because Ferrari is deemed to be over 4% adrift on power, the Italian marque is granted two upgrade tokens.

“We are introducing an updated power unit as part of the development opportunities available under ADUO,” said team boss Fred Vasseur.

“It represents a step in the right direction and as we know, this year is very much about marginal gains.

“Monza is a demanding circuit and the field is extremely close. Our priority will be to execute every aspect of the weekend as well as possible from Friday onwards.

“We want to draw extra motivation from the passion of our home crowd and give our tifosi a strong weekend.”

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

It is understood that the upgrade will add 15bhp to the Ferrari engine, and this will halve the deficit to the Mercedes power unit, which is believed to be the strongest complete package despite the ADUO results.

This is something that has held Ferrari back in 2026 considering its chassis is on a par, if not better, than that of the championship-leading Mercedes outfit, which leads the Scuderia by 87 points.

Ferrari is also set to run a Michael Schumacher-inspired livery this weekend to mark 30 years since the seven-time world champion made his debut at the squad with whom he won five titles.

“Monza is always a very special weekend for Ferrari,” added Vasseur, whose team is searching for its first Italian GP win since Charles Leclerc in 2024.

“Racing in front of our tifosi gives the whole team incredible energy and this year there will be an additional emotional dimension as we celebrate Michael Schumacher and the legacy he has left in our company.

“His relentless pursuit of improvement, attention to detail and strong belief in teamwork are values that remain key to us today.”

Sports.title: Red Bull signs key Aston Martin engineer as Lambiase replacement
Sports.content:
The Red Bull Formula 1 team has confirmed it has hired long-time Aston Martin engineer Tom McCullough to replace McLaren bound Gianpiero Lambiase as head of racing.

Lambiase will join McLaren in 2028 to become its chief racing officer, reporting into team principal Andrea Stella. The Briton is currently serving a dual role at the team as Max Verstappen's race engineer, dovetailing those duties with a more overarching "head of racing" position.

As previously reported, Verstappen's former performance engineer Tom Hart has decided against a move to Williams to take over the race engineer role starting in 2027. The Milton Keynes squad has now also found a successor for Lambiase as head of racing in the shape of Aston Martin man McCullough.

"We're delighted to welcome Tom to the team at the beginning of 2027 and look forward to the wealth of experience and expertise he will bring to the role," the team shared in a statement.

Gianpiero Lambiase is set to depart Red Bull by 2028 at the latest. Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

McCullough was a long-time servant of Aston Martin through its Force India and Racing Point days, performing the chief race engineer role for four seasons before becoming its performance director, a job which he held until the end of the 2024 season.

As part of a restructuring of the team in early 2025, McCullough's duties were taken on by previous team principal Mike Krack. McCullough was shifted to non-F1 projects at Aston Martin Performance Technologies in a senior leadership role, which he is now set to vacate.

The 50-year-old, who started his career at chassis builder Reynard, also served spells at Sauber and Williams.

Sports.title: McLaren to deliver rotating rear wing at Italian GP but calls it H-wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will introduce the H-Wing, its own version of the rotating rear wing, at this weekend's Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix.

McLaren had been working on its own interpretation of the rotating rear wing, which flips 180 degrees between cornering mode and straight mode, after seeing Ferrari introduce its own version during winter testing.

The Woking team first brought a prototype to the Austrian Grand Prix, but decided against trialling it in free practice after encountering an issue in the garage. It subsequently ran a revised example in Hungarian GP FP1 with a view to introducing it at low-drag, high-speed circuits later, when the concept should help reduce drag on the straights.

Monza is the first such opportunity, and McLaren has now committed to introducing the H-Wing on both cars.

The name for the device is not a Star Wars reference, but a nod to the letter H in the Etihad logo that adorns the rear of the MCL40's rear wing. The letter H runs along the centreline where the H-Wing's straight mode actuator is positioned.

McLaren's new wing features an innovative actuator Photo by: Marcel van Dorst / EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

It follows a tradition set by the team's famed F-duct in 2010, which was named after the F in Vodafone along the nose where the duct was installed.

"This weekend, we have brought what we believe is needed to be competitive, including a new low-drag rear wing specification, including the first use of our H-Wing, alongside some small aerodynamic and low-drag options that we will evaluate before deciding the final specification for qualifying," said McLaren's technical director Neil Houldey.

"Overall, we know there is still more performance to unlock from the MCL40, both through maximising the package we already have and through further upgrades planned for the races ahead.”

McLaren will also run a tweaked livery at Monza and at next week's Spanish Grand Prix to promote its partnership with cryptocurrency company OKX.

Sports.title: Haas rules out switch to 2027 development as VF-26 updates coming in Monza
Sports.content:
After starting the 2026 Formula 1 season strongly, Haas admits that it has been overtaken and out-developed by its rivals this year. However, team boss Ayao Komatsu and driver Oliver Bearman both remain hopeful that it can catch back up with the pack “soon”.

Haas has traditionally started the season strong, and continued this tradition in 2026 when it picked up points in the first three races – including a fifth-place finish for Bearman in the Chinese Grand Prix. However, as the season progressed, the team has been caught by its rivals as it struggles with an inconsistent car and a slower upgrade rate compared with midfield teams like Alpine and Racing Bulls.

“2025 was really the first year for us, or one of very few years, where we seemed to have good pace throughout the year,” Bearman explained ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix. “We actually improved our relative performance as the year went on.

“Now, 2026 is more of what we've seen from Haas in the past, of starting incredibly strong with a really quick car as a base, but not being able to improve like the others have.

“Quite frankly, we've been overtaken right now. We are the 10th-best team. It really hurts, myself and all the others. We were working really hard to make that not be the case, but that's the reality of where we are right now.”

Case in point, the team has not scored points since the Monaco Grand Prix in June when Esteban Ocon managed to bring his car home in ninth. Since then, the team has struggled with inconsistency – which has impacted its ability to extract the most from the 2026 car.

Ayao Komatsu says Haas will not pivot all its resources to 2027 just yet Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

However, team principal Komatsu is hopeful that Haas will soon be able to uncover solutions to the issues it is facing.

“So, the last two years, I think we proved to ourselves and the outside world that we can develop the car. We've got the people, the technical department is functioning,” Komatsu said ahead of the Zandvoort race.

“For us to have any remote chance of keeping up with the others, because of the size of our team, everything has to be perfect. But that's just not realistic in anyone's life. And the Montreal upgrade wasn't perfect. Some bits worked, some bits made the car faster, but some bits wasn't perfect. Actually, [it] made the drivability more difficult as well.

“So, we're learning from those lessons. And what's the objective for the rest of the season? For me, it's the same as the last two years. We've got to prove to ourselves that we can identify the key issues, we can solve the issues and then put it on the car to move forward.”

As a result of the struggles, Komatsu said he is now fielding questions about when Haas will give up on its 2026 challenger and switch focus to next year. This, Komatsu explained, is not an option for the team and it will instead work to unlock the performance of the VF-26 - a move that will benefit the team in the long run.

“If you say, OK, fine, ‘26, we started well, but tail off, it's the first year of regulation. Fine, let's move on, start '27. We haven't solved the fundamental issue. If we do that, it doesn't give confidence to people,” the Japanese engineer explained.

“They've got to believe in themselves. One of the main driving factors in the way they're tackling now, together as a team, is the confidence and togetherness they've gained from the last two years. That's why we are developing out of it.”

Oliver Bearman is hopeful that Haas will have an upgraded F1 car "soon" Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Haas will bring upgrades to Italian GP

To develop its way out of the problem, Haas will bring new parts to the VF-26, which the team confirmed would arrive this weekend in Monza for the Italian Grand Prix.

"This weekend, we’re bringing another upgrade package to the car," Komatsu explained in a statement shared by the team. "So again, it’s critical we maximise our practice time, evaluate our data comprehensively, and strive to keep pushing in the midfield."

However, despite the positives that these upgrades could bring, Bearman warned that new parts don't always equate to a jump forward on track.

“We have new parts coming,” the Briton said. “But we're very sceptical in some ways. We have discrepancies in a race like Budapest. We have discrepancies of downforce equivalent to the size of an upgrade. If I have the car that I had in Spa, here [in Zandvoort], it's like putting an upgrade on the car.

“An upgrade, I don't know how much it costs, but many millions. If we can figure out how to get our car to work, it's for free. If we get the upgrade but it doesn't perform, then it's like not getting it. There's many factors at play, it's a big challenge.”

Looking ahead to the next race in Italy, Bearman believes Haas could at least move a step up to be the ninth best team on the grid. Despite a radical overhaul of the Aston Martin AMR26 in recent weeks that has seen it jump off the back of the pack, the Briton says Haas should have an advantage over the British outfit in Monza.

“We expect to beat [Aston Martin] in Monza, where it's a power track,” Bearman said. “But in Hungary, they were faster than us, or at least more consistent. Those are the facts in terms of that. That's where we are.

“It really hurts to be sitting here saying that, but that's the case.”

Sports.title: How Ferrari can "push until the end" with F1 2026 upgrades, and why it will
Sports.content:
Ferrari will "push until the end" of the 2026 Formula 1 season with car upgrades, team principal Fred Vasseur confirmed, as he shrugged off suggestions the team will have to slow down its development because of cost cap limitations.

Ferrari has rolled out an impressive number of incremental upgrades to its 2026 challenger, the SF-26, which have kept the squad in second place in the constructors' championship and allowed Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc to clinch a grand prix win each thus far.

That upgrade push will continue at its home race this weekend in Monza, where Ferrari is expected to introduce smaller aerodynamic improvements alongside its second engine update following the latest ADUO ranking.

Read Also: Formula 1 Ferrari to deliver upgraded F1 engine at Italian GP

The field is becoming incredibly closely matched on performance, especially on circuits where the 2026 power units make less of a difference. Mercedes, McLaren and Ferrari were all covered by one tenth in sprint qualifying in Zandvoort, and three tenths has routinely become the difference between pole and the third row of the grid.

That's why teams who are able to continue bringing performance to the car until late on can still make a solid push in the championship, but they have to balance cashing in their wind tunnel development against the constraints of the cost cap and resources required for the 2027 car project.

Speaking exclusively to Autosport, Ferrari chief Vasseur has revealed the Scuderia will continue its relentless upgrade push, and it has no issues with the cost cap.

"The strategy is that we will continue to push until the end," Vasseur said. "We have a plan. We have no issue with the cost cap, we are following the plan and will continue like this.

Photo by: Marcel van Dorst / EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

"It's true that you have different strategies. You have McLaren coming each three or four races with a big package on the car, and we are more trying to bring upgrades each race but much smaller. But at the end, in terms of cost, it's the same.

"What is challenging, probably, is that we are still developing with 11 races to go, and I think a crash like Max [Verstappen] in Zandvoort is huge in terms of cost cap [for Red Bull]. It's difficult to anticipate the number of crashes that you could have until the end of the season."

While Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have all rolled out significant updates, Mercedes has been lagging behind, with its next major package coming at October's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, and it has seen its rival teams close the gap as a result in recent weeks and months.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff claimed the team "hasn't got the money to put developments on the car" beyond what is currently planned, but he did suspect the likes of Ferrari would have to slow down their rate of development given the number of items they had already introduced.

Read Also: Formula 1 McLaren rejects Mercedes claim it cannot afford aggressive upgrades in F1 2026

Vasseur didn't want to comment on Mercedes' upgrade strategy without fully understanding its approach, but he did lift the lid on how Ferrari has been able to bring so many improvements to the car efficiently, something that had raised eyebrows in the paddock.

"I don't want to speak about Mercedes because I don't understand, but with McLaren it's a bit linked to how you develop in the wind tunnel and the capacity of production," the Frenchman said.

"We found our best approach by almost bringing upgrades each race. One week it's mechanical, one week it's aero, and we are continuing like this. It's fitting with our capacity of production, with our wind tunnel capacity, and it's going well.

"Now, if McLaren want to do things differently, it's because they have good reasons to do it. The set-up of the teams is different; the configuration is different. But at the end of the day, over a season we are almost following each other in terms of development."

Sports.title: Mario Andretti and Jacky Ickx: A friendship that has endured for almost 60 years
Sports.content:
Mario Andretti and Jacky Ickx were remarkably versatile even by the standards of their generation, competing and succeeding across multiple disciplines. Having won some of the biggest prizes in motorsport between them, both can look back on their journeys with immense pride.

But competition was only one part of the story, and the relationship Andretti and Ickx built stands out from the rest in motor racing.

So, when the two joined Motorsport.com on a video call for a special double interview, it felt like two old friends had been reunited. The pair always got along well when they were team-mates at Ferrari in Formula 1 and the World SportsCar Championship. But it’s remarkable how, six decades after they first met at the Mexican Grand Prix in 1968, their admiration and affection for each other remain undimmed.

“You have to explain to me how you stay in such good condition, because you look good,” Ickx said of Andretti.

“I understand, yesterday you won [IndyCar’s Freedom 250] and you finished on the podium. You have many reasons to smile. We hope at Genesis to be like you.

“You are amazing, my dear Mario. It brings me some emotions to think that what we did more than almost 60 years ago - yes, almost 60 years ago.

“You are the most famous driver - the celebrated, the iconic Mario Andretti. I had the fortune to share with you, it was yesterday, I believe, 1972, in a Ferrari 312 PB. So thank you very much.”

Andretti, clearly touched by Ickx’s praise, simply replied: “No, thank you. You were the best.”

Endurance exploits ​brought them together

Jacky Ickx, Mario Andretti, Ferrari 312 PB Photo by: Rainer Schlegelmilch / Getty Images

When you see that kind of admiration from the pair, it’s easy to understand why they formed such a formidable pairing on track. It was in 1971 when they first shared a garage, teaming up at Ferrari for a double programme. Even as reliability held them back in F1, both scored a win each, with Andretti - who wasn’t even racing full-time - driving the 312B to victory on his debut outing for Enzo’s squad.

It was in sportscars, though, that their partnership really flourished. Their similar physical dimensions already made life easy for Ferrari’s designers, but it was ultimately mutual respect and understanding that turned them into such a formidable pair. Ickx, for instance, famously let Andretti qualify the car according to the American’s preference.

As a result, Ferrari dominated the 1972 season, with Andretti and Ickx winning four of the 11 races together, including Daytona, Sebring, Watkins Glen and Brands Hatch. Had Ferrari not skipped Le Mans after concluding its F1-derived engine wasn’t fit for a 24-hour contest (that year's Daytona race was reduced to six hours), the pair would most certainly have been among the victory contenders at the legendary La Sarthe.

Andretti admitted that sharing a car in endurance racing brought him and Ickx together, laying the foundation for a friendship that has lasted to this day.

“Long-distance racing taught me a lot,” he said. “You're sharing the moment with someone else to do the same thing.

“There's no bigger pleasure when you're in victory lane together with your partner. The ones that have accomplished the same thing for you - and with you.

“We all depend on each other to minimise the mistakes - and make no mistakes - to be able to bring it home.

“You're sharing your victory in a different way when you're driving in long-distance races. We're both in the same seat during the race at one time or another and we're both experiencing exactly the same thing. That's something that brings you together.

“Jacky, specifically, from the long-distance racing factor, I did most of my long-distance races with him. That's why I said he's my best buddy, my best team-mate.”

Still chasing the same goal

Jacky Ickx, Genesis Magma Racing Photo by: Genesis

Following his stint with Ferrari, Ickx went on to become one of the most successful names in sportscar racing history, winning Le Mans six times. He also triumphed in the Spa 24 Hours and Bathurst 1000 before turning his hand to rally raid and winning the Dakar Rally on his third attempt.

Andretti, likewise, accomplished almost everything he set out to achieve, winning marque races such as the Indy 500 and the Daytona 500 and claiming the championship in both Formula 1 and IndyCar.

Both may have long retired from active competition, but the passion for motorsport still burns brightly in their 80s. Andretti, besides being the patriarch of one of America’s biggest racing dynasties, works as a director for Cadillac’s new F1 team. Ickx, meanwhile, serves as a brand ambassador for Genesis Magma Racing, and recently sampled the GMR-001 at Paul Ricard.

Their lives may now be separated by geography - Andretti remains based in Pennsylvania while Ickx spends a significant amount of time in Africa - but the distance has done little to weaken their connection. If anything, they continue to follow each other’s careers and genuinely want to see the other succeed.

“I'll be watching with interest,” said Andretti. “I wish you guys all the very best. Whatever your endeavours are, maintain your objectives and always go for the sky.”

“I wish you to enjoy life in your projects,” Ickx adds. “We are in very good company. We are lucky to still be active, to be in good health.

“We are very lucky, Mario. I keep in mind these days the years we have shared together, where we have shared long-distance racing.

“Of course, I follow you in your championships, F1, IndyCar, NASCAR, Midget.”

Mario Andretti, Jacky Ickx, Ferrari 312 PB Photo by: David Phipps / Sutton Images via Getty Images

As the call drew to an end, both Andretti and Ickx bid each other goodbye. They could have spent the hour trading stories about their past glories, but instead, the conversation repeatedly returned to the time they had shared together on and off the track.

“You have been a real friend and such a talented driver,” concludes Ickx. “I was tempted to say I love you, but you're not supposed to say that.

“Mario, stay safe, please,” he adds. “Stay safe. And thank you very much for your friendship.”

Sports.title: The underlying upgrade that boosted McLaren's performance jump
Sports.content:
McLaren’s win in Zandvoort, their second in a row after Budapest, highlighted a key point: the updates introduced on either side of the summer break did more than restore the aerodynamic load the car had been missing. They also enabled the team to take a decisive step forward.

At the Barcelona Grand Prix, for instance, McLaren’s strengths had already begun to emerge, and the same was true at Spa, where the car appeared in its most convincing form. The faster and longer the corner, because absolute speed alone is not the sole factor, the more competitive the car becomes. The latest upgrades delivered the extra downforce required to turn the car into the benchmark through those sections.

The effectiveness of these developments surprised even McLaren, as the performance shown in the high‑speed sections exceeded internal expectations.

Yet another factor behind the Zandvoort victory went somewhat under the radar: the debut of the new front wheel rims, a detail that McLaren technical director of engineering Neil Houldey had already hinted at ahead of the weekend.

McLaren wheel cover comparison Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

“We introduced a small change to the rear section of the floor to generate a bit of extra load, along with some minor tweaks to the rear brake ducts. We also have new front wheel rims, which will help us build more temperature in the tyres. These updates are not significant in terms of lap time, but they do make us slightly more competitive”, Houldey said.

Why is this detail so interesting? After the race, team principal Andrea Stella noted that both Budapest and Zandvoort were high-downforce circuits that naturally suited the car's characteristics better than other tracks. However, looking back at Monaco, where the team hoped to fight at the front and repeat previous successes of last year, McLaren and struggled ended outside the podium positions.

The reason for those struggles went beyond cornering speeds and circuit characteristics. While Monte Carlo gives teams greater set-up freedom with fewer compromises, the car suffered from a lack of downforce and from difficulty generating temperature in the front tyres, which reduced overall grip. This limitation had already emerged earlier in the season, most notably in Australia and China, where the car experienced pronounced graining, while in Japan, where graining was not an issue and the new asphalt improved the overall grip, the MCL40 gained its first podium of the season.

One of the concerns heading into the Zandvoort weekend was the possibility of front‑axle graining, although it ultimately proved to be minimal for everyone. The real challenge was getting the tyres into the right temperature window, even over a single lap. That became clear in the final Q3 attempt on Saturday, when Lando Norris secured pole position, while other teams, struggled to bring the tyres up to temperature and needed an additional lap.

Aston Martin 2026 wheel comparison demonstrates a difference between the front and rear to manage temperatures Photo by: Gianluca D'Alessandro

This is where the topic connects with the updates introduced in the Netherlands. With wheel rim development open once again this season as part of the rule changes, teams have gained a powerful tool for managing tyre temperatures and operating pressures. The internal cavities of a custom rim design, that some teams call “pockets”, allow engineers to passively control air exchange and thermal transfer to the tyre.

At Zandvoort, McLaren focused specifically on this area to retain higher temperatures within the rim structure and, in turn, transfer that heat more effectively to the tyre. This is why only the front rim, manufactured by long‑standing partner Enkei, was updated, accompanied by a more closed wheel cover designed to limit the cooling effect of ambient airflow as it strikes the assembly and to reduce drag.

The rear rim remained unchanged because rear‑tyre degradation was already a key factor throughout the weekend, as seen during the sprint and the race. In that area of the car, the priority was to keep temperatures under control in the traction phases and the high‑speed sections rather than adding more heat. Strong gusts caused the cars to slide through the high‑speed corners, where additional downforce becomes critical, as well as through the key traction zones on the exit of the slower corners.

Sports.title: Hadjar to miss Italian Grand Prix, Lawson and Tsunoda continue as substitutes | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar will miss a second consecutive grand prix due to his wrist injury, Red Bull has confirmed.

As when Hadjar missed the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, Liam Lawson will take his place at Red Bull. Red Bull’s second team Racing Bulls confirmed Yuki Tsunoda will return for another round in place of Lawson.

“It’s good to hear Isack is recovering well and is back in the car soon, but it’s great to have another weekend with the team,” said Lawson, who finished seven in the Dutch Grand Prix.

“Zandvoort gave me a really useful first reference in the car, and having a full sprint [race] weekend behind me means I’m coming into Monza with a much better understanding of the car and what I need from it.”

Red Bull said Hadjar is making “encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break” over two weeks ago. The team added it “will take no unnecessary risks with his return to competition and wishes him a speedy recovery.”

Neither of Red Bull’s regular race drivers will appear in the first practice session at Monza. Ayumu Iwasa will drive Max Verstappen’s car as Red Bull completes one of its mandatory practice session runs for junior drivers.

Sports.title: ‘Dad was driving angry’: Jacques Villeneuve on his father Gilles’ fatal crash | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Jacques Villeneuve said he was close to tears as he watched footage from a new movie on the life of his father Gilles.

“Villeneuve: Rise of a Legend” (trailer below) will have its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 19th. The film tells the story of the future F1 driver’s early racing exploits, leading up to his hiring by Enzo Ferrari.

“Watching the trailer, it was difficult to hold back the tears,” said Villeneuve, who won the world championship in 1997.

“I love that it focuses on the early years, the years no one but our family knows about. Most biopics focus on when someone’s in their prime, and they tend to rush through or gloss over how they got there. They give the audience what they already know, whereas this film shows the building blocks.”

Jacques was 11 when his father died in a crash during qualifying for the 1982 Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder. He had fallen out with his Ferrari team mate Didier Pironi two weeks earlier, believing the team had issued orders for them to hold position with Villeneuve leading.

The 1997 world champion now has seven children of his own and has explained the circumstances of their grandfather’s death to them.

“Our four-year-old, Gilles, is really into racing,” he said. “He’s the same age I was when I first believed I would become a racing driver.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’s always difficult to know, but it seems to be inside him. He relates a lot to his grandad. He knows the full story. He understands his grandad passed away because he was racing angry.

“He understands death. It’s important, I think, to be able to handle these things so you don’t have a big shock when you’re 60 or something.”

Villeneuve said he managed the risks of racing more successfully than his father did. “I’ve never really raced angry, but my upbringing was different to my dad’s,” he said. “The fact that I was in boarding school and ski-raced a lot meant I paid the price very quickly when I made a mistake.

“I’m able to calculate risk better than he did. I know the risk-to-reward ratios. When I was racing in F1 there weren’t many crazy drivers anymore, which made me look a little bit crazier than I actually was.

“But this thing about driving angry, it’s something I’ve come to understand much more recently. In part, that’s the result of talking to guys like Alain Prost, guys that raced against my dad. They have so many amazing stories, and it’s given me a different picture of who my dad was and the situation he was in. It’s helped me connect some dots.”

He described watching some of his father’s most famous races, including some of his six grand prix victories.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I was there when he won the 1978 Canadian Grand Prix. I was on the podium with my grandparents, and I was wearing a winter ski coat because it was freezing.

“I remember when he won the [1981] Monaco Grand Prix. I was sitting in the grandstand by the swimming pool with my grandparents. I remember talking to myself: ‘Come on, you’ve got to win this…’

“I remember Dijon [Villeneuve’s famous battle with Rene Arnoux during the 1979 French Grand Prix]; I was watching that on TV at a house just outside the track.

“I also have a vivid memory of sitting in the Bosch Kurve grandstand at the Osterreichring in Austria. I could be left alone in the grandstand all day just watching the cars drive by.”

However he was not at Zolder on the weekend his father was killed. “At that point we didn’t go to races anymore,” he said. “We’d moved to Monaco and we were really lagging behind at school.”

“My mother hadn’t gone to that race either. I remember walking back from school, getting home and then the phone ringing and my mother picking up. It was a very emotional moment.”

Sports.title: Temple of Speed or Cathedral of Clipping? Eight talking points for the 2026 Italian GP | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Will Formula 1’s new engines ruin Monza’s high-speed spectacle? Will Isack Hadjar return? Eight talking points for this weekend’s race.

Cathedral of Clipping?

Formula 1’s disastrous 2026 regulations have left its cars with power units which are woefully inadequate for the challenge of racing on the world’s fastest and most demanding circuits.

Those in F1 prefer language which lays the blame for the series’ current predicament more on the venues than the regulations. “Monza is an energy-poor track,” Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff noted in their pre-event press release, “you spend much of the lap asking everything from the power unit and don’t have many opportunities to charge the battery.”

Whether you blame a circuit which has stood for over a century or the FIA’s rules governing the new cars which race on it, the fact remains Monza will be the most extreme challenge for the latest generation of cars. The FIA has set the lowest harvesting limits of the season in a bid to reduce the notorious ‘super-clipping’ and drivers will have few chances to deploy energy around the lap. The ‘Temple of Speed’

Expect to see a lot of ‘towing’ in qualifying. Don’t expect to hear much from F1 Italian CEO Stefano Domenicali about the problem as he gazes across the stadiums packed with fans, most of which likely purchased their tickets long before the 2026 cars hit the track, and tells himself they don’t know or understand what ‘clipping’ is.

Ukraine’s appeal over FIA’s boost to Russia

The FIA’s sudden decision to soften its stance on Russia in the wake of its invasion of Ukraine will be challenged in its own Court of Appeal. F1 drivers previously spoke out against the war when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, but since then the FIA has tightened its rules on drivers making political statements.

Is the Formula 1 paddock happy with the FIA’s decision to help Russia burnish its reputation while it continues to kill Ukrainians and is accused of targeting other European nations?

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ferrari or Antonelli?

Andrea Kimi Antonelli arrives at Monza with a 59-point lead over Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton. So who will get the loudest cheers?

It goes without saying that huge portions of the Italian crowd will be hoping for a Ferrari victory. But will the fans at Monza also take Italy’s new driving talent to heart – particularly now he’s in such a strong position in the championship?

Penalty gives opportunity to Antonelli’s rivals

Antonelli’s hopes of becoming the first Italian to win the Italian Grand Prix in 60 years have already suffered a blow as he will have to change his power unit this weekend, meaning he will start closer to the back.

That hands a useful opportunity to Hamilton as well as George Russell, who is also 59 points adrift.

McLaren ready rear wing upgrade

Another driver hoping to make inroads into Antonelli’s points lead is Lando Norris, the winner of the last two grands prix. He lies 83 points behind the Mercedes driver.

The good news for Norris is McLaren intend to race their new rear wing configuration, which it calls the ‘H-wing’ in reference to a sponsor.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ferrari’s ADUO engine boost

Ferrari are expected to introduce their latest engine specification this weekend. The upgrade is allowed under F1’s new Additional Development Upgrade Opportunity regulations which are intended to balance the performance between the combustion engines.

With another high-speed circuit (sorry, ‘energy-poor track’) coming in three weeks’ time, it could prove a well-timed boost for Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

Will Hadjar be back?

At the time of writing, Red Bull are yet to confirm whether Isack Hadjar will return to action this weekend following the wrist injury which prevented him from competing at Zandvoort.

Red Bull can hardly fault the job Liam Lawson did as his stand-in two weeks ago and it would be a surprise if they turned to anyone else. This would likely mean another call-up for Yuki Tsunoda to replace him at Racing Bulls: the team has tested Red Bull Junior Team member Nikola Tsolov since the last race but the Formula 2 championship leader does not have enough superlicence points to race in F1.

Update: Hadjar to miss Italian Grand Prix, Lawson and Tsunoda continue as substitutes

Will Hadjar get his podium back

Hadjar is also waiting to learn whether he will regain the third-place finish he scored in Monaco. The FIA Court of Appeal met after Zandvoort to hear Red Bull and McLaren’s arguments against the stewards’ decision to cancel Pierre Gasly’s two pit lane speeding penalties but a decision may yet take days or even weeks to emerge.

Sports.title: On This Day: Collins hands his car – and the championship – to Fangio | Brief
Sports.content:
70 years ago today Peter Collins surrendered his car to team mate and championship rival Juan Manuel Fangio during the Italian Grand Prix, in a remarkable gesture which ensured Fangio beat him to the 1956 world championship.

The Ferrari pair went into the final race of the season with Fangio on 30 points, eight ahead of Collins, who was tied with Maserati’s Jean Behra. Fangio’s steering arm broke 19 laps into the race and Luigi Musso, in another Ferrari, refused to hand his car to his team mate (as he had at the season-opener in Argentina).

Collins was running third when he pitted on lap 36, saw Fangio’s predicament, and handed over his car. Had Collins continued, with both Musso and Stirling Moss hitting trouble later in the race, he likely would have won it and beaten Fangio to the title.

Instead he and Fangio shared second place in the race and the latter took the title by three points from Moss. Fangio went on to win a fifth world title the following year, though Collins was killed in a crash in 1958.

Sports.title: Ukraine appeals to FIA Court of Appeal over lifting of Russia ban | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Ukrainian Automobile Federation is reportedly appealing against the FIA’s decision to reverse its ban on Russians competing in motorsport and displaying their flag at its events.

The federation is bringing an appeal to the FIA Court of Appeal over the U-turn.

The FIA’s decision came into effect on August 3rd, though the governing body did not announce it for another 10 days. The federation formally objected to the decision three days later and subsequently requested the FIA’s ethics committee.

The governing body originally announced the ban, which also applies to Belarussia, in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The war continues and the FIA’s announcement of its decision did not give any reasons for its change.

Until 2022, Russian racer Nikita Mazepin competed in Formula 1 and his father’s company sponsored Haas, which ran in Russian colours. F1 also held a race in Russia, at Sochi Autodrom, from 2014 to 2021. F1 cancelled its contract in response to the invasion and the FIA has not relaxed its ban on events taking place in Russia or Belarussia.

In 2023, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said he had opposed taking action against Russia over the war. The BBC reported Ben Sulayem proposed relaxing the ban on Russian participation in motorsport, and stated the FIA said its decision followed a similar announcement by the International Olympic Committee in July.

The Ukrainian Automobile Federation is challenging the FIA’s decision as it claims the Russian Automobile Federation is operating offices in parts of Ukraine which Russia has invaded, in Sevastopol, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia. The federation’s website prominently displays names of its members who have been killed in the war since it began.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Admits Early Success Cost Him Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
“I felt a bit too comfortable maybe with the really early knockdown, then followed by another one in the third,” Wardley said during the kick-off press conference. “I thought this is near on a foregone conclusion. I’ve done it once, I’ve done it twice, I can get him out of there. “I was a victim of my own success in them early stages. I just got trigger-happy, got carried away with trying to launch that right hand. In the moments when I did have him hurt, I don’t actually think I jumped on him enough.”

The mistake was not simply failing to throw enough punches. Wardley stopped disguising the right hand and began loading up from too far away. Dubois steadied himself behind a stiff jab, controlled the distance, and forced him to expend more energy each time he attempted to close the space.

The challenger needs greater variety in London. Hooks to the ribs would give Dubois something else to consider behind his tight guard, while doubling the lead hook may create a cleaner route for Wardley’s power. Hunting for one spectacular shot only makes his attack easier to read.

Pacing will be just as important. An early knockdown does not require an immediate all-out assault, particularly in a fight scheduled for 12 rounds. Wardley must allow his successes to count on the scorecards without emptying his energy reserves in search of a dramatic finish.

The five-month turnaround adds another concern. Wardley absorbed sustained punishment before the 11th-round stoppage and has gone directly into another demanding camp without an interim bout. He dismissed questions about his condition, saying he had “absolutely zero excuses” for the defeat or the rematch.

Dubois carries the psychological advantage. He knows he can withstand Wardley’s heaviest punches, regain command with his jab, and break him down over the later rounds. The harder mental test for Wardley may arrive if he lands cleanly again and the champion refuses to fold.

The first fight established that Wardley can hurt Dubois. On October 17, he must show that early success will sharpen his decisions instead of distorting them.

Sports.title: Janibek Corners Hamzah Sheeraz Before WBO Deadline
Sports.content:
Sheeraz has already built a possible defense for refusing the fight. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, he called the WBO’s ruling a “joke” and criticized the organization for rewarding Janibek after his positive test for meldonium.

The clean-sport objection has merit. The WBO shortened Janibek’s suspension, allowed him to move directly into a mandatory position at 168 pounds, and selected him over Jacob Bank despite Janibek never fighting in the division. Bank had actively campaigned at super middleweight and petitioned for the same opportunity.

Still, Sheeraz’s moral position also provides a convenient exit. He can vacate while claiming he refused to cooperate with a sanctioning body order he considers disgraceful, rather than admitting that Janibek presents too much danger for too little money.

Surrendering the title would harm Sheeraz’s reputation. He won the vacant belt against 39-year-old Alem Begic and struggled through a majority verdict over Simon Zachenhuber in his first defense. Leaving before facing Janibek would support the Kazakh’s claim that Sheeraz was only a “champion by name.”

Facing Janibek carries the greater career risk. He is a precise southpaw counterpuncher with the power to punish the defensive lapses Sheeraz showed against Zachenhuber. A decisive loss would cost Sheeraz his belt and reduce his value for larger fights against Canelo Alvarez or Chris Eubank Jr.

The history makes an escape harder to disguise. Sheeraz withdrew from negotiations when the WBO ordered him to challenge Janibek at middleweight. After Sheeraz moved to 168 and became champion, Janibek followed him into the division.

Vacating can be presented as a principled business choice. Getting stopped by the opponent who pursued him through two weight classes would be far worse. Janibek has left Sheeraz to choose which consequence he is willing to accept.

Sports.title: Two Minutes in Tokyo: George Foreman Slaughters José Roman
Sports.content:
Roman had little chance of testing him. The Puerto Rican challenger stood 5-foot-10 and weighed between 196½ and 197 pounds, leaving him considerably smaller than the 6-foot-4, 219-pound champion. He had been outside the rankings when the fight was signed before being elevated to No. 9 by the WBA and WBC.

That placement gave the promotion official legitimacy, but it did not make Roman a genuine threat. Foreman was 38-0 with 35 knockouts and had just destroyed Frazier in two rounds to seize the championship. Roman brought a 43-7-1 or 44-7-1 record, depending on the source, with 21 knockouts.

Once the bell rang, even two minutes proved too long.

Foreman did not merely follow Roman and swing wildly. Under trainer Dick Sadler, he had learned to take broad lateral steps that closed escape routes. His lead hand served as more than a jab. He posted it against Roman, pushed him off balance, and turned him toward the right hand.

That rough leverage helped Foreman control opponents before the power punches landed. Some of it crossed into boxing’s gray area, particularly when he shoved or extended his lead arm, but Roman lacked the strength and composure to resist it.

The destruction of Frazier also followed Foreman into the ring. Roman knew that six knockdowns had reduced the previous champion to a helpless target. His tense movement and reluctance to commit gave Foreman little reason to respect anything coming back.

Foreman cut down the available space, drove Roman toward the ropes, and attacked his body. Roman fell along the ropes near the one-minute point, but referee Jay Edson initially treated it as a slip or loss of balance rather than a knockdown.

The decision became controversial when Foreman landed a right while Roman was sitting on the canvas. Roman’s manager, Bill Daly, and trainer, Al Braverman, jumped onto the apron demanding a disqualification. Edson ruled that Foreman had been following through and that the punch carried little force. Because the original fall was ruled a slip, Roman received neither a mandatory count nor additional recovery time.

The challenger rose, only to be dropped by a right hand. Roman made it up once more, but Foreman finished him with a right uppercut at exactly 2:00 of the opening round. Roman’s corner later called Foreman “the dirtiest fighter in the world,” while some members of the Tokyo crowd booed the abrupt ending.

Roman’s ranking exposed the business behind the defense. He was outside the WBA and WBC ratings when the fight was arranged, then elevated to No. 9 so the organizations could approve him as a challenger. The placement did not make him a mandatory contender or establish championship credentials. It allowed an overseas title defense to proceed against an opponent selected for limited risk.

Promoters advertised Foreman’s purse as $1 million, a figure that became attached to the fight in later records. Contemporary reporting placed his actual guarantee near $250,000, while other accounts and Foreman’s later recollections put his earnings in the $250,000 to $300,000 range. Roman received approximately $100,000.

Attendance reached roughly 7,500 to 8,000 in an arena capable of holding nearly twice that number. The midday Saturday scheduling and expensive tickets hurt local sales, leaving Japanese promoters braced for a financial loss despite televising the bout free to domestic viewers.

Foreman followed the Roman destruction by stopping Ken Norton in two rounds the next year. Across the Frazier, Roman, and Norton fights, he needed only five rounds to dispose of three heavyweights who had a combined 91 professional victories.

The two-minute result also concealed a flaw that Muhammad Ali later exploited. Foreman committed heavily to his power punches and expected resistance to collapse under the first sustained attack. Roman rewarded that approach by folding almost immediately.

Ali refused to provide the same response in Zaire the following year. He forced Foreman to keep punching after the quick finish failed to materialize, turning the champion’s aggression and confidence in his strength into an exhausting trap.

Foreman’s comeback decades later produced one of boxing’s greatest stories, capped by the heavyweight championship at age 45. Yet the older Foreman relied more on patience, positioning, and conservation. The 1973 version brought something more frightening: youth, crushing strength, and an appetite for immediate destruction.

Roman was never equipped to disprove it.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says Crawford Resents His Boxing Takeover
Sports.content:
“I gave my honest opinion, saying that he left a lot on the table. That’s all I said. Crawford is the one that’s always coming up and slightly hating on me little by little. In the meantime, you’re retired. You should be in Turks and Caicos chilling on a yacht, enjoying your family. He’s desperate, bro,” said Ryan to Fight Hub TV. “Nobody knows him outside of boxing, so he’s doing everything he can to continue his name. He actually likes the attention. I used to think Crawford didn’t, but now I know he does. He realized nobody cares after you retire.”

Ryan also dismissed Crawford’s presence at Benn’s gym. “I feel like I’ll beat your ass, so what are you going to teach him?” he said.

Their bad blood highlights the fundamental difference between the two men. Crawford pursued championships, pound-for-pound recognition, and technical supremacy. Garcia measures his position through audience size, financial leverage, and the ability to command boxing’s most valuable dates.

Crawford built the greater traditional legacy, but Ryan attracts the larger mainstream audience. If Garcia defeats Benn and becomes boxing’s leading commercial figure, he will have achieved something Crawford never managed despite accomplishing far more inside the ring.

Working with Benn does not necessarily prove Garcia’s accusation that Crawford craves attention. It may represent a retired fighter transferring his knowledge to another contender. Garcia has turned that mentorship into an insult, reducing Benn to a pupil who cannot be saved even by one of boxing’s finest technicians.

That approach also keeps Benn’s abilities outside the discussion. By treating the fight as a proxy battle with Crawford, Garcia portrays him as little more than the vehicle for another man’s resentment.

The claim brings considerable risk. Garcia’s argument carries force only if he beats Benn. A loss would damage his attempt to place drawing power above championships while giving Crawford every reason to question both his boxing and his self-appointed status.

The message was simple: Crawford had his run and should either return to face someone such as Jaron Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr. or stay quiet in retirement.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Faces Duty as Oleksandr Usyk Exits
Sports.content:
The champion would naturally prefer a larger fight. Revenge against Dubois carries commercial value after Hrgovic’s stoppage loss to him in 2024, while a unification would pay considerably more than defending against Sanchez. The IBF mandate leaves little room for shopping around unless Sanchez accepts another step-aside agreement.

Dubois first has his own business to settle. He defends the WBO title against Fabio Wardley in their October 17 rematch at London’s O2 Arena. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May meeting, but the punishment he absorbed makes the return dangerous. Hrgovic cannot build his plans around Dubois retaining.

Oleksandr Usyk is operating outside that championship traffic. The former unified champion is targeting Deontay Wilder for a final fight in the United States in 2027. It offers Usyk one more famous name, but little clarity about the division’s best heavyweight.

Usyk struggled more than anticipated against boxing novice Rico Verhoeven in May. He trailed on one scorecard and was level on the other two before producing an 11th-round stoppage. Wilder also carries the wear of a long career and no longer releases his right hand with the conviction that once made him boxing’s most feared puncher. Their proposed fight sells history and name recognition rather than determining the division’s leader.

The active championship race now belongs to Hrgovic, Dubois, WBA champion Murat Gassiev, and WBC interim champion Agit Kabayel. Gassiev stopped Peter Kadiru in six rounds in July, while Kabayel demolished Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. A Gassiev-Kabayel unification would immediately reduce the number of competing titleholders.

Hrgovic wants access to those lucrative fights, but Sanchez remains positioned directly in front of him. Beating Itauma won Hrgovic the belt. Defeating his mandatory would prove that he can keep it.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Waits for the Winner of Canelo-Mbilli
Sports.content:
Martinez was much more effective and landed the harder punches. Lester had the support of the Guatemalan people with a healthy attendance of 6,848 at the USC Galen Center. The interim WBC super middleweight champion is the only boxing champion of any kind for Guatemala; Martinez is held in high esteem, receiving the full support of his country. After the victory, he celebrated at Lafayette Park at the Festival Chapin with his fellow countrymen.

ProBox promoter Garry Jonas stated at the post-fight press conference they’re exploring the options of holding a Lester Martinez fight at a soccer stadium somewhere in Guatemala, hopefully for January of 2027. The energy and crowd at the Galen Center was electrifying as the crowd would erupt in cheers every time Lester would land a big punch.

Holding an event in Guatemala would definitely draw a crowd. Lester is becoming a bigger star with every fight, and if he’s able to secure a fight with the winner of the Canelo Alvarez-Christian Mbilli fight, he would only become that much bigger. Trainer Esau Dieguez said of the fight, “The truth is we would like to face the winner, but because of name recognition and what it would bring, we would like to fight Canelo. Being that we already fought Mbilli, but I expect Canelo to win. I think Canelo will win, I hope we can make the fight. I know the WBC may beat around the bush, but our hope is Lester will fight for the full world title.”

It was the fight against Mbilli that raised Lester’s profile and introduced him to the world. Although it was ruled a draw, there are many who believe Martinez should have been awarded the decision. Lester stood toe-to-toe with the power puncher, exchanging punch for punch with him. Martinez outlanded Mbilli 412 to 273 in total punches, outlanding him in 9 of 12 rounds (Compubox).

He tried securing the rematch with Christian, but the fight never materialized. Expecting a tough fight against the Canelo-Mbilli winner, Lester said, “I think for now I will relax, but I know what is coming will be more difficult, and we will prepare for it.”

Knowing that he will have to perform at his absolute best against whomever the winner may be. Lester has proven he has the skills to compete at the championship level, and he has the full support of an entire country with him in Guatemala; they want nothing more than to have their first full world champion.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Questions Daniel Dubois’ Sudden Attitude
Sports.content:
“It’s way too early for all of this. Last time I saw him, we shook hands. We congratulated each other on a great fight. I lost and took it on the chin, but then he turned up with a bit of attitude. I was like, ‘Hang on, what’s going on here?’ But if that’s what he needs to do to get himself geared up for another fight, if you know what war you went through last time, if that’s what he’s got to do to get himself in the right frame of mind, then be my guest. I’m just going to stay cool as a cucumber,” Wardley said to DAZN.

Confidence comes partly from Wardley’s two fights with Frazer Clarke. Their first meeting ended in a draw after 12 exhausting rounds, but he changed his approach and demolished Clarke in the opening round of their second encounter.

That comparison also exposes the danger in Wardley’s thinking. An explosive start solved the Clarke puzzle, but it contributed to his defeat against Dubois. After dropping Dubois twice, Wardley burned through his energy trying to force the stoppage. His output and defensive discipline declined as the rounds passed, allowing Dubois to take control with his jab before finishing an exhausted opponent.

Those knockdowns also demonstrated that hurting Dubois does not guarantee he will unravel. He used the jab to regain his balance, interrupt Wardley’s attacks, and buy the recovery time needed to survive the crisis. Clarke never received that opportunity in his rematch.

A different result will require more than another fast start. Wardley must shorten his right hand, recover his guard after throwing it, and resist loading up during pocket exchanges. His eagerness to finish left his head exposed to Dubois’ counters throughout their first fight.

The decisive adjustment will be psychological as much as technical. Wardley cannot allow two knockdowns, another roaring crowd, or Dubois showing vulnerability to convince him the fight is already won. Remaining “cool as a cucumber” during a face-off is easy. Maintaining that restraint after hurting Dubois will determine if the rematch produces a different result.

Sports.title: Hrgovic Shows Why Joe Joyce Keeps Fighting
Sports.content:
Hrgovic reversed the result as a professional in April 2025, winning a 10-round unanimous decision. The Croatian has since stopped Moses Itauma in the ninth round to capture the vacant IBF belt, showing how quickly one major result can transform an aging heavyweight’s career.

That example may reinforce Joyce’s belief that he can do something similar. If he survives an early attack and overwhelms a recognizable opponent late, one fortunate result might return him to contention. The immediate difficulty is finding that fight. Five defeats in six appearances leave promoters with little reason to offer him a major name without a rebuilding win first.

His former intimidation has also disappeared. Joyce’s pressure once forced opponents to expend energy while backing away because they doubted they could hurt him. Zhilei Zhang broke that psychological advantage by stopping him twice. Suslenkov then held his ground, committed to power punches, and treated Joyce as a target who could be hurt rather than an advancing force who had to be escaped.

As a result, the style Joyce used during his best professional years no longer works the same way. He was never difficult to hit, but his punch resistance allowed him to accept clean shots while exhausting opponents with his jab, size, and output. Once rivals stop fearing that exchange, his slow entries give them repeated chances to load up before he reaches punching range.

Excess weight has become another obstacle. Joyce scaled 255 pounds for his professional debut against Ian Lewison in 2017, already looking slower than he had during his amateur years. He reached a career-high 289 for July’s stoppage loss to Artem Suslenkov.

For comparison, Hrgovic arrived lighter against Itauma. Under Abel Sanchez, he dropped from 248¼ pounds against David Allen to 236¼. He looked more agile and preserved enough energy to take control after Itauma exhausted himself.

He may need to work gradually toward the 260-pound range as a starting point before SugarHill Steward can determine how much mobility and sustained output remain.

His recent record also changes how promoters will view him. A 40-year-old who has lost five of six is more likely to be offered as a test for a younger heavyweight than positioned for his own title run. Accepting that role may produce another recognizable fight, but Joyce would enter as the opponent rather than the investment. His best chance of changing that calculation is to return lighter and defeat a domestic name before another prospect’s team comes calling.

Shedding weight cannot make Joyce young again. It can remove an unnecessary burden and give him a better chance of earning the type of opening Hrgovic just seized.

Ghana News.title: Food vendor recounts how she narrowly escaped New Winneba attack
Ghana News.content:
A beans seller at New Ateitu near New Winneba in the Central Region, Rebecca Kukua, has recounted how she narrowly escaped an attack that has left residents fleeing the community for fear of their lives.

According to her, the attack has created widespread panic among residents, with many abandoning their homes and leaving the once-busy community largely deserted.

Speaking in an interview with Adom News, Ms Kukua described the situation as worrying, saying New Ateitu has virtually become a ghost town following the violence.

She appealed to the security agencies to intensify their presence in the area and take urgent steps to restore calm to enable residents to safely return to their homes.

The incident occurred on Tuesday when a group, reportedly from Gomoa Oguakrom, Gomoa Yenkuadze and Gomoa Pomadze, attacked residents and allegedly vandalised shops and properties belonging to natives of the area.

The violence reportedly left at least three people dead, while about 15 injured persons, including a police officer, were transported to the Trauma and Specialist Hospital in Winneba for treatment.

Following the attack, police personnel from the Winneba Divisional Headquarters and Agona Swedru District Patrols were deployed to contain the situation and restore calm.

The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) subsequently deployed a reinforcement team from the National Police Headquarters, including two armoured vehicles, to strengthen security in the area.

Ghana News.title: Military to secure James Town after massive waste evacuation – Ayariga
Ghana News.content:
The military is expected to take charge of security at James Town following a planned government operation to evacuate the huge volumes of waste accumulated in the area.

Local Government Minister Ahmed Ibrahim Ayariga says the military will secure the cleared site to prevent residents from returning to dump waste and to stop squatters from occupying the land.

He said the measure is intended to ensure that the government’s cleanup exercise is not undermined by renewed illegal dumping or unplanned settlements.

“After we've moved it out of the James Town area, the military will take responsibility for protecting that area and making sure that we don't bring back waste and also squatters don't stay on the land that we have cleared and create a mess again for us,” he said. The Minister was speaking during a tour of waste management facilities as part of efforts to assess the country's waste management challenges and identify sustainable solutions.

This comes as the government is preparing a major operation to evacuate the huge volumes of accumulated waste from James Town in Accra to the Adipa Waste Management Centre, an engineered landfill facility at Nsawam in the Eastern Region, with the military expected to play a key role in securing the area after the cleanup.

The operation will bring together the Ministries of Local Government, Defence, Roads and Highways, and Finance as authorities work to determine the logistical requirements for clearing the waste.

Local Government Minister said officials are currently assessing the volume of waste, the distance to designated landfill sites and the capacity of available trucks to determine the number of trips and the amount of fuel required.

He said the government is also working to ensure that the waste removed from James Town has suitable receiving sites.

Mr Ayariga said the government is also considering broader plans for the redevelopment of the James Town area once the waste has been removed.

The Ministry of Finance is expected to play a role in financing the operation and supporting plans for the redevelopment of the site.

The government says the exercise is part of efforts to address persistent sanitation challenges in the capital and prevent cleared areas from becoming dumping grounds again.

Ghana News.title: Charlie Kirk murder suspect pleads not guilty as judge clears way for death penalty trial
Ghana News.content:
A 23-year-old Utah man has pleaded not guilty to the murder of conservative activist Charlie Kirk – as a judge ruled prosecutors can seek the death penalty at trial.

Tyler Robinson denies aggravated murder, a capital offence in Utah, and six other charges in connection with the shooting of Kirk at a campus event on September 10, 2025.

Defence lawyers had tried to have the death penalty taken off the table, but prosecutors argued that aggravating factors, such as firing into a crowd in the presence of children, warranted a capital trial.

Turning Point USA co-founder Kirk, 31, was shot in the neck while speaking at Utah Valley University in Orem.

The defendant, wearing a grey suit and occasionally consulting with his lawyers, appeared in court in the city of Provo on Tuesday.

Kirk's widow, Erika, the mother of their two children, and his parents, ⁠Robert and Kathryn, were also at the hearing.

In a statement shared afterwards, the Kirk family said the judge's decision "marks an important step" in their "pursuit of justice".

"Every step in this process carries the weight of all that Charlie's murder has taken from his family, especially his children who will grow up without their father," the statement added.

Closing arguments followed a five-day preliminary hearing in July, during which prosecutors outlined their evidence to show probable cause for trial.

That included DNA allegedly tying Robinson to the murder weapon and other items recovered at the scene; confessions he allegedly made to loved ones; and a taped video statement from his roommate and romantic partner, Lance Twiggs.

"There is a mountain of evidence that proves that he is the shooter," prosecutor Ryan McBride told the court on Tuesday, outlining video that he said showed Robinson "dressed to kill" on campus on the day of the shooting.

"We know that the defendant is the shooter… first, because of the video evidence; second, because of the DNA; third, because of his admissions; and fourth, because of circumstantial evidence," McBride said.

Prosecutors said the accused, a former apprentice electrician, was in a relationship with his roommate and regarded Kirk's conservative views, particularly on transgender issues, as "repugnant" - which they argued was the motive.

On Tuesday, prosecutors also outlined "aggravating" factors - accusing the defendant of "gambling with the lives of others" when he allegedly fired towards Kirk, who was surrounded by other people.

"He was playing, in effect, a game of ballistic roulette," prosecutor Chad Grunander said.

"It's been 356 days since Tyler Robinson assassinated Charlie Kirk," Grunander added. "It's time for him, the defendant, to be bound over for trial and arraigned. Today."

Defence lawyers attempted to sow doubt about the prosecution's evidence.

During July's hearing, they raised questions about procedure and the credentials of experts who testified. Robinson's lawyers have repeatedly objected to cameras livestreaming court proceedings.

Judge Tony Graf again listened to arguments on the issue during a sealed hearing on Tuesday morning before closing arguments began - but he ruled in favour of transparency in a case that has sparked conspiracy theories.

On Tuesday, the defence sought to downplay the aggravating factors outlined by prosecutors - arguing that no bullets hit anyone in the crowd apart from Kirk.

The court heard and saw during July's hearing how the accused allegedly scouted the campus repeatedly on the day Kirk was shot - interacting with TPUSA members and eating Chick-fil-A before returning in different clothes.

The new outfit included "long pants to obscure the rifle he had concealed down his pants", McBride said on Tuesday.

According to prosecutors' evidence presented during the July hearing, Robinson's DNA was found on his grandfather's rifle stashed in a wooden area near campus after the shooting, as well as on a towel it was wrapped in and a screwdriver recovered at the scene.

McBride also told the court on Tuesday that engravings found on casings from the shooting allegedly matched a Dremel tool recovered at the home the defendant shared with his roommate.

Twiggs' videotaped interview with prosecutors was played in July during the hearing. Robinson's roommate testified that the defendant had confessed to the shooting, cried and said he wished he hadn't done it.

Robinson, in the company of his family and a neighbour, turned himself in the day after the murder.

He is next due in court on October 23, when a trial date is expected to be set.

Ghana News.title: Signals Bureau case: ‘We were battle-ready’ – Atta Akyea fires at AG over absence of prosecution team
Ghana News.content:
Counsel for former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene, Samuel Atta Akyea, has criticised the Attorney-General’s Office after the prosecution team failed to appear in court to continue cross-examination.

The case was adjourned to September 8 after the prosecution was unable to proceed with the cross-examination.

The development comes a day after Mr Atta Akyea had expressed enthusiasm about an additional day granted by the Accra High Court to allow him to further cross-examine the fourth prosecution witness.

He had indicated that he had about 60 questions prepared for the witness but would reduce them to 40 following a three-hour limit imposed by the court.

According to the lawyer, the extra day was necessary to ensure that all relevant areas of the witness’s testimony were adequately covered.

However, appearing in court on Wednesday, September 2, Mr Atta Akyea said he was surprised that no representative from the Attorney-General’s Office was available to continue the proceedings.

“I was surprised that no single human being from the Attorney-General’s Office was able to come for the cross-examination to continue. We were battle-ready, but they, who are on an ambulance mode to prosecute this case, did not show up.”

Mr Atta Akyea said although the Attorney-General’s absence was explained by his appearance before the Supreme Court on another matter, the prosecution should have anticipated the clash and requested a different date.

He argued that the failure to do so feeds into what he described as an “ambulance mode” in the prosecution of the case, suggesting that the prosecution has consistently sought to expedite proceedings.

The court subsequently adjourned the case to September 8.

Mr Atta Akyea maintained that the defence was prepared to proceed and had expected to make use of the additional time granted by the court to complete its cross-examination.

Ghana News.title: NSA sets September 4 deadline for final rectification of biodata mismatches
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Authority (NSA) has given students with unresolved discrepancies between their academic records and Ghana Card details until Friday, September 4, to complete the rectification process or risk being unable to undertake National Service this year.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, September 2, the NSA said the latest intervention was specifically for students who had already commenced the process of resolving discrepancies but had not yet completed it.

Affected students who still require assistance to align their institutional records with their Ghana Card details and have all relevant supporting documents have been directed to visit the NSA Headquarters or the NSA Kumasi Regional Office from Wednesday, 2 September to Friday, September 4.

The Authority said the exercise was intended to provide a final opportunity for such students to regularise their records and complete their National Service registration.

The NSA also urged schools and other educational institutions that had identified errors in students’ records but had not completed the rectification process to take part in the exercise.

Where necessary, the institutions and affected students are expected to have the required documentation, including Gazette publication, Gazette Receipt and Affidavit, prepared and available to support the formal correction of records.

The Authority stressed the importance of ensuring that students’ academic records correspond with their official identification documents.

“Students are strongly encouraged to ensure that their academic records are consistent with their official identification documents,” the NSA said.

It warned that failure to resolve the discrepancies by the deadline could have serious consequences for affected students.

“Failure to rectify all issues on or before Friday, 4 September will mean the inability of affected students to undertake their National Service this year,” the statement said.

The NSA therefore urged students who had started the correction process but had not yet concluded their registration to act immediately and take advantage of what it described as the final window of opportunity.

The Authority also cautioned students against individuals claiming to be NSA officials and offering to resolve biodata or registration problems in exchange for money.

Students were advised not to share personal information or make payments to unauthorised persons in connection with the rectification exercise.

“Do not share your personal details or make payments to unauthorised persons. Use only official channels for assistance,” the NSA cautioned.

Ghana News.title: Gospel musician Bernice Offei reported missing
Ghana News.content:
Sixty three year-old Ghanaian Gospel musician Bernice Offei, has been reported missing after she was last seen in Accra on Tuesday, 1st September 2026.

She was last seen at Nyaho-Tamakloe Street, Agbogba, in Accra, with her family appealing to the public for information that could help locate her and ensure her safe return home.

Anyone with information about Bernice Offei’s whereabouts is urged to contact 024 878 1971 or 024 755 3431.

Members of the public may also report any information to the nearest police station.

The family is urging the public to share the information widely to help bring Bernice Offei home safely.

Bernice Offei is known for songs including Hold On, Life Is Short, Kaashe Gbeyi, Odo A Wodo Mi Nti, Nyame Kokroko, N’adom Ara Kwa, Don Bi Rebo and Nyame Aye Bi Ama Yen.

Her discography also includes albums such as Hold On, By Grace, Life, Grateful and Me Ko So.
