World.title: Half marathon champs postponed over bomb scare now to take place in Tartu
World.content:
The national half marathon championships which had been due to take place in June will now be held in Tartu in October.

The original race was set to take place in Narva on June 6 and were canceled over a bomb scare which turned out to be a false alarm.

The Estonian Athletic Association on Wednesday announced that this year's Half Marathon Championships will take place in Tartu as part of the Tartu City Marathon event. The half marathon will start at 11 a.m. on October 3.

The championships will determine the Estonian champions in the men's and women's categories. Leonid Latsepov and Liis-Grete Hussar were crowned Estonian champions in the men's and women's categories the last time the race was held in Tartu, two years ago.

The Narva City Run half marathon was canceled after a suspicious bag was found along the route. June 6, 2026.in Narva on Saturday. June 6, 2026. Source: Dmitri Fedotkin/ERR

The planned Estonian Half Marathon Championships were canceled shortly before the start after authorities received a tip about a suspicious bag.

The small bag was found abandoned on a park bench. After examination by the bomb disposal squad; the Rescue Center announced the bag contained personal items and was not a danger.

World.title: Paul Aron to get Alpine F1 drive again, this time at Monza
World.content:
Estonian racing driver Paul Aron will get another Formula One opportunity this week, driving for Alpine in first practice at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza at the weekend.

Aron, 21, is this season a test and reserve driver for the BWT Alpine F1 Team, seen as a stepping stone to a full F1 career. He already took the wheel in practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix this season.

"I'm excited for the first free practice session with the team this weekend," Aron said in a team statement. "I'm grateful to the team for giving me the opportunity to get back behind the wheel again so soon.

F1 NEWS



Estonian driver Paul Aron will take part in the first free practice session in Italy with Alpine. He will replace Pierre Gasly in the cockpit. #F1 #ItalianGP #Alpine pic.twitter.com/M8yRy6QHY4 — Sport Chronicle (@SportFilesF1) September 2, 2026

"I was delighted with my session in Budapest and hope to build on that here, especially by helping the team with our upgrade package, which I have driven with in the simulator," he went on.

"It will be a busy weekend, as I'll be in the simulator in Enstone on Friday evening to help the team further fine-tune the setup before returning on Saturday," the Estonian continued. "I'll give it everything to hopefully contribute to a successful weekend for the team."

Aron made his first official practice appearance of the season for Alpine at the Hungarian Grand Prix in July, where he took part in Friday's free practice.

Alpine's starting drivers are Pierre Gasly (France) and Franco Colapinto (Argentina); Aron deputized for Colapinto in Hungary and is now filling in for Gasly in Italy. The team is French, though based at Enstone in Oxfordshire, England, and traces its DNA back as far as the Toleman team of the early 1980s, which became Benetton and subsequently Renault.

This year's Italian Grand Prix weekend starts this Friday with the race on Sunday as per tradition. There are still another nine races left in 2026, with Kimi Antonelli (Italy) topping the drivers' table for Mercedes with 242 points, over his teammate, Britain's George Russel, and seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari), both on 183 points.

No Estonian has yet raced full-time in F1 even as its northern neighbor, Finland, has had several down the years, three of them becoming world champions.

World.title: Estonia's top defense officials point finger at predecessors
World.content:
At a Riigikogu special committee hearing, the Defense Ministry blamed procurement problems on the Estonian Center for Defense Investments, which in turn blamed its former director. The EDF acknowledged lacking a modern inventory system.

On Wednesday morning, a Riigikogu special committee discussed disarray in the defense sector's accounting. The hearing was prompted by a National Audit Office summary report that identified major problems in the defense sector.

It also emerged Wednesday that Estonia had sought to buy artillery shells for Ukraine and paid a total of €70 million in advance to Indian companies that had never previously sold a single shell. Instead of military materiel, Estonia received repeated promises and the dispute is now in court.

The National Audit Office criticized the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK), which is responsible for procurement, for failing to provide it with the contract for the €70 million shell deal despite repeated requests. RKIK said the contract had been sent on June 5. The National Audit Office maintained that it had not received the contract and the hearing failed to establish which side was correct.

RKIK was also unable to comment on the terms of the contract at the hearing because of a confidentiality clause.

Urmas Reinsalu (Isamaa), who chaired the hearing, asked Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur (Reform) why the contract had not been made available to the National Audit Office.

"I can't recall all the details right now, but as far as I know, some of these contracts simply contain confidentiality clauses agreed with suppliers. Perhaps RKIK can clarify that better," the minister replied. He stressed, however, that in his view, the National Audit Office must be given access to the contracts.

Reinsalu noted that advance payments had been made to a company that had not previously produced ammunition and asked whether the contracts had reached the defense minister in writing and whether the decisions had been documented in writing.

Defense Ministry Permanent Secretary Kaimo Kuusk replied that procurement is RKIK's responsibility and that RKIK also assesses the risks. "Advance payments don't go before the minister for a decision. That's not how it works," he added.

Reinsalu asked whether the Cabinet had also been informed of the risks associated with the intermediary contracts.

Pevkur said the Cabinet had discussed aid to Ukraine in broader terms.

"How to implement the million-round initiative and how to use foreign donors to purchase equipment for Ukraine — implementation of all of that was handed over to the Estonian Center for Defense Investments, which negotiated with the European Commission and donors, agreed on the financing terms and then searched the global market for materiel," Pevkur said.

When Reinsalu again asked whether the minister's position was that no memorandum on the risks had been presented to the Cabinet, Pevkur replied that this was part of RKIK's ordinary business operations. Reinsalu took this as a no.

Kuusk added that information about the contract that had gone sour had also been shared with the Internal Security Service (ISS) and that officials had been in contact with the ambassadors of the countries connected to the contract. "When it became clear that this wasn't producing results, RKIK was instructed to terminate the contract and go to court," he said.

Reinsalu asked how the problematic companies had come into contact with Estonia.

"We trusted the Estonian Center for Defense Investments. The ministry gave the general instruction that assistance needed to be found for Ukraine," Pevkur said.

Pevkur: The minister does not pick contractors

The defense minister confirmed that he had not personally read the problematic contract. The permanent secretary, for his part, stressed that negotiations are RKIK's responsibility.

"We contacted the Internal Security Service (ISS) when delivery deadlines had been missed across the board and the RKIK leadership at the time kept saying that they would still get it done, that the contracts would be fulfilled despite the delays. That no longer inspired confidence. Negotiations over the substance of these issues are RKIK's responsibility," Kuusk said.

Pevkur stressed that the defense minister does not decide who contracts are signed with.

"The minister's decision-making meeting takes place every two weeks. RKIK provides an overview there and it also provided updates on aid to Ukraine. Of course, it reported who contracts were being signed with and what was being procured for Ukraine. This was always agreed with Ukraine and the European Commission as well. These were three-way arrangements. The information presented at the minister's decision-making meeting was who the contractual partners were and what was being procured. It was provided for information purposes," Pevkur said.

The defense minister confirmed that he had been informed of heightened risks related to aid for Ukraine, but said the ministry's position was that those risks had to be mitigated.

"There were no additional risks with the vast majority of partners. Those deliveries reached Ukraine without problems. The delivery from this partner might also have arrived, but the goods they supplied were not of sufficient quality and those goods are still being held pending resolution," Pevkur said.

Kaimo Kuusk told Eesti Ekspress that while the company did deliver some components to an intermediary warehouse, the goods were not of sufficient quality. "The shipment was completely lacking in essential components," Kuusk said. "An artillery round requires a fuse, a propellant charge that ignites in the gun barrel and a primer. Without any one of these components, the round is unusable. Estonia rejected the incomplete shipment," the weekly wrote.

Because RKIK has undergone personnel changes, its current leadership is unable to comment on the problematic deals.

RKIK's current director general, Elmar Vaher, told ERR in an interview that former RKIK director general Magnus-Valdemar Saar bears responsibility for the failed €70 million shell deal.

Estonian Defense Forces lack a modern inventory management system

The hearing also revealed that the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) lacks a modern inventory management system.

The National Audit Office has criticized the Defense Forces over problems with inventory records both in previous reports and at Wednesday's hearing.

Chief of Defense Lt. Gen. Andrus Merilo told the hearing that the EDF has more than 200 million items subject to inventory checks, but insisted there is no issue with whether the items actually exist.

"What can improve the situation are technical solutions that we don't have today. Inventory management and everything else is very much done manually. We don't have the kind of system used by companies with highly advanced warehousing operations because our core mission isn't inventory management, but carrying out military tasks. Once those systems are introduced, things should improve," Merilo said.

Auditor General Janar Holm noted that the inventories conducted by the Defense Forces do not provide sufficient assurance that the items are actually there. Holm stressed that the Defense Forces has been entrusted with a large amount of money and said he did not want to hear the issue dismissed as a "pointless" accounting problem.

"I have never said that accounting is pointless," Merilo replied. "At the same time, I don't accept that after 34 years of service, I'm now hearing suggestions that I have somehow siphoned off money or that the entire Defense Forces has done so. Once again, the supplies exist and are in the possession of subordinate units."

The chief of defense said much of the confusion was related to paperwork. "So I won't allow this to be framed in a way that suggests we don't know where the money is or that money has disappeared when it comes to the Defense Forces," Merilo said.

The auditor general replied that, in that case, the Defense Forces must provide that assurance.

Merilo stressed that Defense Forces personnel are not professional accountants, but said the organization is working to recruit people with the necessary expertise.

World.title: Court issues mostly suspended terms in conscription‑evasion scheme
World.content:
Harju District Court ruled Wednesday that Andrei Vesterinen, Janika Butkevitšus and Armylaw OÜ were guilty of fraud and submitting false information to the Defense Resources Agency (KRA). The court did not find evidence of document forgery or use of forged documents.

The court sentenced Vesterinen to two years and eight months in prison. One month and four days must be served immediately. The remaining two years, six months and 25 days will not be enforced if Vesterinen does not commit a new intentional crime during a three‑year probation period.

The court sentenced Janika Butkevitšus to two years and four months in prison. The sentence will not be enforced if she does not commit a new intentional crime during a three‑year probation period.

The court also found Armylaw OÜ guilty and imposed a fine of €12,000. The fine will not be enforced if Armylaw does not commit a new intentional crime during a one‑year probation period.

Vesterinen must pay €4,824.75 in procedural costs, Butkevitšus €3,519.89 and Armylaw €3,279.28. The defendants must also compensate victims' legal costs totaling €5,414.88. The court granted the civil claims filed by the victims.

According to the charges, Armylaw board member Vesterinen and employee Butkevitšus offered legal services on social media and the company's website in 2021–2022 that promised clients they could "legally" avoid conscription.

Prosecutors said clients were misled and instructed to submit false address information to the population register, forged and used falsified address notices, and changed contact details to prevent KRA from reaching them. They also provided false information about language skills in misdemeanor proceedings to delay cases.

The scheme caused financial losses totaling €16,224.99 to ten victims.

The court found that Vesterinen promised on Armylaw's website and in personal communication with clients that he offered a service allowing them to be released from military service obligations on a legal basis and in a legal manner. He also repeatedly used the slogan "100% guarantee" that clients would not have to enter military service. Based on this, various people — including victims and witnesses — turned to Armylaw for help, believing they were guaranteed a legal way to avoid conscription.

The court found that the instructions given by Vesterinen and Butkevitšus through Armylaw were not lawful. Their actions were aimed at violating norms set out in the Military Service Act and avoiding legally established military service obligations. Their instructions also met the elements of submitting false information to an administrative authority. Their legal guidance misled clients and created the need for further legal assistance.

World.title: Cost of electricity forecast to keep growing due to soaring natural gas prices
World.content:
While cheaper in August year-over-year, electricity became noticeably more expensive in the second half of the month, while developments in the gas market are tending to keep electricity prices higher.

Despite large price swings, the average price of electricity in Estonia was lower in August than a year earlier. While the average exchange price in August last year was €77.30 per megawatt-hour (7.7 cents per kilowatt-hour), this year it was €59 (5.9 cents).

However, the lower price compared with last year was not due to increased wind and solar power generation, but rather limited interconnection capacity with Latvia. As a result, Estonia's exchange electricity price was at the same level as Finland's for more hours than it was at the same level as Latvia's, Marko Allikson of Baltic Energy Partners told ERR.

"The bottleneck in interconnection capacity [with Latvia] was caused by additional storage capacity in Estonia, which was able to successfully enter the Baltic market by making competitive reserve capacity bids," he said.

In August, the average daily price could be just over €4 per megawatt-hour on some days, while on others it rose to €150, with prices fluctuating throughout the month. Comparing the first and second halves of August, electricity prices were clearly higher in the second half.

"Exchange prices were higher in the second half of August because there was less wind and sunshine in Europe, while consumption is also beginning to rise. Rising natural gas prices are also supporting higher prices. These factors reached us primarily through the Lithuania-Sweden and Lithuania-Poland interconnections," Allikson said.

Elektrum Marketing Manager Frederika Frey noted that while electricity prices fell to one of their lowest levels of the year in early August, this was also due to increased wind and solar power generation. In Estonia, however, limited transmission capacity kept prices lower than in Latvia and Lithuania.

"But the situation changed rapidly in the second half of the month. There was less wind and sunshine, meaning more expensive energy sources had to be used to generate electricity. As a result, prices rose sharply within a couple of weeks," she said.

Wind power generation during the last full week of August was among the lowest levels recorded this year, while solar power generation fell to its lowest level since April, Frey added.

A summary by the website elektribörsihind.ee shows that the cheapest hours in August were, on average, between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., while the most expensive were between 7 p.m. and 10 p.m.

Electricity in Estonia was nevertheless clearly more expensive in August than in July, by about one-third.

Comparing the three summer months — June, July and August — with last year, electricity was more expensive this year. Last year's summer average was nearly €52 per megawatt-hour, compared with nearly €56 this year.

Fall prices to be determined by weather and rising natural gas prices

Throughout the summer, forecasts have suggested that energy prices could be unpredictable during the coming fall and winter and that electricity prices on the exchange could fluctuate significantly.

Both Allikson and Frey said prices will depend heavily on weather conditions.

"Windier and sunnier days can quickly push prices down, while low renewable energy generation could lead to another price increase. In addition, prices are affected by constraints on the Baltic states' interconnections, meaning the electricity market could remain quite volatile in the near future," Frey said.

Allikson noted that a cold winter with little wind would mean greater reliance on gas, introducing another factor that increases uncertainty. In particular, it will be important to monitor how successfully European countries can build up their gas stocks for the winter, as low storage levels mean higher prices.

At the same time, the rise in gas prices on the Dutch TTF gas exchange could have a positive effect on European stocks, Allikson said. The current price of more than €70 per megawatt-hour means Europe can attract more LNG, or liquefied natural gas, because gas prices are lower in Asia.

Just a month ago, gas was trading at around €52 per megawatt-hour on the TTF before prices rose rapidly. The last time gas prices were as high as they are now was in late 2022.

However, low storage levels in some European countries could eventually cause gas prices to spike again, Allikson noted.

"Larger price spikes could occur if, for example, Germany or the Netherlands were to begin applying government pressure to fill gas storage facilities at the last minute before winter, regardless of the price level," he said.

Gas storage facilities across the European Union are currently 65 percent full on average. In Germany, for example, storage facilities are currently only slightly more than half full, at 53 percent.

World.title: Estonia elects new president
World.content:
Estonia's parliament elected Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise as the country's next president on Wednesday after one round of voting.

In total, 71 votes were cast in favor of Madise in a secret ballot, and 68 were needed for her to become the head of state. There were seven unmarked ballots and none were judged to be invalid.

Seventy-eight members of the 101-seat Riigikogu received ballots, and all 78 took part in the vote.

After the results were read out, Madise told the MPs present: "I will do my best to be worthy of this trust. I hope that through mutual understanding, debating vigorously when necessary while still supporting one another, we can accomplish a great deal together for Estonia, so that life in Estonia is happy, good and safe."

Madise will become Estonia's seventh president and the second female head of state. She will be sworn into office on October 12.

Madise replaces one-term President Alar Karis, who said he would not stand again in June.

Karis congratulated his successor. "Serving as head of state is a great honour and an even greater responsibility. I wish you strength, wisdom and resolve," he wrote on social media.

Congratulations, Ülle Madise, on your election as the next President of Estonia. Parliament has made its choice, and I will soon hand over the office to you. Serving as head of state is a great honour and an even greater responsibility. I wish you strength, wisdom and resolve. pic.twitter.com/ApQFnjHWjj — Alar Karis (@AlarKaris) September 2, 2026

This story is being updated...

Who is Ülle Madise?

Ülle Madise (born Ülle Anton on December 11, 1974, in Tartu, Estonia) is an eminent Estonian jurist, legal scholar, and the country's chancellor of justice.

She earned her law degree and master's degree from the University of Tartu. In 2007, she completed her PhD in administrative management at the Tallinn University of Technology

Her career reflects a steady rise through Estonia's public institutions. She held early roles in the Ministry of Justice, served as an adviser to the Riigikogu Constitutional Committee, and worked as chief auditor at the National Audit Office.

From 2009 to 2015, Madise served as the legal adviser to then President of Estonia Toomas Hendrik Ilves. Concurrently, she pursued an academic career, teaching as a professor of public law and constitutional law in several Estonian universities.

Ülle Madise after being elected president on September 2, 2026. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

On March 31, 2015, Madise assumed office as the chancellor of justice. In this role, she has been advocating for individual liberties, criticizing over-regulation, and maintaining a non-partisan stance.

Beyond constitutional duties, Madise is a passionate champion of the Estonian language. She has strongly advocated for clear public communications.

Madise is widely regarded as one of Estonia's most influential public officials. This standing culminated in the summer of 2026 when she emerged as a leading apolitical candidate for the Estonian presidential election, backed by several major parties.

She is married to Lauri Madise, a judge on the General Court of the European Union's Court of Justice.

World.title: Gun found in French lake may unlock Iraqi family murder mystery
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — French detectives are looking into a weapon discovered from Lake Annecy, which might give a fresh clue in the unsolved 2012 murder of British-Iraqi engineer Saad al-Hilli, his family, and a French cyclist.

British holidaymakers discovered the Luger handgun on August 20 in roughly two meters of water near Le Solitaire du Lac, the campground where the al-Hilli family had been camping before to the deaths, according to French magazine Marianne.

The location and kind of weapon have piqued investigators’ attention since the four victims were slain using a Luger P06 handgun, which was formerly used by the Swiss military.

The murder weapon was never found.

Forensic specialists are now investigating the severely damaged pistol to establish if it is a P06 and whether it is related to the murder.

Al-Hilli, an Iraqi-born British citizen from a prominent Iraqi family, was on holiday with his family in the French Alps when he, his wife Iqbal, mother-in-law Suhaila al-Allaf, and cyclist Sylvain Mollier were found shot dead near Chevaline on September 5, 2012.

The couple’s two young girls escaped the deadly assault, with one hiding inside the family’s vehicle for hours before someone found her.

Over the last 14 years, French and British detectives have exvariousiety of possibilities, including familial and financial issues, a random assault, and the likelihood that Mollier was the intended target.

No clear motive or perpetrator has been established.

The finding might be important since detectives have long considered retrieving the murder weapon as a possible way to solve the cold case.

France’s cold-case section in Nanterre has said that the newly recovered handgun may be pertinent to the inquiry.

Investigators must now determine if the pistol is the same type used in the deaths and, more importantly, whether forensic evidence may link it to one of France’s longest-running murder mysteries.

World.title: Iraqi oil shipments surge by 70% in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two Iraqi energy officials told Reuters that Iraqi oil exports surged by more than 70 percent to around 2.34 million barrels per day in August, compared to approximately 1.35 million barrels per day in July.

The officials explained that the arrival of more oil tankers at southern Iraqi export terminals and the loading of crude oil led to an increase in shipments during August.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said on Tuesday that the country’s crude oil exports through its southern marine outlets, which link to the Strait of Hormuz, fluctuated between two million and 2.2 million barrels per day in August.

The ministry stressed that these outlets are the major conduit for Iraqi oil exports and a vital part of the national export system.

As part of its attempts to increase the flexibility of the oil export system and minimize dependency on a single route, al-Rikabi stated that the ministry is supporting and developing various alternative export outlets through northern and western Iraq.

Al-Rikabi emphasized that Iraqi oil flows to the Turkish port of Ceyhan are continuing with volumes ranging between 150,000 and 180,000 barrels per day.

Advanced steps are being taken to explore the possibility of increasing oil exports through the Syrian port of Baniyas, according to al-Rikabi. This initiative would offer Iraq an additional outlet to the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: Baghdad to unify digital customs system across Iraq including Kurdistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Falih Al-Sari has called for expediting customs automation and extending the ASYCUDA system to border crossings in the Kurdistan Region, as Baghdad strives to unify customs operations and boost non-oil income.

During a meeting on customs modernization, al-Sari authorized authorities to start advance payment of customs taxes on October 1, while continuing to develop the Automated System for Customs Data, or ASYCUDA.

The Finance Minister also emphasized the necessity to implement the system at border crossings in the Kurdistan Region, which would integrate federal and regional customs operations under a more unified digital framework.

The move is part of a larger government initiative to replace paper-based customs processes with computerized systems that may increase supervision, speed up clearance, and give authorities with more accurate import and revenue data.

Expanding ASYCUDA throughout Iraq might also help resolve long-standing disagreements between Baghdad and Erbil over customs processes and border income.

A unified system would provide both sides with a standard method for documenting transactions and determining tariffs at border crossings.

The government has increasingly resorted to customs and other non-oil sources to diversify state income and lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

Digital customs systems are also seen as a key instrument for limiting potential for fraud and revenue leakage at border crossings by keeping electronic records of goods, payments, and customs declarations.

Al-Sari’s initiative comes as the Finance Ministry collaborates with other state agencies to electronically connect customs operations to Iraq’s banking and payment infrastructure, enabling fees to be collected and recorded via legitimate financial channels.

The anticipated October 1 implementation of advance customs payments would be another step in that transformation, forcing tariffs to be cleared earlier in the import process rather than depending on customary processes at individual crossings.

Implementing the same system in the Kurdistan Region would be especially important, bringing Iraq closer to a unified national customs framework and perhaps allowing Baghdad and Erbil more control over income produced at the country’s borders.

World.title: Iraq rejects proposal to keep international coalition forces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has publicly rejected a plan to keep any US-led international coalition forces in Iraq after the September 30, 2026, deadline.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi government, Haider al-Aboudi, said during a press briefing that Baghdad remains strictly committed to the conclusion of the foreign military mission in the country, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that October 1, 2026, will mark a new day in Iraq’s statehood when the country achieves complete sovereignty free of foreign troops.

The military mission of the international coalition will expire on September 30, 2026, and the decision is final and irreversible, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister underscored that October 1 will bring in a new period of total Iraqi independence and full territorial sovereignty, with no foreign military presence.

Iraq’s future interactions with the international coalition’s member states will focus on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared military victory over ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to provide advice and training services at Baghdad’s request.

The official withdrawal of the international coalition follows a bilateral arrangement agreed upon by Baghdad and Washington.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes 4,152m horizontal well in East Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Technical and engineering crews from the state-owned Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) have completed drilling operations on horizontal oil well EBS-157 in the South East Baghdad oil field, reaching a total measured depth of 4,152 meters, the company announced on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

Executed under the directives of Minister of Oil Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abbadi and supervised by IDC Director General Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Ozairjawi, the project represents a technical milestone in deploying advanced directional drilling within structurally complex reservoirs.

Technical Specifications and Drilling Parameters

Rig Deployment: Executed utilizing the IDC-36 drilling rig, operating with a rated capacity of 1,500 horsepower (HP).

Trajectory Profile: Drilled horizontally with a maximum deviation inclination reaching 90.31 degrees, maximizing reservoir contact within the target formation.

Subsurface Engineering: Tailored to address the geological characteristics and pressure profiles of the South East Baghdad field in full adherence to international engineering standards.

Operational Scope: Forms part of an ongoing multi-well development contract signed with China’s EBS (ZhenHua Oil subsidiary operator) to drill 17 oil wells, carried out in technical collaboration with COSL (China Oilfield Services Limited).

Director General Al-Ozairjawi affirmed that the Iraqi Drilling Company continues to upgrade its technical capacity across a diverse fleet of drilling and workover rigs.

By executing complex horizontal, directional, and deep vertical profiles using domestic engineering cadres, IDC aims to reduce dependence on external contractors and accelerate upstream field development plans set by the Ministry of Oil.

World.title: Integrity and Investment commissions partner to safeguard capital in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Federal Commission of Integrity and the National Investment Commission (NIC) have agreed to deepen joint operational coordination to insulate Iraq’s investment climate from corruption, bribery, and regulatory extortion, officials announced on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The alignment was formalized during a bilateral meeting between the President of the Federal Commission of Integrity, Dr. Mohammad Ali Al-Lami, and the Chairman of the National Investment Commission, Adel Al-Yasiri. Both officials underscored that asset recovery and anti-graft enforcement must directly reinforce national reconstruction and economic development.

Core Areas of Institutional Cooperation

Shielding Investors from Extortion: Establishing streamlined reporting mechanisms to identify and prosecute illicit extortion, bureaucratic bribery, and administrative gatekeeping targeting domestic and foreign businesses.

Streamlining Project Clearances: Eliminating regulatory bottlenecks and discretionary hurdles that impede licensed development projects and delay the entry of foreign direct investment (FDI).

Creating a Predictable Business Environment: Dr. Al-Lami emphasized that robust oversight bodies provide the legal certainty and security assurances necessary to attract multinational capital and corporate partners to Iraq.

Reinforcing Public Confidence: Emphasized that transparent judicial outcomes—convicting corrupt actors and recovering stolen assets—must advance in tandem with tangible improvements in municipal services and infrastructure.

Strategic Alignment Between Oversight and Investment

Institutional Focus Operational Objective Impact on Business Climate Federal Commission of Integrity Probing extortion networks, tracing illicit wealth, and prosecuting corrupt officials. Reduces transaction friction, illicit compliance costs, and regulatory risk. National Investment Commission (NIC) Licensing strategic development projects and facilitating capital entry. Accelerates infrastructure execution and safeguards investor concessions. Judicial Partnership Enforcing convictions and securing asset freezes in coordination with specialized courts. Establishes binding legal safeguards for foreign and domestic private capital.

NIC Chairman Adel Al-Yasiri commended the Integrity Commission’s field operations conducted alongside the Iraqi judiciary, noting that dismantling extortion networks that illicitly profit off state resources is a prerequisite for a competitive economy.

Al-Yasiri affirmed that creating an accountable administrative framework provides institutional protection for capital inflows, ensuring that licensed projects proceed without illicit disruptions.

World.title: Mahua slams rebel TMC MPs  over delay in responding disqualification notices
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MP

on Wednesday slammed the party's rebel MPs for seeking additional time to respond to notices issued to them by the Lok Sabha secretariat.

While talking to reporters, Mahua said that the rebel MPs' inability to respond within the stipulated period shows that they know they are in the wrong.

"We have filed 20 disqualification petitions against MPs who were elected on TMC tickets but joined hands with the

. The Lok Sabha Secretariat sent notices last week to them asking them to reply within seven days. The deadline is over, but they could not reply. Now they have sought another two-three weeks," Mahua said.

"We had written to the Lok Sabha Speaker in June. Why were they unable to reply in two months? Why does it take you more than one week to reply? If you ask me, I will not take so much time to reply," she added.

"The wigs and masks have come off. Their shamelessness and betrayal are for everyone to see," she said.

World.title: Ram temple trust gets three new trustees, brings in education, philanthropy and public life experience

LUCKNOW: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has appointed three new trustees, bringing into its governing body a philanthropist associated with the legacy of late VHP leader Ashok Singhal, a former public representative from Ayodhya and an educationist from Shikohabad whose family has links with the Indian Air Force, the RSS and the erstwhile Jana Sangh.The appointments of Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav were announced after the Trustâs meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday. The three have filled vacancies in the Trustâs governing body.Mahesh Bhagchandka, 68, is founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation, is related to Ashok Singhal, one of the prominent figures associated with the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Bhagchandka is also a graduate, businessman based in New Delhi. He is also the author of Hindutva ke Purodha, a book on prominent figures associated with the Hindutva movement.He participated in the rituals as a yajman during both the bhoomi pujan ceremony for the construction of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple and the templeâs pran pratishtha programme. His association with Ram-related cultural initiatives also includes work connected with the Shri Ram Van Gaman Yatra.Bhagchandka has been involved in the installation of Shri Ram Stambhs at 292 sacred sites associated with the route believed to have been taken by Lord Ram during his exile.He is also a member of the executive committee of the World Hindu Economic Forum.His appointment gives the Trust a member with experience in social and cultural initiatives as well as temple-related programmes. He is also related to late Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Ashok Singhal and is a founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation.Madan Mohan Pandey 74, is a law graduate and advocate based in Ayodhya Cantonment. He represented Shri Ram Lalla Virajman and late Mahant Ramchandra Paramhans Das in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi legal dispute from 1990 to 2019 before the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court.His long association with the temple case places him among those who were directly involved in the legal proceedings that culminated in the Supreme Court judgment paving the way for the construction of the Ram temple at Ayodhya.Pandey also served as Uttar Pradeshâs additional advocate general for six years. Besides his legal practice, he is associated with religious and educational activities. He is the vice-president of the Shri Hari Satsang Samiti and the patron of the Kathakar Yojana training centre in Ayodhya.The third appointee, Nirmala Yadav, comes from a family with a long association with education and public life in Firozabad district. Though the family is originally linked to Uravar village under Sirsaganj tehsil, it has been settled in Shikohabad for several decades. Yadav herself originally hailed from Etah and moved to Shikohabad after her marriage.Yadav served as principal of BDM Girls PG College in Shikohabad from 1999 to 2006. She later became principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya (PG) College in Firozabad and retired in 2022.Priyadarshini Upadhaya, the present principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya and a former colleague of Yadav, described her as a highly capable administrator. She said Yadav had a strong command over institutional management and was particularly efficient in handling administrative and desk responsibilities.Yadavâs late husband, advocate Harendra Yadav, had served as an RSS district chief. Her father-in-law, Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav, served in the Indian Air Force and was later associated with the Jan Sangh.According to her nephew Sachin Yadav, the familyâs association with education dates back to 1916, when his great-grandfather, Chaudhary Shyam Singh Yadav, founded Kanhai College in Shikohabad. The family also produced a former MLA, Captain Nihal Singh and Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav.

World.title: ‘Not democratically elected’: SC says Manan Kumar Mishra only ‘pro tem’ BCI chairman till fresh election
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Wednesday said Bar Council of India (BCI) chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra was only a âpro tem Chairmanâ until a freshly constituted BCI elects its office-bearers, and directed that major policy decisions be taken in consultation with the Attorney General for India and the Solicitor General, who are permanent ex-officio BCI members.

A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said Mishra could oversee the BCI's day-to-day functioning but could not be treated as a democratically elected office-bearer once the newly elected state bar councils complete the process of constituting a fresh BCI.

âYou should also bear in mind that you are like a pro tem chairman till a fresh election of the Bar Council of India, pursuant to the elections already conducted in the state bar councils, takes place,â Justice Bagchi told senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the BCI chairman, according to LiveLaw.

âSo, it is not a situation where he is democratically elected and continues to be so. His term is co-terminus with the elections which are imminent,â the judge said.

The court said the existing arrangement could continue for routine administrative work but stressed that institutional checks would apply to policy decisions.

âIn such situations, day-to-day functioning can be left to the existing arrangement. However, when a policy decision is taken, the participation of a permanent ex officio member acting independently, such as the Attorney General, is necessary,â Justice Bagchi remarked orally, PTI said.





The bench also said it was not endorsing Mishra's continued tenure.

âWe are not placing any stamp of approval upon the existing arrangement. It is apparent that the present chairperson can continue only until a fresh election to the Bar Council of India takes place pursuant to the state bar council elections already conducted,â it said.

The observations came while the court heard pleas challenging Mishra's continued occupation of the BCI chairperson's post and the legal basis for extending his tenure until 2030.

Senior advocate Madhavi Divan, appearing for the petitioners, said Mishra was unanimously elected chairman for a term from April 17, 2025 to April 16, 2030. She also challenged a resolution extending the tenure of the chairman and vice-chairman from three years to five years despite rules prescribing a two-year term.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for one of the petitioners, questioned the creation of the Bar Council of India Trust for Promotion of Education, Legal and Professional Reforms and Improvement in Research.

Sankaranarayanan alleged that its deed made 11 managing trustees âoriginal and permanent trusteesâ. The bench questioned how elected members could appoint themselves as perpetual trustees.

âThe Bar Council of India is a juristic entity. That entity has created a trust from its assets through the elected members who constituted the Council. Can those elected members make themselves permanent trustees of those assets when the composition of the corporate entity that settled the trust is itself determined through elections?â it asked.

The court directed the newly constituted state bar councils to elect their office-bearers and representatives to the BCI within three weeks of notification of their composition. The matter will be heard next on September 23.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) president Dr Farooq Abdullah on Wednesday questioned recent threats allegedly targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees serving in the Kashmir Valley, asking why senior Hindu officials posted in the region were not facing similar threats.

A fresh threat letter was allegedly circulated on social media targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees, prompting the All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir to seek enhanced security from the Jammu and Kashmir administration.

In a letter to the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, the forum said the purported threat poster, allegedly issued by an outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) and dated August 23, contains the names, addresses and vehicle numbers of some employees.

Speaking in Anantnag, Abdullah said, âWho is issuing them? Do Kashmiri Pandits not live here?â He questioned why officials such as the DIG, DG, district SPs and Deputy Commissioners were not receiving threats if Hindus were being specifically targeted.

World.title: West Asia conflict LIVE: Iran security chief says U.S. to face new war strategy; Bessent warns 'everyone' against backing Tehran
World.content:
Iran threatened to take a tougher line in its war with the United States on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) after the heaviest exchanges in weeks left at least 19 Iranians dead, including four at a wedding -- an incident slammed as a “war crime” by Tehran. A wave of Iranian attacks earlier targeted US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, after extensive U.S. bombardment hit sites across Iran.

Watch | U.S., Iran exchange fresh strikes near Strait of Hormuz

U.S. President Donald Trump had warned earlier of “much harder and higher” attacks if Iran retaliated to the U.S. strikes, which Iran’s military and state media said killed 18 people. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesperson Tim Hawkins said “the U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC”, referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

The latest flare-up is part of a cycle of retaliation that followed U.S. strikes on Iran, with fighting over the Hormuz strait expanding to Washington’s Gulf allies, military bases and commercial shipping. It began when Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday (August 30, 2026), the first known strikes in several weeks, after which Tehran’s forces targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks.

World.title: Madurai RTO office comes under DVAC scanner
World.content:
The officers attached to the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) raided the premises of the Regional Transport Office (South), Madurai, and seized ₹1.80 lakh from “brokers” on Wednesday.

Sources said following specific inputs, the DVAC officials, led by Additional Superintendent of Police Sathyaseelan and Inspectors Jayaprabha, Ramesh Prabhu and Kumaraguru, conducted the raid from 3 p.m.. They seized ₹60,200 from Kani, who introduced himself as a broker. The DVAC team also seized ₹79,000 from Mariskumar, and the remaining amount as unclaimed money.

RTO (South) Karthikeyan was also interrogated by the officials. Preliminary inquiries and confession by some of the brokers suggested that they had collected the money from the public for getting various services done in the RTO office and the money was meant for select officers in the department.

A few days ago, a similar raid was conducted at Madurai North Sub-Registrar Office in Chettikulam, and the DVAC officials seized ₹1.86 lakh. The officers found the money stashed in the cupboards used by the staff memebers, including Sub-Registrar (in-charge) Rajan.

Camera operator Muthumani 31, Arunpandi 26 from Karuppayoorani, Seerajudeen, 30, from Surya Nagar, Santosh Balaji, 27, from Vandiyur, Venkatesan, 37, from Thirupparankundram and Premkumar, 58, from Kalai Nagar were investigated.

A senior official said the DVAC unit received specific complaints of bribery in the office and based on that they conducted the check. A few documents were seized from the premises and further investigation was on.

World.title: After missing deadline, Bengaluru’s Namma Metro Pink Line’s 7.5-km stretch ready, inauguration expected in September
World.content:
After missing several deadlines, the 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch of Pink Line is ready for inauguration, with Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda expressing hope that the Centre will approve an inauguration date within September.

Speaking about the new addition to the city’s metro network, Mr. Gowda said the stretch is ready to be opened for public use and will be inaugurated once the Government of India provides a date. “We are ready. As soon as the date is given by the Government of India, this stretch will be inaugurated and opened to people for commuting,” he said on Wednesday.

Mr. Gowda had earlier stated that the inauguration would happen in August 2026. This was announced after his first high-level review meeting with senior officials of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), after he took over charge of the portfolio.

The Minister had noted that the elevated section of the Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere was expected to become operational by August 15, 2026, and that the underground stretch from Tavarekere to Nagawara was slated for completion by March 2027.

The 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch of Bengaluru's Pink Line is ready for inauguration and will soon be open to the public. We are hopeful of receiving a date from the Government of India in September.



Along with MP Tejaswi Surya, MLA M. Krishnappa, Metro MD P.C. Jafar… pic.twitter.com/9BwxeZK0Ks — Krishna Byre Gowda (@krishnabgowda) September 2, 2026

The Pink Line, a 21.3-km corridor connecting Kalena Agrahara in the south to Nagawara in the north, is a crucial component of the metro expansion. Of the total length, 13.8 km runs underground, linking key central areas such as Dairy Circle, M.G. Road, Shivajinagar and Tannery Road, while 7.5 km is elevated.

The project has faced repeated delays, missing several deadlines and drawing criticism from commuters. Once operational, the corridor is expected to significantly improve north-south metro connectivity.

“A sufficient number of trains are presently available for commissioning the elevated stretch. The trains are currently undergoing the prescribed trials and testing and are required to complete the mandatory 750-km running before deployment for passenger services. Train operators are identified and their mandatory training is expected to be completed this week,” Mr. Gowda said.

BMRCL is expecting approval from the Railway Board for the new rolling stock shortly. This will be followed by inspection and authorisation by the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety for opening the elevated section of the Pink Line for public service.

World.title: Kadapa SP calls for enhanced training in modern policing
World.content:
Superintendent of Police (SP) Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath inaugurated a modern computer laboratory and a newly-constructed dais at the District Police Training Centre in Kadapa on Wednesday.

Laying emphasis on future policing, the SP wanted comprehensive training to be imparted to the modern day police personnel, which would involved technological knowledge, professional competence and discipline. “Strengthening infrastructure at the police training centre will provide a better learning environment for trainee police and enhance the overall training quality,” Mr. Nachiket said.

World.title: Students’ Counselling and Guidance Centre established on Collectorate premises
World.content:
In a novel initiative, the district administration has established a District Counselling Centre on the Collectorate campus to counsel and guide the school and college students.

District Collector Anand Mohan and Superintendent of Police Vishwesh Balasubramanian Shastri inaugurated the facility on Wednesday.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Anand Mohan said the younger generation, especially school and college students easily get influenced by negative social media posts and were exposed to liquor, tobacco and even drugs. Consequently, the younger generation was suffering from lack of attention in the classroom and interest in studies, depression, anger, violence, examination fear that collectively create dropouts.

At the same time, a few more children undergo the trauma of child abuse, child marriage, physical and emotional harassment by the family members, relatives and friends. A large number of children get addicted to mobile phone and online games.

“Hence, we’ve established this counselling centre at the Collectorate to identify the children’s exact problems and rehabilitate them from these habits through proper counselling and guidance. Instead of legally punishing the young offenders, we need to counsel and guide them as they have got a future,” Mr. Anand Mohan said.

The District Counselling Centre, established by District Child Protection Unit, is a joint venture of Departments of School Education, Higher Education, Technical Education, Public Health, Social Welfare and Police. Qualified counsellors and professional psychologists will be there between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. on all working days to counsel and guide the students and their parents or guardians.

“The personal information about the youth coming here for counselling and guidance will be closely guarded secret and will never be shared with anyone at any cost,” assured Mr. Anand Mohan.

World.title: Keralam raises demand of detailed technical study of Mullaperiyar dam before safety  panel
World.content:
Keralam has demanded a rigorous, long-term technical evaluation of the Mullaperiyar dam before the five-member comprehensive safety panel. The State submitted an eight-page written document detailing its safety concerns. According to officials, both Keralam and Tamil Nadu presented their arguments during the meeting.

James Wilson, adviser to the Kerala government on inter-State water issues, said the State emphasised critical safety parameters. “We spoke to them about floods, seismology, and the necessity of extracting and testing core samples from the dam. We pointed out that this is not a process that can be concluded with a routine one-day inspection; it is an extensive, detailed process. We didn’t just state our concerns verbally; we submitted them in writing as well,” Mr. Wilson said.

He said the expert panel agreed to consider the State’s concerns, though whether to act on them remained within the committee’s mandate. “What we primarily demanded is that the safety review proceed strictly in accordance with the terms of reference (ToR) fixed in August 2025,” he added.

“All our safety concerns have been presented before the committee in detail. Our demands fall under four main areas, namely, hydrological safety, covering capacity and response under severe flood scenarios; structural safety, regarding material integrity, which necessitates core sampling and rigorous physical testing; seismic vulnerability, involving a re-evaluation of geological risks and earthquake resilience; and seepage instrumentation, for precise measurement and assessment of seepage parameters,” the official said.

On Tuesday, the panel carried out a comprehensive field inspection of the main dam, baby dam, earthen dam, and spillway. The panel’s chairman, former NHPC CMD Balraj Joshi, stated on Tuesday that the committee will submit its report within two weeks.

Sources said the State also requested that if the panel cannot conduct a full scientific study as part of its present inspection, it should formally recommend one in its final report.

The panel includes Gopal Dhawan (former ED, NHPC), Prof. M.L. Sharma (Head, International Centre of Excellence in Earthquakes and Professor of Earthquake Engineering, IIT Roorkee), Gulshan Raj (former Chairman, Ganga Flood Control Commission), and Ashutosh Dash (former Engineer-in-Chief-cum-Special Secretary, Water Resources Department, Odisha).

The safety evaluation follows a 2022 Supreme Court directive ordering a comprehensive review of the Mullaperiyar dam, based on a petition filed by Kothamangalam resident Joe Joseph.

World.title: Pakistan 'hopeful' despite US-Iran escalation, will continue to strive for dialogue and diplomacy: FO
World.content:
Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said on Wednesday that Pakistan remained “hopeful” despite recent escalations between the US and Iran and would continue to strive for dialogue and diplomacy.

Pakistan has been spearheading efforts for an end to the ongoing war that began with US-Israeli attacks on Iran in February.

Besides signing the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding as the mediator in June, Islamabad had also brokered a ceasefire between the US and Iran in April. The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement.

Recapping Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in this connection over the week, the FO spokesperson recalled that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of an SCO summit earlier this week and discussed the evolving regional situation.

“The prime minister had reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to peace through restraint, dialogue and diplomacy, while stressing that the Islamabad MoU offered the most viable pathway to lasting peace and stability in the region,” he said.

He said Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also interacted with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the SCO summit, while Pakistan and Iran’s leadership had earlier discussed the Middle East and Gulf situation in Istanbul on the sidelines of the Makkah defence pact meeting.

Andrabi added that Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir had also visited Tehran last week as part of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to facilitate an end to the US-Iran conflict, particularly reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital passageway for the world’s fuel supply.

“Regional de-escalation, breaking the military stalemate and exploring a negotiated settlement to restore regional peace and stability were the main topics discussed” during the meeting, he said.

The visit, he said, “underscored Islamabad’s sincere and constructive role in bridging differences between Washington and Tehran”. It generated momentum, as evident by the subsequent visits of Oman and Qatar’s leadership to Iran, he added.

Pakistan welcomes Hague court ruling on IWT

During the briefing, the FO also spoke about the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s (PCA) decision on Monday, under which it directed India to uphold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir.

He said the PCA had reaffirmed that the IWT remained fully enforced and binding, rejecting India’s unilateral attempt to place the treaty in a so-called “abeyance”.

“The unanimous award of the Court of Arbitration constitutes an important reaffirmation of the sanctity of the IWT and the rule of international law,” he said.

Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025.

Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties.

In its order, the PCA backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement.

The FO spokesperson said, “The court had confirmed that India’s purported decision to place the treaty in abeyance does not relieve it of its obligations under the treaty and the treaty’s dispute settlement mechanism remained operative.”

Moreover, he continued, the court’s interim measure concerning the Ratle hydroelectric power project further affirmed that rights and obligations under the treaty could not be altered or displaced through unilateral action, he added.

“Pakistan welcomes this clear and authoritative announcement, which validates our consistent position that differences concerning the Indus Waters Treaty must be strictly addressed within the framework of the treaty and in accordance with international law,” he said.

Concluding his opening statement, he introduced Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan to his audience and said the latter would replace him as the FO spokesperson after the briefing.

According to state-run APP, Andrabi will be assuming the role of Pakistan’s permanent representative to the United Nations in Geneva.

World.title: IHC sets aside 2022 verdict declaring Pakistan Naval Farms, sailing club in Islamabad illegal
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) division bench on Wednesday set aside a 2022 judgment by then-chief justice Athar Minallah declaring the Pakistan Naval Farms and Pakistan Navy Sailing Club along Rawal Lake illegal.

The court also nullified directions for the demolition of the sailing club and the initiation of misconduct and criminal proceedings against former naval chief Admiral (retd) Zafar Mahmood Abbasi and other officers.

A division bench comprising Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas and Justice Shahrukh Arjumand allowed the intra-court appeals filed against the single-bench judgment.

The bench also set aside the direction to the Auditor General of Pakistan to assess the alleged loss caused to the national exchequer and recover the amount from the officers held responsible.

The court further nullified the order declaring the transfer of Naval Farms to the Pakistan Navy illegal, as well as the direction to transfer the land in the name of the headquarters office.

The appeals had been filed by the Ministry of Defence, former naval chief Admiral (retd) Abbasi and other affected parties against the 2022 judgment of the single bench.

During the hearing, Sardar Ahmed Jamal Sukhera, counsel for the federation and the Ministry of Defence, argued that the original petition filed by Zeenat Salim primarily concerned notices issued by Pakistan Naval Farms over alleged violations of building bylaws.

He submitted that in 2020, the Directorate of PN Farms had itself written to the Capital Development Authority (CDA), informing it that under the NOC issued by the CDA, Naval Farms was required to comply with building bylaws. Consequently, notices were issued to the concerned residents over alleged violations, while the CDA was also informed and requested to take appropriate action.

According to the counsel, Naval Farms subsequently informed all residents that CDA building bylaws would be implemented at the farms with immediate effect.

Sukhera argued that these developments had taken place in 2020, well before the single-bench judgment was delivered in 2022, and that the principal grievance raised in the petition had therefore already been addressed.

He contended that the subsequent judgment contained findings against the armed forces which, according to him, were baseless and unsupported by the evidence on record.

The counsel further relied on Supreme Court precedents, arguing that a court should not decide matters beyond what is necessary to determine a dispute.

He also challenged the maintainability of the petition after an amendment was allowed to introduce objections regarding the existence of the sailing club. He argued that public-interest litigation could not be maintained where the petitioner had a personal interest in the matter, claiming that the record showed Zeenat Salim had such an interest.

In another appeal, Sukhera argued that the earlier judgment had been passed in violation of the principles of natural justice, due process and a fair trial.

He submitted that the judgment had adversely affected the vested interests of more than 100 club members, but none of them had been issued notices or impleaded as necessary parties.

The counsel further pointed out that no notice had been issued to the respondent in the petition filed by Nasir Ali, contending that the judgment was therefore legally unsustainable.

Former naval chief Admiral (retd) Zafar Mahmood Abbasi also presented additional evidence before the court in support of the appeals.

After hearing the arguments and examining the record, the division bench held that the principles of natural justice, due process and a fair trial had been violated, as the affected parties had neither been issued notices nor provided an opportunity of being heard, while necessary parties had also not been impleaded.

Consequently, the division bench allowed the intra-court appeals and set aside the findings and directions contained in the single-bench judgment.

As a result, the declaration of Pakistan Naval Farms and Pakistan Navy Sailing Club as illegal, the order for demolition of the sailing club, proceedings against the former naval chief and other officers, and directions concerning the assessment and recovery of losses to the national exchequer all stand nullified.

Ashtar Ausaf, Sardar Ahmed Jamal Sukhera and Abdul Wahid Qureshi appeared on behalf of the appellants, while the additional attorney general, assistant attorney general and counsel for the CDA represented the federation and other respondents.

World.title: PMD predicts more rain in upper regions over the weekend, including Islamabad
World.content:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) issued a weather advisory on Wednesday predicting more rain in the upper regions of the country over the weekend, particularly in the Potohar region and Islamabad.

The Met office said that monsoon currents were penetrating the upper parts of the country, according to the advisory issued at 3pm on Wednesday. It added that a westerly wave was also affecting these regions and likely to strengthen on September 4-5 (Friday and Saturday).

Under the influence of this weather system, it said that rain-wind and thundershowers — with isolated heavy falls — were expected in Kashmir’s Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur from Thursday to Sunday, with occasional gaps.

In Gilgit-Baltistan, the same is expected in Diamer, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar during the same time period.

Rain-wind and thundershowers “with scattered heavy falls, at times very heavy” were forecast in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Peshawar, Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Malakand, Mardan, Nowshera, Charsadda, Swabi, Shangla, Battagram, Buner, Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Karak, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Dera Ismail Khan, Bannu and Waziristan, from the evening of Sep 3 to Sep 5 with occasional gaps.

In Islamabad and upper Punjab, similar thundershowers and isolated heavy or very heavy falls were predicted in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Galliyat, Jhelum, Chakwal, Talagang, Attock, Lahore, Sialkot, Sheikhupura, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Wazirabad, Hafizabad and Kasur from Sep 3-5. The PMD forecast the same in Okara, Nankana Sahib, Sargodha, Khushab, Mianwali, Noorpur Thal, Faisalabad, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh, Layyah, Bhakkar, Sahiwal, Dera Ghazi Khan and the surrounding areas between Sep 4-5 with occasional gaps.

The Met Office added that “mainly hot and humid weather” would prevail in most parts of Sindh and Balochistan during the forecast period, but noted that rain-wind and thunderstorms were expected in Zhob, Bar Khan, Musakhel and the surrounding areas.

The PMD advisory warned that the heavy rains may cause urban flooding in low-lying areas of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, as well as Peshawar, Mardan, Swabi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, Faisalabad and Lahore on Friday and Saturday.

It also warned of flash flooding in local streams and nullahs in Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Shangla, Battagram, Buner, Malakand, Mansehra, Abbottabad, GB, Kashmir, Murree, Galliyat and the twin cities during the forecast period.

“Landslides may occur in hilly areas of KP, GB, Murree, Galliyat and Kashmir during the forecast period,” it added, advising tourists and travellers to “remain cautious”.

The PMD also advised farmers to manage their crop activities in view of the weather conditions. It asked all concerned authorities to remain alert and take necessary measures to avoid untoward situations.

Heavy rain has already been lashing Rawalpindi and Islamabad this week, inundating low-lying areas on Tuesday morning and raising the water level in Leh Nullah.

On Monday, about two hours of heavy showers caused rainwater to accumulate in streets and low-lying areas of Rawalpindi, turning roads into small ponds. Many cars and motorcycles were seen stranded in rainwater.

World.title: Act for Nutrition conference: Experts call for multisectoral approach, community-led intervention in addressing malnutrition crisis
World.content:
Gates Foundation official says nutrition should be framed as a GDP statistic; WHO official says “no bigger risk than lack of action”.

Listen to article 1x 1.2x 1.5x

Day 1 of the two-day international conference, ‘Act For Nutrition: The Emergency We Can No Longer Ignore’ — held at Islamabad’s Serena Hotel — concluded on Wednesday, with experts urging urgent action on Pakistan’s malnutrition and stunting crisis, with a focus on multisectoral interventions.

With more than 40 per cent of children under five stunted, a maternal mortality rate of 155 deaths per 100,000 live births, and malnutrition costing Pakistan upwards of $17 billion annually, the country stands at a crossroads: continue on the current trajectory and surrender an entire generation’s potential, or choose a different future.

The two-day conference is bringing together policymakers, international development leaders, health professionals and nutrition experts to confront the burgeoning crisis and build momentum for urgent, coordinated action.

The focus of discussions will be on moving the national conversation beyond statistics towards practical, measurable interventions that can improve nutrition outcomes and protect Pakis­tan’s human capital and future generations.

View the full agenda here.

5:27pm - Day 1 of the conference concludes

5:15pm - Researcher calls for nutrition-related interventions at community, systemic levels

Director at the International Research Force Dr Hana Mahmood said focus on nutrition was needed at the community, systemic, and legislative levels.

Remarking on awareness campaigns on the community level, she said, “Interventions are not designed according to the latest theories and latest approaches towards designing behaviour change”.

She stressed a multisectoral approach to nutrition, adding that “no specific industry owns nutrition”.

5:00pm - Doctor stresses rigorous testing for pregnant women

Dr Nosheen Ashraf of the National Institutes of Health, speaking about maternal nutrition, said that during antenatal visits, mothers are asked to take supplements to address nutritional deficiencies; however, she noted a lack of consistent monitoring.

Dr Ashraf said there were not enough laboratories in far-flung areas, as she called for rigorous testing of pregnant mothers to track any nutritional deficiencies.

4:55pm - Gynaecologist stresses nutrition should not be limited to pregnancy or childbirth

Capital Hospital Associate Gynaecologist Dr Urooj Yasir Khan said the focus of nutrition should not be limited to pregnancy or childbirth.

“There is hardly any awareness about nutrition in our adolescent girl groups.” Following a substantial loss of iron during menstruation, micronutrient deficiencies in the body at the onset of pregnancy, especially if it’s a teenage pregnancy, can lead to growth-restricted babies, she said.

Commenting on treatment for obesity, she said, “we don’t say what’s important to eat”, adding that the focus seems to be on the number of calories consumed.

4:53pm - Founder Nutradevice calls for equitable access to nutritious food

Founder Nutradevice Dr Nosheen Taqvi held that creating awareness about nutritious food did not guarantee nutrition; rather, she maintained that it was worth examining “if the mother can access it, implement it, afford it and keeping in view the power of the woman in the household, can she give it to the children”.

Dr Taqvi also clarified misconceptions around nutrition. “It is not true that healthy food is always expensive [..] as you don’t always have to focus on animal-based food”.

She also noted that mothers in Pakistani households did not prioritise themselves. “Food is given to the family first. and then the mother eats whatever is left of it.”

She also noted that stigma around weight gain was leading to nutritional deficiencies in women as well.

Founder Nutradevice Dr Nosheen Taqvi speaks at the conference. — White Star

4:38pm - Researcher explains why ‘1,000-day’ period is critical to addressing malnutrition

Director of the International Research Force Dr Hana Mahmood explained why the first 1,000-day period of an infant’s life remained critical in addressing malnutrition.

“The most important thing we have to attend to right now is that these 1,000 days are those days in which growth is exponentially high and the requirement for micronutrients is massive,” Dr Mahmood said.

She added that during this time, the immune system and major organs were developing in such a way that any lack in nutritional input could lead to irreversible damage.

“During the first two years of life, 80pc of a child’s brain develops,” she said. Dr Mahmood also noted that Pakistan had one of the highest child-under-five mortality rates, a majority of which was contributed by malnutrition.

“250m deaths can be averted by focusing on prevention of stunting,” she said.

Director of the International Research Force Dr Hana Mahmood at the conference. — White Star

4:27pm - Session titled ‘First 1,000 days: Why women and girls matter for nutrition’ begins

Panelists at the session titled ‘The first 1,000 days: Why women and girls matter for nutrition’. — White Star

4:10pm - Agri consultant highlights need for demand pull in producing nutritionally rich food

Agriculture consultant Hasan Khurrum Hanif, talking about producing nutritionally dense food, said, “Pakistani farmers need a demand pull, rather than a supply push”.

“Farmers will produce what you pay us to produce and if there is a market where I can sell zinc-fortified wheat, where I can sell vegetables with lower pesticide residue, all of those require a different input package, which has a cost component,” he said.

Hanif added that processors needed to provide farmers an ecosystem.

3:55pm - Food safety infrastructure critical for nutrition, economy, says Tetra Pak executive

Corporate Affairs Director at Tetra Pak Noor Aftab stressed the significance of food safety, saying that “food systems need to be treated as critical infrastructure”.

He said that Pakistan is one of the largest milk-producing countries, but there were no safe milk or pasteurisation laws in the country, depriving the economy of $30bn export potential.

He added that in Pakistan, milk is taxed at one of the highest rates in the world. “If there is a resilient food systems infrastructure built within Pakistan, coupled with sustainable fiscal roadmaps… that will allow […] the infrastructure to act as a catalyst for nourishment and improvement.”

Corporate Affairs Director at Tetra Pak Noor Aftab speaks at the conference. — White Star/ Muhammad Asim

3:45pm - Nutrition investment reduced absenteeism rate in Bangladesh, says official

Project Manager at the Workforce Nutrition GM Reza Sumon, joining the conference through video conference from Bangladesh, discussed nutrition investments for the workforce.

He said that in Bangladesh’s government sector, the anaemia rate within the workforce was at 51.9pc. However, after interventions via funding for fortified rice, oils and iron and folic acid tablets, the anaemia rate dropped to 32pc, Sumon said, which helped convince the private sector to make similar investments in nutrition.

He said after the private sector invested $10m in nutrition in the past year, absenteeism in workplaces has reduced from 70pc to 40pc.

3:40pm - EBM executive shares details on a fortified biscuits initiative

Head of Corporate Communications & Sustainability at English Biscuit Manufacturers (EBM) Attiyah Inaam Khan shared details of an initiative launched by the company in which fortified biscuits were provided to mothers to address malnutrition.

“We tracked them for five years, and mothers who received biscuits showed great iron levels during pregnancy, and children born under the study showed stronger cognitive development,” she recalled.

“It is not about margins but more about whether there is evidence on the ground and whether the intervention can be scalable,” she added.

“Government can also play a very important lever here: tax credit for fortification in products and reduce the import duty on fortification,” she added.

Head of Corporate Communications & Sustainability at English Biscuit Manufacturers (EBM) Attiyah Inaam Khan speaks at the conference. — White Star/ Muhammad Asim

3:36pm - Session on mobilising private capital and partnerships begins

A panel discussion on mobilising private capital and partnerships has begun.

3:12pm - ADB views malnutrition as an economic issue, working with BISP, says official

Senior Project Officer at Asian Development Bank (ADB) Mansoor Ali Masood said the bank was looking at malnutrition through an economic lens rather than viewing it solely as a health issue.

“Hence, we are trying to mainstream it through social protection, education, agriculture and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services,” he said, adding that ADB was supporting the Benazir Nashonuma Programme and had allocated around half of a $960m fund to address stunting.

“ADB is supporting the expansion of BNP, helping BISP in expanding the awareness of mothers who are better informed and can take better decisions for their children and ensure dietary diversity.”

Senior Project Officer at Asian Development Bank (ADB) Mansoor Ali Masood speaks at the conference. — White Star/ Tanveer Shahzad

3:07pm - ‘Nutrition is part of human capital’

The Dean of Research at Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) Dr Shujaat Farooq, said that the economic cost of malnutrition was “too much”.

Citing statistics, he said 40pc of children in the country are facing stunting while 25 million children are out of school. He added that 75pc of children in schools were unable to learn proficiently due to malnutrition.

“Nutrition is part of human capital,” Farooq said.

3:00pm - No multi-sectoral nutrition programmes in the past decade: Planning ministry official

Chief of nutrition at the planning ministry, Dr Nazeer Ahmed, said in the past “one to two decades, there had been no major nutrition programme implemented in the provinces, except the Benazir Nashonuma Programme”.

“We have the policies in the four provinces, and nutrition strategies [..] But on the ground, we do not have any multi-sectoral programmes implemented,” he said.

Panelists at the Building Human Capital and Driving Economic Growth. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad
